title: Add SM90 BF16 grouped GEMM with gathered activation rows
body:
Routed BF16 forward paths currently materialize `a.index_select(0, rows)` before grouped GEMM. This adds `m_grouped_bf16_gemm_nt_contiguous_gathered(a, b, d, grouped_layout, a_row_indices)` on SM90, loading A through row indices directly into the existing WGMMA pipeline.

The first version supports K-major BF16, K divisible by 64, contiguous weights, 128-row expert alignment and an int64 CUDA row map. A may have a padded row stride. The A loader uses 16-byte `cp.async` copies with the existing shared-memory swizzle; B/output retain TMA. It does not add a fused SwiGLU epilogue or change default dispatch.

## Current revision

Commit `ca1291f7cd2dbe483af7d89f033b2a5a1e96ca1f`, based on main `1fc9c66975ee322d628b3288534ca0e9ce12a64d`, keeps the change in six existing files:

- Public API and registration in `csrc/apis/gemm.hpp`; configuration, TMA descriptors and launch in the existing SM90 implementation header.
- Integrated coverage in `tests/test_bf16.py`, rather than a separate gathered test file. It covers three generated configurations, six boundary cases and three rejected invalid inputs.
- The CUDA kernel's executable tokens are unchanged from the previous published revision. Host checks are reorganized while retaining the dimensionality, dtype, device, row-stride, alignment and empty-input constraints.

The native extension was forcibly rebuilt from this exact source and the focused gathered test passed on the original H200/SM90 stack: PyTorch `2.13.0+cu132`, CUDA runtime 13.2, seed 42, strict deterministic algorithms and uninitialized-memory filling disabled. All generated results are checked bitwise against the materialized path. Both paths use CUDA events in the integrated test, but those printed timings are not a new controlled performance result.

This is build/numerical/boundary validation, not a rerun of the historical full integration, sanitizer or performance studies below.

## Earlier 2.8.1 measurements

The following results were collected against the 2.8.1 release, #462 (`057ca5964aae0879ff2e0eb71ee05a3cb0ba3df7`), at PR commit `0ff99780929827f24f19d5e67a10c390c5f77592`.

On eight H200s, against activation gather + the existing GEMM with **prepacked gate/up weights** + the same fused output-compaction/SwiGLU kernel:

| D=3072, F=1280, 16 experts | Eager reduction, run 1 / repeat | CUDA Graph reduction |
|---|---:|---:|
| R=8192, M=16384, random routes | 6.42% / 6.31% | — |
| R=108031, M=170003, random routes | 6.07% / 5.83% | — |
| Source-ordered routes, nominal shape | 6.18% | 5.78% |
| Source-ordered routes, packet stride D+64 | 6.39% | 6.16% |

Eager numbers are median per-GPU ABBA/BAAB reductions; Graph is one GPU. The general eager sweep uses random routes with replacement, while Graph uses source-ordered unique routes; only the explicitly source-ordered rows compare matching routes across modes. Workers and process repeats reuse seed 42. An additional same-GPU, matching-row-map test at R=8192/M=16384 measures 6.25% eager / 6.01% Graph. The small R=1024, M=512, D=F=256 case measures 26.07% eager but **regresses 2.31% under Graph**, on matching routes. This is a fixed-route forward benchmark, not a full-model speedup.

All tested h/gate/up outputs match both existing-library baselines bitwise. API tests cover partial/empty M, empty experts, source/output stride, aligned offsets and misaligned pointer rejection. An additional 79-case regression covers existing BF16 GEMM/einsum layouts, output dtypes and accumulation modes using exact references and bytewise repeats. Independent FP32 reference checks pass; compute-sanitizer memcheck reports 0 errors. The full 13-phase 2.8.1 run passed, including live EP8 integration and receive-view lifetime checks; combined forward reductions are 16.99%–17.59% across two runs when both this change and [DeepEP #769](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepEP/pull/769) are enabled.

[2.8.1 reproducer, raw cycles, source hashes and limitations](https://gist.github.com/yuweih205/d3fd1e4c3fcb97364f36ec8fda996cfe#file-dg281-infra-report-md). These measurements retain their original test revision and predate the current reorganization; this update makes no additional performance claim. The earlier 2.8.0 measurements remain separately preserved in the same Gist.

Before this reorganization, the PR test scripts also passed a separate eight-H200 correctness rerun against the frozen production-equivalent runtimes. That DeepEP test revision checked an independent input/route oracle, raw deterministic order and two delayed consumer streams under both record-stream policies. [Exact test revisions and retained test-development failures](https://gist.github.com/yuweih205/d3fd1e4c3fcb97364f36ec8fda996cfe#file-review-gates-report-md).

title: Fix cross-expert output overwrites in SM90 masked GEMM
body:
SM90 masked GEMM flattens the output into a 2D TMA descriptor. When a store tile extends past an expert's capacity, it can overwrite valid rows of the next expert. This affects both BF16 and FP8: capacity 32 reproduces it, and capacity 96 also fails when experts are nearly full.

Keep the expert dimension in the output descriptor and reuse the existing 3D TMA store path. This preserves tile selection and the compute pipeline without adding buffers or synchronization. Boundary regressions are integrated into the existing BF16 and FP8 test suites.

This revisits the limitation discussed in #15 and the small-capacity failure reported in #268. #15 previously fixed small capacities by shrinking the store tile and rejected larger capacities not divisible by the tile size; it also suggested 3D TMA but deferred support for those cases. This change handles both small and non-tile-aligned capacities through the same output path.

On H200, the median paired latency changes across six rounds were between −0.17% and +0.16% for the larger tested shapes. The smallest shape was about 1.9% slower for BF16 and 1.5% slower for FP8, roughly 0.06–0.08 µs. The uniform 3D path avoids maintaining separate aligned and unaligned implementations, at that small measured cost.

<details>
<summary>Reproduction and validation</summary>

Requires an SM90 GPU and a source build of DeepGEMM. Save the following as `repro.py` outside the source checkout and run `python repro.py` against the installed baseline or patched package:

```python
import torch
import deep_gemm
from deep_gemm.testing import calc_diff

torch.manual_seed(29)
a = torch.randn((8, 32, 256), device='cuda', dtype=torch.bfloat16)
b = torch.randn((8, 256, 256), device='cuda', dtype=torch.bfloat16)
d = torch.empty((8, 32, 256), device='cuda', dtype=torch.bfloat16)
counts = torch.tensor([0, 1, 16, 31, 32, 1, 32, 32],
                      device='cuda', dtype=torch.int)
valid = torch.arange(32, device='cuda')[None, :] < counts[:, None]
reference = torch.bmm(a.double(), b.double().mT).bfloat16()

for _ in range(16):
    deep_gemm.m_grouped_bf16_gemm_nt_masked(a, b, d, counts, 32)
    diff = calc_diff(d[valid], reference[valid])
    assert diff < 1e-5, f'{diff=}'
```

Running this exact script against the baseline failed with `AssertionError: diff=tensor(0.1456, device='cuda:0', dtype=torch.float64)`; the patched wheel completed all 16 checks. Only valid rows are checked; padding values are unspecified.

Run the included regressions from the checkout after building and installing the patched package:

```bash
cd tests
python - <<'PY'
import torch
import test_bf16
import test_fp8_fp4

torch.manual_seed(17)
test_bf16.test_m_grouped_gemm_masked_boundaries()
test_fp8_fp4.test_m_grouped_gemm_masked_boundaries()
PY
```

Both passed with the final built wheel, including a fresh-JIT-cache run. Both fail at capacity 16 when run against the baseline package. A separate timed run with the JIT cache populated took 0.23 s for the BF16 test body and 0.09 s for FP8; this excludes process startup and imports, and does not estimate cold compilation time.

Supplemental validation, using separate local harnesses not included in this PR:

- Base: `057ca5964aae0879ff2e0eb71ee05a3cb0ba3df7`; candidate: `20865936a058d55c4c583cc2b0c2bcf3bc319a2f`. H200, PyTorch `2.13.0+cu130`, CUDA 13.0.
- 34 configurations per arm, covering BF16 and FP8, capacities from 1 to 257, single-expert and all-empty cases; 16 eager and 16 Graph calls each. Baseline and revert each had 24 failing configurations; the fix had none. Two configurations were all-empty and only checked completion. The revert reused the original package in a fresh process/cache.
- Independent FP64 matmul references, rounded to BF16; FP8 references used the actual quantized inputs and scales. No run-to-run changes were observed in the fixed panel.
- 37 adjacent-path checks passed, covering ordinary GEMM layouts, output dtypes and accumulation, batched GEMM, and K-grouped GEMM.
- Native `python setup.py bdist_wheel` passed with setuptools `75.8.0`.

Performance used six paired rounds with alternating arm order. Each measurement took the median of seven CUDA-event samples, each containing 1,000 Graph calls. Input generation and quantization were outside timing; FP8 API scale conversion was included. Positive values below mean slower; values are medians of paired latency changes.

| Groups | Capacity | N | K | Expected M | BF16 | FP8 |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 8 | 128 | 256 | 256 | 64 | +1.931% | +1.526% |
| 32 | 4096 | 1536 | 2048 | 20 | +0.070% | −0.143% |
| 6 | 4096 | 4096 | 4096 | 1024 | +0.155% | +0.023% |
| 32 | 4096 | 6144 | 7168 | 192 | −0.167% | −0.056% |

Clocks were not locked; sampled SM clocks ranged from 1305 to 1980 MHz. Small differences on the larger shapes should not be interpreted as established speedups. CPU launch latency, model-level impact, other GPU architectures, and the full build matrix were not evaluated.

</details>

On SM90 GPUs, tf32_hc_prenorm_gemm can produce incorrect and non-deterministic GEMM outputs when processing multiple K blocks.
Repeated calls with identical inputs can return different results.
Root cause
The kernel uses asynchronous WGMMA instructions with register-source A operands. Previously, the next iteration loaded its A fragment
before waiting for the preceding iteration's WGMMA to complete. This could overwrite A registers while they were still being read by
the in-flight WGMMA.
Fix
Proposed fix:
#448
The fix moves
warpgroup_wait<0>()
immediately after
warpgroup_commit_batch()
, ensuring that each iteration's WGMMA completes
before its A registers are reused.
The PR also adds a regression test covering split-K, PDL enabled/disabled, and default/side streams. It checks outputs against FP32
references and verifies repeatability across identical launches.
Validation
With the fix applied, both the existing hyperconnection tests and all 24 configurations of the new regression test passed on an SM90
GPU.

fix will introduce some performance regression which suppose to be mitigated in upcoming PRs。

title: [Feat]Add native FP8 Tensor Core GEMM support for SM89 (Ada Lovelace)
body:
**Title**  
Add native FP8 Tensor Core GEMM support for SM89 (Ada Lovelace)

**Body**

## Summary

This change adds a native FP8 Tensor Core GEMM for SM89 (Ada Lovelace). SM89 is the first architecture below Hopper that has FP8 Tensor Cores.

Previously, SM80 and SM89 used the same path. The path required SM90 or higher for FP8. This was correct for SM80 because Ampere has no FP8 Tensor Cores. It was wrong for SM89. SM89 implements the instruction `mma.sync.aligned.m16n8k32.row.col.f32.e4m3.e4m3.f32` (`QMMA.16832.F32.E4M3.E4M3`). The change separates the two architectures and gives SM89 a real kernel.

## Why

- SM89 has FP8 Tensor Cores. It does not have the SM90 features (no TMA, no `mbarrier.try_wait.parity`, no WGMMA, no clusters). It could not reuse the SM90 or SM100 kernels. It fell back to BF16 through cuBLASLt.
- FP8 users on Ada had to dequantize and run BF16. They lost about 2× of Tensor Core throughput.
- The shared SM80/SM89 path also gave wrong error messages. An SM89 user saw a message that did not apply to their GPU.

## Design

SM89 has no TMA and no asynchronous barriers. The kernel uses the pre-Hopper primitives.

- It uses `mma.sync` (wrapped in `deep_gemm/mma/sm89.cuh`, with A/B/C fragment layouts documented) and `ldmatrix.x4` for operand staging.
- It uses a multi-stage `cp.async` pipeline with a 128-byte XOR swizzle.
- It uses a persistent block scheduler (one CTA per SM). Tiles walk in a loop.
- It uses direct global stores because SM89 has no TMA store. It has an alignment-safe scalar tail. An MMA lane owns a pair of adjacent columns. For odd N the element offset of a row can be odd. A 2-element vector store is then illegal. This caused the original misaligned address failure.
- Block K is fixed at 128 because of the per-128-channel scaling granularity. Pipeline depth and tile shapes come from a new cost model in `csrc/jit_kernels/heuristics/sm89.hpp`. The warp split uses one shared function `get_mma_sync_warps_n()`. Host heuristics and device code both call it so they cannot disagree.

Both SM90 SF recipes are supported:  
`(1, 1, 128)` (per-token A and B scales) and  
`(1, 128, 128)` (per-token A, one B scale per 128-column N block).  
The second recipe is the default when FP32 scales are used. SM89 uses the same FP32 SF layouts as SM90. The function `transform_sf_into_required_layout` was extended. It was not duplicated.

## Scope

Supported features:  
dense FP8 GEMM, K-major (NT) operands only, FP32 and BF16 outputs, `D = C + A @ B`, ragged M/N, `k % 16 == 0`, both aliases (`fp8_fp4_gemm_nt`, `fp8_gemm_nt`, `fp4_gemm_nt`), and shape specialization.

Still rejected (with an explicit message that names the requirement):  
grouped and K-grouped FP8, MN-major FP8 operands, FP4, custom epilogues, `alpha` scaling, PDL, and MQA/attention.  
BF16 keeps its cuBLASLt fallback.

## Incidental fixes

- `set_pdl()` now panics below SM90. It no longer sets a flag that `griddepcontrol` cannot honour.  
  `cudaGridDependencySynchronize()` is wrapped in a no-op below `__CUDA_ARCH__ >= 900` so the SF-layout kernels compile for SM89.
- `call_cublaslt_api` used `CUBLAS_COMPUTE_32F_FAST_TF32` for non-FP32 operands. That mode only down-casts FP32 inputs to TF32. BF16/FP8 operands ran at TF32 precision by mistake. Now only FP32 inputs use that mode.
- A new `DG_PANIC` macro throws always and carries a message.

## Bug found during validation

The persistent loop primed its `cp.async` pipeline only in the prologue before the tile loop. It relied on a cross-tile tail load to prime the next tile. A tile’s tail can only reach the stages that are already free of the current tile — prologue stages `p ∈ [0, kNumStages-2-num_k_blocks]`. The next tile’s K loop consumes `p = 0..num_k_blocks-1`. When `num_k_blocks < kNumStages-1` (example: `k=512`, 4 blocks, 8 stages) the high stages were never reloaded. The next tile read the previous tile’s shared memory. Symptom: non-deterministic `nan` and values near 1e30. The problem appeared only for small M spread over many N tiles.

The fix extracts the prologue into `prime_pipeline()` and re-primes unconditionally after the epilogue. The re-prime is guarded by `cp_async_wait<0>()` and a `__syncthreads()`. `cp.async` completion is per-thread, so both are required before the stages can be reused. The change removes a prologue/epilogue overlap that was never correct. Measured cost is about 0–3.5 % (4096³: 2518 µs vs 2507 µs, within noise; 4096×4096×512: 420 µs vs 405 µs).

`tests/test_sm89.py` added the shapes `(1, 4096, 512)`, `(64, 4096, 512)` and `(128, 4096, 128)`. Reverting the fix makes these tests fail (34 failures). They are real regression tests.

## Testing

Hardware: RTX 4060 Laptop (SM89, 24 SMs, 7.6 GiB), CUDA 13.0, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130.

- `tests/test_sm89.py` — 17 tests, OK from a cold JIT cache (~130 s).  
  Covers both recipes × both output dtypes × accumulate × 12 shapes, explicit `recipe=(1,128,128)`, `recipe_a`/`recipe_b` pairs, entry-point aliases, compiled-dim specialization, bitwise determinism across repeats, accumulation-versus-zero-C equivalence, BF16 GEMM and all its layouts, cuBLASLt FP8/BF16, SF layout kernels, and one rejection case per unsupported feature.
- `tests/test_layout.py` — OK.
- Upstream `tests/test_fp8_fp4.py::test_gemm` — OK.  
  The upstream shape grid reaches m=129280 / n=7168 and OOMs on a 7.6 GiB card. Shapes were clamped to m≤4096, n≤4096, k≤1280 by monkey-patching `enumerate_normal` in a throw-away driver. The test body, recipes and assertions were not changed.
- Upstream `tests/test_bf16.py::test_gemm` — correctness OK, same clamping.  
  The perf-print block was stubbed because `bench_kineto` matches on the kernel name `bf16_gemm`, which does not exist on SM89 (BF16 goes through the cuBLASLt fallback). All `diff < 1e-5` assertions ran without change.
- Other suites fail only for environmental reasons and are unchanged by this PR:  
  `test_einsum` raises the intended “Unsupported architecture”,  
  `test_lazy_init` and `test_locality_domain` need multiple GPUs,  
  `test_bf16` / `test_legacy` OOM at upstream shapes.

Throughput, single GPU, FP8 in / BF16 out:

| m    | n    | k    | time      | TFLOPS |
|------|------|------|-----------|--------|
| 1    | 4096 | 4096 | 33.6 µs   | 1.0    |
| 128  | 4096 | 4096 | 168.4 µs  | 25.5   |
| 4096 | 4096 | 4096 | 2517.8 µs | 54.6   |
| 4096 | 4096 | 512  | 419.7 µs  | 40.9   |

Inspired by the SM90 FP8×FP8 MegaMoE implementation introduced in
deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM#383
and the SM90 FP8×NVFP4 work in
AichenF/DeepGEMM@megamoe_nvfp4_dev_m
, this PR adds an optimized FP8×MXFP4 MegaMoE backend for SM90 GPUs. Keeping routed-expert weights in MXFP4 enables native reuse of Hugging Face MXFP4 MoE checkpoints, while substantially reducing GPU memory pressure by avoiding a persistent FP8 weight expansion.
Summary
Unified SM90 persistent execution.
Unlike
[SM90] Add FP8 MegaMoE support
#383
, this implementation fuses dispatch, routed/shared L1 and L2, and combine into one persistent kernel. It adapts the SM100 ring-buffer and wave-interleaved scheduler to a cluster-free Hopper design using register-resident WGMMA, one CTA per task, and two resident CTAs per SM.
Humming-inspired MXFP4×FP8 compute path.
Routed weights remain packed MXFP4 in global memory. Model-load preprocessing rebases the K32 UE8M0 exponents into bounded relative scales plus one FP32 secondary scale per expert, following the fused MXFP4×FP8 approach used by Humming. During execution, packed E2M1 tiles are loaded into compact shared-memory staging, decoded and expanded on the fly into E4M3 FP8 tiles, and then consumed by Hopper WGMMA. This avoids materializing a persistent FP8 copy of the routed weights.

2c71fb6
DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash stores each KV token as 528B: 512B of FP8 E4M3 covering
the full 512-wide K (rope lanes quantized, no BF16 rope segment) plus a 16B
footer of 16 UE8M0 scales over 32-wide groups (the
deepseek-ai/FlashMLA#221
layout, SM100-only there). Add ModelType::DSV4_1 on top of the ScaleSpec
groundwork: GLM53_NOPE-style geometry (D_ROPE=0) composed with a 32-wide
UE8M0 footer.

Kernel side the format is simpler than DSV4 (one 512B bulk per row, a single
unified block-scaled FP8 QK pass, no rope MMA paths). The two new mechanics:

- the 16B footer row generalizes the scale gather from one uint64_t to a
  width-selected load (uint4) in both the prefill IO helper and the decode
  kernel's staged gather;
- the 32-wide groups constrain the XV W-fold (one scale group per W buffer),
  so an 8-warp XV split would floor NT_PER_WARP_XV to 0: decode runs a
  4-math-warp tile at BI=64 (the DOTS3_SWA halving precedent) and prefill is
  SG-only on the BI=32 producer/consumer tile. The ComputeTraits/SmemLayout
  aliases now take the XV warp count so the NT_PER_WARP_XV assert evaluates at
  the warp count the XV MMA actually runs at.

Selection is explicit everywhere (d_qk=512 collides with DSV4, the 528B
payload with GLM53_NOPE): the functional API gains kv_scale_format=
"ue8m0_g32", the TRTLLM-compat entry kv_cache_format="fp8_dsv41", and the
decode-dsv4 FFI takes an explicit model_type (-1 keeps the legacy width
inference, matching the paged-entry kAuto convention). Dual-cache decode is
supported like DSV4; dual-cache prefill (MG_DUAL) is intentionally not
instantiated. Calibration keys a new dsv4_1 family at topk 512.

Tests: decode matrix (dedicated/runtime-H heads, partial-tail topk, sinks),
SG prefill, dual-cache through the TRTLLM entry, poisoned-slot-0 NaN safety
on both gather paths, dispatch/plan/envelope coverage. 666 passed on RTX PRO
6000 (SM120).

Upstream restructured csrc/ into csrc/kernels/<arch>/<op>/, turned the
csrc/api/*.h header-only interfaces into .cpp translation units with their
own pybind registration, replaced the per-kernel format constants with a
KVCacheFormat<ModelType> descriptor, and renamed MODEL1 to DeepSeek-V4.
The fork's changes were carried onto that structure:

* libtorch build: dropped the csrc/flashmla_utils.h shim -- upstream's
  includes are now "kernels/utils.h", which no longer collides with
  sgl-kernel's bare utils.h. csrc/api/common.h keeps Python-free headers
  under FLASH_MLA_LIBTORCH_ONLY, and the register_* functions that upstream
  moved into csrc/api/*.cpp are guarded by the same macro, so a libtorch-only
  build still compiles the interface TUs without Python.
  csrc/python_api.cpp declares the three interfaces extern instead of
  including the (now non-header) api files.

* B200 V3.2 accuracy: upstream still narrows V3.2's inline fp32 KV scales to
  1-byte ue8m0 in the index warp, which drops the mantissa. The bf16-scale
  fix is ported into the generic KVBlockDequantizer through one new format
  constant, KVCacheFormat::SCALE_SMEM_BYTES (2 for the V3.2 formats, 1
  otherwise). NUM_INDEX_BUFS stays 2 for V3.2, keeping the scale smem
  footprint identical to upstream.

* V32_NO_ROPE: expressed as a KVCacheFormat (d_qk 512, no RoPE, V3.2's
  inline fp32 scales) instead of ad-hoc constants, so the sm100 head64 kernel
  reuses the D_BF16 == 0 path upstream added for V4.1. NOTE V3.2-no-RoPE and
  V4.1 are both 528 B per token with d_qk 512, so the shape alone can no
  longer identify the format: sparse_decode_fwd / flash_mla_with_kvcache take
  a new optional kv_format argument, and auto-detection reads 528 B as
  V3.2-no-RoPE so that callers written before V4.1 keep working.

* sm90 dense decode HEAD_DIM_K=512 and the decode-meta low-smem fallback
  carried over with no semantic change.

Deleted csrc/kernels/sm90/decode/sparse/components/config.h: nothing includes
it any more and its hardcoded V3.2 constants are misleading.

body:
Conversation
Livinfly
commented
Aug 30, 2026
Copy link
Copy Markdown
Summary
This PR adds optional per-request
topk_length
support to the SM90
DeepSeek-V3.2 FP8 sparse decode kernel (
d_qk=576
). SM90 V3.2 can now use
dynamic top-k instead of always processing the full allocated top-k capacity.
When
topk_length
is provided, the kernel:
loads the valid length for each batch row;
schedules only
max(ceil_div(topk_length, TOPK_BLOCK_SIZE), 1)
blocks;
masks a partial tail before its indices can be used for KV addressing; and
includes the absolute top-k position in the softmax validity predicate.
When
topk_length == nullptr
, the existing fixed top-k behavior is preserved.
There is no public API change, and MODEL1 and SM100 behavior are unchanged.
Why
template<bool DYNAMIC_TOPK, ...>
I also tested a single-device-kernel implementation that checks
params.topk_length != nullptr
at runtime. The condition is grid-uniform, but
the compiler cannot remove the length load, tail predicates, extra control
flow, or their value lifetimes from the fixed path.
template<bool DYNAMIC_TOPK>
moves the choice to host launch dispatch:
false
: the dynamic-length logic is compiled out, preserving the fixed path;
true
: per-row block counts and partial-tail safety checks are enabled.
The comparison implementation is available at
7b7c831
on
test/sm90-v32-dynamic-topk-runtime-device
. It regresses the representative
B64-B128 fixed cases by 8.4%-9.4%, while the specialized implementation stays
within 0.5% of the baseline. Both builds report 168 registers, 12 barriers,
and no spills, so the generated hot-path instructions—not an occupancy
change—explain the observed difference.

title: Support for DeepSeek-V4-Flash and DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision-Exp
body:
### Summary

`deepseek-recipe` currently supports two model versions (`ModelVersion::DeepseekV4Pro` and `ModelVersion::DeepseekV41Flash` in `deepseek-recipe/src/request/options.rs`). **DeepSeek-V4-Flash** and **DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision-Exp** are not supported, and neither existing encoding fits them:

| | V4-Flash-Vision-Exp (official `encoding/encoding_dsv4.py`) | `DeepseekV4Encoding` (`dsv4.rs`) | `DeepseekV41Encoding` (`dsv41.rs`) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Tool-call tags | `tool_calls` / `invoke` / `parameter` | same | ` calls` / ` invoke` / ` parameter` (leading space) |
| `<｜System｜>` token | no | no | yes |
| Reasoning effort | text preamble, default `low` (no preamble) | text preamble, default "Absolute maximum…" | numeric |
| Images | `<｜deepseek_image｜>` | replaced with `[Unsupported Image]` | supported (`<｜image｜>`) |
| Historical tool calls | kept in call order | sorted by id (`normalize_messages`) | kept in order |

So with the V4 encoding the visual input is lost, and with the V4.1 encoding the model receives markup it was not trained on.

### Questions

1. Is support for V4-Flash / V4-Flash-Vision-Exp planned?
2. If not, would you accept a PR adding a `DeepseekV4Flash` (and Vision-Exp) model version? The idea is to reuse the V4 encoding, add image support with the Vision-Exp image token and preprocessing, use the reference default effort, and keep the historical call order. It would be validated byte for byte against the official `encoding_dsv4.py` shipped with the model.

Happy to contribute it if that direction works for you. Thanks for open-sourcing the recipe.

## Summary

Fix the encoding/decoding demo's Responses output for declared custom tools.

The demo consumed the typed request before preserving `custom_tool_names()`. Its Responses generator therefore treated `apply_patch` as a function call and left its input inside JSON `arguments`, despite the request declaring a custom tool.

Fixes #21

title: perf(cudnn): reuse bounded ragged graphs for short prefill
body:
<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

Allow qualified BF16 ragged D128 and MLA D192/V128 prefill with 2–63 query tokens to reuse the existing bounded Q<=128 graph class. Previously these requests used the broad `(4096, 128, 65536)` declaration, hiding their small launch geometry from cuDNN Frontend's split-KV selection.

The change extends the existing admission condition; it adds no bucket class, public knob, run-time staging, or engine-specific execution path. Q=1 retains the separate decode class. Existing FE/native capability checks preserve the old behavior on released FE 1.30 and earlier.

**Depends on #6168; merge that first.** The incremental change above that PR is one production condition plus its comment, and extensions to the existing lifecycle tests.

B200 (148 SMs, 1000 W), BF16, cuDNN 9.27, FE 1.31 development source, DSL 4.8, Torch 2.12/CUDA 13.2. Actual public `backend="auto"`, normal cache settings, no forced engine/split. Four independent layer buffers; warm CUDA-event graph replay medians in microseconds, both benchmark orders, HN natural-log LSE:

| Shape | Before (#6168) | This change | FA4 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| D128, B1, H4/1, Q8, KV32768 | 368.70 | 24.51 | 24.82 |
| D128, B1, H4/1, Q32, KV32768 | 368.88 | 25.49 | 24.57 |
| MLA D192/V128, B1, H4/4, Q8, KV8192 | 130.33 | 16.96 | 20.35 |
| MLA D192/V128, B1, H4/4, Q63, KV32768 | 523.68 | 31.22 | 34.53 |
| D128, B3, H16/4, Q=[31,7,2], KV=[8192,4097,2048] | 106.92 | 41.26 | 21.48 |

The full 12-shape comparison covers Q2/7/8/32/63, Q64/128 controls, mixed lengths, a batch outside the bounded range and short-KV controls, with and without LSE. All 144 runs passed O/LSE and changed-input replay checks. Cold-cache measurements confirm the short-Q gains. Mixed batches and the unchanged broad fallbacks still have gaps relative to FA4; this is not a general serving-throughput claim.

The comparison includes FE #1452, but the improvement does **not** depend on it: a separate source run without #1452 gave 24.51/25.50/16.84/31.24 us for the first four rows. The existing bounded Q128 declarations already expose supported split plans.

title: perf(gemm): let the untuned SM107 mm_mxfp8 default pick B-reuse tactics
body:
## 📌 Description

On SM107 the untuned `mm_mxfp8(backend="cute-dsl")` tactic (`_compute_sm107_mxfp8_tactic_for_m`) never picks B-reuse tactics, where the tile M is twice the MMA instruction M and each CTA issues two MMAs that share one B tile (e.g. a 512x256 tile with 256-row instructions), because `_score_block_scaled_tactic` could not model them. This is the tactic `mm_mxfp8` uses whenever it runs without autotuning.

Changes, all in `flashinfer/gemm/kernels/utils.py`:

- `_score_block_scaled_tactic` takes an optional `mma_inst_shape_m`. The CTA group is 2 iff the instruction M is 256, and each CTA computes `tile_m / cta_group` rows. Callers that don't pass it get the same scores as before; that includes every mm_fp4 path, whose tiles are 128 or 256 rows.
- The SM107 mm_mxfp8 default scores B-reuse tactics with a 1.25 weight and skips them at K <= 2048.
- One pick serves the whole M bucket (rep_m/2, rep_m], and 512-row tiles change the wave count more within a bucket than other tiles do. So a B-reuse pick must also beat the best non-B-reuse tactic at 5/8, 3/4 and 7/8 of rep_m.

### Results on Rubin

Untuned `mm_mxfp8`, timed with CUPTI over CUDA graphs, cold L2, memory clock locked. 14 linear shapes (13 from MiniMax-M3 at TP2/TP4, one from Qwen) at 43 M values from 4 to 16384, including non-multiples of 512. Median of 5 rounds per point on each of two nodes; the ratio is this PR's time over main's, geomean over the two nodes (below 1 is faster).

| 513–4096 | 294 | 64 | 0.978 | 0.905 | 1.050 |

title: Reuse bounded cuDNN ragged prefill graphs for D128 and SM107
body:
## Description

Ready for review. The companion default-selection fixes in NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend#1421 are merged, and this FI head has now been validated with both current FE develop and the published FE 1.30.0 wheel on B200.

Extend #6134's bounded ragged prefill declarations to BF16 SM100/SM107 D128/V128 with 4–64 query heads and integral GQA1/2/4/8. Small prefixes reuse power-of-two B/Q/KV capacity classes and a packed-Q bound instead of the broad B=4096 / long-sequence=65536 declaration. FE can then size split workspace and select a useful launch. The existing prepared run path is reused; there is no per-run preparation or engine-specific caller API. Equal-head D192/V128 MLA also gains SM107 bounded admission.

Admission requires FE 1.31+ and the matching native packed-split capability. FE 1.30 and mixed installations retain the existing broad graph. The dependency floor remains `nvidia-cudnn-frontend>=1.30.0`; users obtain the new optimization with a qualifying newer FE installation. FE 1.31 is not released yet, so current release-only installations do not activate these new classes.

## B200: actual default selection

FI baseline `2582f2ae0744` versus this PR `b654ddc1957c`, both with unchanged FE develop `75bc3664aab4`, cuDNN 9.27.0.42 and CuTeDSL 4.8. B200, 148 SMs, 1000 W; Torch 2.12 nv26.04 / CUDA 13.2. Public wrapper `backend="auto"` resolved to cuDNN in every case. FE opt-in was unset; no engine, split count or heuristic was forced.

BF16 causal ragged prefill, D128, packed HN LSE, four independent layer buffers; CUDA-event replay includes all captured kernels. Values are microseconds per layer, medians of two reverse-order rounds. O/LSE and changed-input replay were checked against FP64.

| B; Hq/Hkv; Q; KV | Baseline | This PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| 1; 16/4; 128; 8192 | 106.76 | 22.44 |
| 1; 16/4; 128; 32768 | 370.99 | 44.57 |
| 3; 16/4; 128; 8192 | 108.88 | 44.69 |
| 4; 16/4; 128; 8192 | 108.93 | 46.81 |
| 1; 8/1; 65; 16383 | 193.20 | 22.30 |
| 3; 16/4; 257; 8193 | 109.15 | 109.39 |

All 44 comparisons across 11 shapes passed, including mixed/empty requests, bucket boundaries, full prefill, larger-batch controls and unchanged MLA. B3/Q257 and mixed B4 still select backend and retain performance opportunities; bounded declarations do not guarantee the ideal candidate for every workload. These are layer measurements, not serving E2E.

Host costs were measured separately with the same LSE-enabled calls. For the first row, plan was 45.40 → 46.60 us and enqueue was 47.90 → 41.51 us per layer. D128 plan cost rose about 1–1.6 us across this grid; a mixed control's enqueue rose about 2.7 us. Do not infer universal host improvement from GPU replay gains. Additional capacity classes still need prewarming before capture and can require more cold compilation and split workspace.

These stock-FE measurements supersede the earlier provisional two-guard heuristic experiment in the PR description. NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend#1421 supplied the upstream selection fix; this FI patch contains no heuristic override.

- SM107: **24 bounded public-wrapper tests passed**, covering O/LSE, replan, current pointers/strides, prewarming, changed live lengths, retained captures and older-FE fallback. Performance details remain internal.
- Earlier broader B200 suites: 236 passed / 1 two-device skip; host contracts: 50 passed. These are prior qualification, not a claim that every suite was rerun on the newest head.
- Changed-file pre-commit passed. Existing tests and the wrapper benchmark were extended; no new test file or heuristic winner/timing golden was added.

```bash
pytest -q tests/attention/test_cudnn_ragged_shape_override.py
```

```bash
python benchmarks/bench_cudnn_wrapper_host.py \
```

title: feat(mla): read DeepSeek-V4.1 inline-scale KV records natively on SM120
body:
## 📌 Description

FlashMLA's DeepSeek-V4.1 ABI (as of its 2026.09.30 release) stores each token as one self-contained record: each token's data is followed by its own scales. vLLM adopted it in vllm-project/vllm#61371. The SM120 sparse-MLA DSv4.1 path reads only footer-scale pages, in which a page holds all its tokens' data and then all their scales.

The two layouts have the same record size (528 B), so a cache in the other layout passes every shape check and decodes into silently wrong output. This PR adds the inline-scale records as new, explicit formats. The existing names keep their footer meaning.

| | main (SWA) cache | FP4 compressed cache |
|---|---|---|
| Footer (`fp8_dsv41`, `ue8m0_g32`) | per page: P × 512 B E4M3, then P × 16 B UE8M0 | per page: P × 256 B E2M1, then P × 32 B E4M3 |
| Inline (new) | per token: 512 B E4M3 + 16 B UE8M0 (group 32) = 528 B | per token: 256 B E2M1 + 32 B E4M3 (group 16) = 288 B |

As in FlashMLA, sparse indices address inline records as rows of the whole cache, and a page stride must be a whole number of rows.

### API

- **SM120 wrapper / functional API:** `kv_scale_format="ue8m0_g32_inline"` selects the inline records; `"ue8m0_g32"` keeps the footer meaning.
- **`trtllm_batch_decode_with_kv_cache_mla`:** adds `kv_cache_format="fp8_dsv41_inline"` and `"fp8_dsv41_inline_fp4_ca"` (`backend="sparse"`). `backend="cake"` rejects them with a `ValueError`.
- **Writers:** the DSv4.1 FP8/FP4 pack and append writers take `inline_scale=True`. They then write records at the cache's row pitch, and append slots address rows.

The names follow the existing conventions: inline-scale vs footer-scale vocabulary, and the record layout is part of the format identity rather than a separate argument.

### Implementation

- **New model type:** a `DSV4_1_INLINE` model on the DSV4_1 routes. Its record is the smem row, which DSV4_1 already pads to 528 B.
- **One copy per candidate:** the gathers issue one bulk copy per candidate and drop the synchronous footer-scale load. The QK, value-dequant and W-fold stages read the scales at +512 in smem.
- **Mixed-cache schedules:** they copy each 288 B FP4 record whole and convert it straight into the inline KV row.
- **Full-BF16 kernels:** these load per thread, and address inline records through an inline layout that has the footer layouts' offset interface.
- **Row strides:** rows of both caches are addressed flat with validated runtime row strides (16 B multiples of at least the record size), as for GLM53_NOPE. The attention metadata gains the extra cache's row stride, appended at the end so positional initializers keep working.
- **Prep refactor:** `qk_k_scale_selector` and `kv_scale_fp32` are now keyed on `SCALE_FORMAT` instead of `SCALE_IN_KV_SMEM`, so an inline model may store UE8M0 bytes. Every existing model keeps its reads.
- **Calibration:** gains a `dsv4_1_inline` family, keyed on the cache's own page size. No device profiles are committed.
- **Bit-exact:** the math order is unchanged, so inline outputs and LSE equal the footer form's bit for bit.

### Performance

Measured on an RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition with CUPTI kernel time, cold L2, median µs, on the same rows and indices. Each layout uses its own calibrated profiles. "512" is a single cache with top-k 512; "128 + fp4" is main top-k 128 plus 512 FP4 compressed candidates. Footer pages hold 64 tokens.

Default precision:

| cache | heads | tokens | footer | inline | inline / footer |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 512 | 8 | 1 | 13.3 | 11.7 | 0.88 |
| 512 | 64 | 1 | 14.1 | 12.7 | 0.90 |
| 512 | 64 | 16 | 34.3 | 30.4 | 0.89 |
| 512 | 64 | 64 | 85.4 | 78.3 | 0.92 |
| 512 (prefill) | 64 | 1024 | 1058.9 | 961.5 | 0.91 |
| 128 + fp4 | 8 | 1 | 14.8 | 12.4 | 0.84 |
| 128 + fp4 | 64 | 16 | 40.4 | 34.3 | 0.85 |
| 128 + fp4 | 16 | 64 | 49.0 | 39.4 | 0.80 |
| 128 + fp4 | 64 | 64 | 111.6 | 101.8 | 0.91 |
| 128 + fp4 (prefill) | 64 | 1024 | 1381.5 | 1160.2 | 0.84 |

Full-BF16 compute precision:

| cache | heads | tokens | footer | inline | inline / footer |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 512 | 64 | 64 | 117.1 | 112.6 | 0.96 |
| 512 (prefill) | 64 | 1024 | 1259.2 | 1212.6 | 0.96 |
| 128 + fp4 | 32 | 64 | 88.5 | 83.1 | 0.94 |
| 128 + fp4 (prefill) | 64 | 1024 | 1644.2 | 1520.6 | 0.92 |

- **Default precision:** inline is 4–20% faster than footer pages across all measured shapes.
- **Full BF16:** inline is up to 8% faster. Small FP4 decode is the exception, within about 1% (one shape 1.2% slower). The BF16 kernels are compute-bound with per-thread loads.
- **Row-stride cost:** making the extra cache's row stride a runtime value costs nothing measurable (after/before 0.997–1.001; BF16 1.000).
- **Reproducing:** `benchmarks/bench_sparse_mla_sm120.py` has a DSv4.1 footer-vs-inline section.

## 🔍 Related Issues

- vllm-project/vllm#61371: vLLM's interleaved V4.1 KV records (FlashMLA 2026.09.30).
- vllm-project/vllm#59846: SM120 DSv4.1 decode through FlashInfer's V4.1 sparse MLA; it switches to these formats. End to end, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash chat GSM8K on SM120 TP4 scores 0.946 (`fp8_dsv41_inline`) and 0.948 (`fp8_dsv41_inline_fp4_ca`), against 0.945 / 0.947 with the footer formats before vLLM's layout change.
- #5197 introduced the SM120 DSv4.1 support this extends.

## 🚀 Pull Request Checklist

### ✅ Pre-commit Checks

- [x] I have installed `pre-commit` by running `pip install pre-commit` (or used your preferred method).
- [x] I have installed the hooks with `pre-commit install`.
- [x] I have run the hooks manually with `pre-commit run --all-files` and fixed any reported issues.

## 🧪 Tests

- [x] Tests have been added or updated as needed.
- [x] All tests are passing (`unittest`, etc.).

**New file:** `tests/attention/test_sparse_mla_sm120_dsv41_inline.py`, 117 tests, covering:
- cache-geometry checks;
- byte-level writer tests (packed blocks, padded row pitches, pitched one-row pages);
- a cross-check of the FP8 append writer against vLLM's V4.1 MXFP8 cache writer in packed blocks;
- inline-vs-footer decode and prefill equality (exact output and LSE) across compute precisions including full BF16, with no / FP8 / FP4 extra cache, packed-block strides, and padded main and extra row pitches;
- native model selection, CUDA graph capture, and Cake rejection.

**Existing suites:** `test_sparse_mla_sm120.py` (587), cache contracts (53), binding guards (9), policy (52), execution (59), LSE (54), calibration (98) and Cake DSv4.1 mixed (117 passed, 1 skipped) all pass on SM120.

**Known pre-existing failure:** in the precision suite, `test_nvfp4_precision_envelope_and_warmup` fails identically on the base commit without this change.

## Reviewer Notes

- **Footer deprecation:** FlashInfer's sparse-MLA cache formats otherwise mirror FlashMLA's ABI, and FlashMLA's V4.1 ABI is now inline-scale. I kept `fp8_dsv41` / `ue8m0_g32` as the footer form, because they shipped in 0.7.1/0.7.2 and the layouts can't be told apart at run time. Should the footer form be deprecated in favor of the inline one?
- **Effect beyond DSv4.1:** the binding's one-row-page rule applies to every inline-scale format, including GLM53_NOPE. A GLM53_NOPE cache built from one-row pages with a padded pitch is now read at that pitch, and its prefill accepts it where it used to reject it. The existing GLM tests pass. I can split this into its own commit if preferred.
- **Writer FFI change:** the four DSv4.1 writer FFI entry points gain an `inline_scale` argument. Existing direct callers in the tests pass `False`.
- **Not covered here:** the experimental SM100 Frost DSv4.1 decode (`flashinfer/deepseek_v41.py`) also stores footer-scale pages. Cake's SM120 mixed-cache family stays footer-only by design.

This PR was written with AI assistance (Claude); I reviewed every line.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

  - Added support for inline-scale caches with optional extra FP4 caches, padded row pitches, and explicit FP8/BF16 precision.
  - Expanded calibration and benchmarking coverage for inline and footer scale placement.
- **Bug Fixes**
  - Improved cache layout and stride validation for main and extra caches across supported execution paths.

title: [Attention] Reuse bounded cuDNN prefill plans and gate Blackwell paged auto
body:
<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

Consolidate the pending cuDNN prefill integration into one review: bounded ragged graph reuse, caller-workspace-aware planning, cheaper paged metadata staging, and a release-gated Blackwell paged-auto path. Serving steps can change lengths and pointers while retaining prepared plans and valid older CUDA Graph captures.

This is the single review entry replacing #6168, #6209, #6213, #6216, and #6223. Their complete commit histories are retained; they are no longer separate merge prerequisites. The branch incorporates main at `3c1d1c2fff9c26f355c3d18b3b3b15c79003828a`, including its single-token GQA LSE guard.

Review the two production files in three parts:

1. **Bounded ragged plans and lifetime capacity.** Extend the existing MLA cache to SM100/SM107 D128 FP16/BF16 and short Q2–63 prefixes; Q=1 remains separate. A CUDA Graph wrapper's enforced initialization capacity participates in immutable graph keys. Replanning fewer live tokens never shrinks that capacity. Ordinary dynamic wrappers retain the B/Q envelope.
2. **Workspace and plan-time staging.** Select a separately cached FE plan within the caller's workspace budget; do not mutate a graph held by an older capture. Reuse page-table capacity and stage page mappings/lengths in `plan()`.
3. **Gated paged auto.** On SM100, admit causal BF16 HND D128/V128, page16, B1–4, Hq8–64, GQA1/2/4/8/16, Q64–1024, KV2K–32K, KV >= 4Q, and `total_query_tokens * Hq * max_KV >= 8 * 1024 * 1024`. This upper bound remains a cheap initial rejection. When KV lengths are already on CPU, additionally require `Hq * sum(Q_i * KV_i) >= 8 * 1024 * 1024`, pairing each query with its own KV length. With GPU-only lengths and explicit maxima, preserve the previous bound-based policy to avoid a fallback-induced host readback. Stable FE1.32+, its matching native paged capability, a compatible FROST runtime and cuDNN9.27+ are required. Unsupported features and older runtimes retain their existing auto route. Full prefill and large batches are outside this admission. Preserve and refresh captured metadata across cuDNN→FA2→cuDNN transitions.

Public signatures are unchanged. Eligible paged `auto` dispatch changes as described above; public wrapper `run()` implementations remain unchanged. Backend and FROST use the same FE graph contract, with no forced engine, split count or new caller knob.

**Remaining merge gates.** The latest published stable FE release is still 1.31.0; the 1.32 release/native pair needs qualification. Current-head upstream review/CI and broader paged-auto performance qualification remain outstanding, including skewed mixed-length batches. This consolidation is not a claim of universal eager or vLLM serving speedup.

### Review follow-up (931a28e2c)

- Preserve FP16/BF16 run-time calibration on the graph route: Q/K scales multiply the attention score scale; V scales O without changing LSE. GPU float32 scalars remain device bindings and are reread on replay. The kernel was receiving incomplete plumbing, not computing a correctly supplied scale incorrectly. FP8 scale handling is unchanged.
- Refresh wrapper-owned page tables retained by older CUDA Graphs even when a later plan supplies an external table. Preserve the captured pointer/row stride, copy the retained width and clear unused tail entries. Cover narrower/wider tables and cuDNN/FA2 transitions.
- Use the native D128 capability for D128 packed-capacity tests and restrict only the bounded-override case to its qualified architectures.
- Keep small work on FA2 using the work floor above. This addresses the [reported small-shape regression](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/6231#pullrequestreview-5556625244), without a tuple-specific blacklist or timing/winner golden. It does **not** establish universal wins for mixed-length batches; those remain a qualification item.

The original numerical probe was rerun **before narrowing admission**: auto still selected cuDNN, `v_scale=0.5` returned0.5, and an older owned-table capture returned3 after replanning to the external table. New tests also independently exercise nontrivial Q-only and K-only scaling, fresh device scalar pointers, and changed scalar/input values on replay.

Default warm execution remains unchanged: both wrapper `run()` bodies and the prepared runtime-key/match/execute functions are AST-identical to07d125a96. Scale-key normalization occurs only in the graph-build/cache path; no new per-run metadata staging or D2H scale extraction is introduced. No main-kernel change or new public API/knob.

### Host-visible work refinement (`884f48531`)

The reported skewed Q=[1,128], KV=[32768,2048], Hq=8 case now retains FA2 by using paired per-request work when host lengths are available. Keep the old cheap upper-bound rejection before optional-runtime queries. Explicit-bound GPU-length planning retains its previous no-readback policy: simply declining cuDNN would make FA2 stage those lengths on CPU. No run, kernel, cache, public-signature or caller-knob change.

Two new cases in the existing wrapper regression file guard that no-readback contract with synchronization debugging and a pending GPU event. They require an admitted CPU-metadata control dynamically, without a heuristic-winner or timing golden. Published931a passes both; an unpublished draft that declined GPU-only lengths fails both; the repaired implementation passes both. This change does not claim to close every remaining mixed-length selection gap or recover GPU-only distribution information.

### Historical B200 evidence

These are earlier component measurements, not measurements of this refreshed head.

**Ragged initialized-capacity slice (#6223):**

Same public ragged wrapper, ordinary shape override enabled, BF16 D128/V128, HN natural-log LSE, four independent layer buffers. B200 (148 SMs, 1000 W), cuDNN 9.27.0.42, FE at merged NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend#1452 (`16e6d19dc`), DSL 4.8, Torch 2.12 / CUDA 13.2. Baseline uses the exact #6209 attention source; two arm orders. GPU times include setup and combine. These are component measurements, not serving throughput.

| Shape | GPU replay before / after | Host plan before / after | Host enqueue per layer before / after |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| H32/8; Q=[300,40,40,40]; KV=[16384,8000,8000,8000] | 292.09 / 146.79 us | 39.52 / 40.51 us | 50.43 / 42.75 us |
| H64/8; Q=[128,10,10]; KV=[8192,8192,8192] | 205.85 / 78.59 us | 39.70 / 40.59 us | 48.66 / 40.57 us |
| H64/4; Q=[61,50,16,16]; KV=[11571,13689,15793,10376] | 369.68 / 100.01 us | 37.93 / 40.50 us | 48.55 / 42.01 us |

Plan plus four submissions improves 279.25→241.03us, 271.90→231.69us, and 269.41→238.10us respectively, despite the small plan-time increase. All three switch from the backend to the existing packed split2 plan; final workspace is 13.87/9.78/9.45MB. L2-flushed replay confirms the improvement. Separate `backend="auto"` runs for both BF16 and FP16 select cuDNN/FROST on all three cases and pass O/LSE and changed-input replay checks.

This evidence applies to FI wrappers initialized with `use_cuda_graph=True` and an enforced query capacity. It does not establish a gain for ordinary dynamic wrappers or stock vLLM serving; those paths need separate capacity integration and end-to-end validation.


**Paged-auto slice (#6231, candidate `63b0955fd`):**

B200,148SM/1000W; Torch2.12/CUDA13.2, CuTeDSL4.8, cuDNN9.27.0.42, FEdevelopc57af965 plus #1469. Exact candidate `63b0955fd`; public FI wrapper with ordinary `use_cuda_graph=False` planning, pinned CPU plan metadata, no caller-supplied block table/maxima. FA2 is the same-source explicit backend and FA4 is vLLM-flash-attention `9cd61de38763d712bb6ce56e2a02cc2bf718c89f` (vLLM source `cbee82324c4ac2e780514122604f8f5fdb7c1d21`). Two reversed measurement orders,32 independent layer buffers, warm CUDA-event replay including all helper/combine kernels, plus directly timed eager attention-chain completion. Outputs and changed-input replay are checked against an FP64 reference.

| B/Hq/Hkv; Q; KV | FA2 GPU us/layer | cuDNN auto GPU us/layer | FA4 GPU us/layer | FA2 plan + 32 completed layers ms | cuDNN auto ms |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
|1/16/4;128;8192|40.46|23.50|32.10|1.386|1.357|
|1/64/8;128;8192|131.81|48.47|78.96|4.328|1.820|
|1/16/4;513;16384|237.83|84.65|136.82|7.716|2.974|
|3/16/4;[257,1,1];8192|90.17|54.06|75.59|2.981|1.993|

L2-flushed GPU replay confirms the direction. This is an attention-only proxy, not serving throughput. Host cost is still higher than FA2: plan94–103us versus43–44us, enqueue about36us versus13us per layer. The first row is consequently close in a completed32-layer eager chain, despite its GPU gain; short host-bound chains can lose. CUDA Graph replay and per-step planning must be evaluated separately. New bucket first-use still needs prewarming, and stock vLLM can select directTRTLLM before reaching this wrapper.


The fixed-graph capacity variant also has an eager tradeoff: historical measurements added approximately 4–6 us per submission while reducing GPU replay. Neither these results nor the paged proxy establish stock-vLLM serving throughput. New bucket first-use must be prewarmed.

Reproducible public-wrapper host/graph benchmark:

```bash
python benchmarks/bench_cudnn_wrapper_host.py --kind paged --batch 1 --q 128 --kv 8192 --qo-heads 16 --kv-heads 4 --layout HND --backends fa2 auto --replan --output paged-auto.json
```


## 🔍 Related Issues

Consolidates #6168, #6209, #6213, #6216 and #6223. Related FE selection/capacity work: NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend#1439, NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend#1452 and NVIDIA/cudnn-frontend#1469.

## 🚀 Pull Request Checklist

Thank you for contributing to FlashInfer! Before we review your pull request, please make sure the following items are complete.

### ✅ Pre-commit Checks

- [x] I have installed `pre-commit` by running `pip install pre-commit` (or used your preferred method).
- [ ] I have installed the hooks with `pre-commit install`.
- [ ] I have run the hooks manually with `pre-commit run --all-files` and fixed any reported issues.

> If you are unsure about how to set up `pre-commit`, see [the pre-commit documentation](https://pre-commit.com/).

Scoped `pre-commit run --files` passed for all nine changed files. The all-files checkbox above is intentionally not claimed.

## 🧪 Tests

Current `884f48531` production: **224 passed / 1 multi-GPU skip** across the prepared-contract and wrapper-regression suites on native SM100, development FE1.32/native, cuDNN9.27, DSL4.8. Separate explicit-bound changing-length probes pass O/LSE without waiting for GPU work. Scoped hooks pass for the three changed files. Fresh-head upstream CI/review remains pending; the previously reported 31/31 CI result applies to931a28e2.

Repair qualification at `931a28e2c`: native SM100 **362 passed / 1 multi-GPU skip** across the same five files (combined broad and final affected-file runs). Final scale-key/capture/prepared check: **84 passed**. Independent H100 scale/capture check: **36 passed / 6 FP8 architecture skips**. FE development1.32/native, cuDNN9.27, DSL4.8. These correctness counts are not a stable-release or serving qualification. Scoped pre-commit passed on all six repair files.

New half-scale and retained-table cases were first run against unchanged07d125a96 production code and failed, then passed after repair. Existing FP8 tests and tolerances are retained. No new test file was added.


- [x] Tests have been added or updated as needed.
- [ ] Exact-head upstream GPU CI is complete.

Earlier consolidation candidate `07d125a96`: **312 passed / 13 skipped** across the five focused files below on SM107, development FE1.32 with matching native extension, cuDNN9.27, DSL4.8, CUDA13.5 and Torch2.15 development. This is correctness/capture qualification, not new performance evidence. Twelve skips require SM100 paged-auto admission; one requires a second visible GPU.

The first run passed 283 tests; 29 reference/fallback tests stopped before execution because the isolated source install lacked its generated `flashinfer/data` JIT source links. After restoring the standard build-backend links, exactly those 29 passed. Source and tolerances were unchanged. All nine PR file hashes match the committed candidate. The native-log2 mock separately reproduced three workspace-query AttributeErrors before its fixture correction; all 28 native-log2 tests pass afterward.

```bash
pytest tests/attention/test_cudnn_native_log2.py tests/attention/test_cudnn_prepared_contract.py tests/attention/test_cudnn_ragged_shape_override.py tests/attention/test_cudnn_wrapper_regressions.py tests/attention/test_cudnn_prepared_graph.py -q -o addopts=
```

New-head upstream CI/review and SM100 paged-auto qualification remain pending. Older B200 and released-FE fallback validation remains documented on the superseded PRs; it is not relabeled as fresh-head validation.

Coverage includes O/LSE references, changed-input replay, retained captures, pointer rebinding, NH/HN Stats, workspace-constrained fallback, runtime capability gates, page-table growth and provider transitions. No new test files, timing thresholds or heuristic-winner goldens are introduced.

## 🔬 Experimental Track

<!-- Only for PRs submitted under the experimental policy (CONTRIBUTING.md → "Experimental APIs and Backends").
     Leave this section untouched for normal PRs. -->

- [ ] This PR is **experimental**: it adds or changes code under `flashinfer/experimental/` and/or an `@flashinfer_experimental_api`. Tracking issue: #
  - [ ] The tracking issue names an owner, the reason for the experimental path, and a graduation plan with a target release.
  - [ ] Core changes are limited to a thin entry point (signature, shared validation, feature-gate check, backend selection, handoff).
  - [ ] Tests live in `tests/experimental/` and were validated on the intended hardware; a runnable example is included.
  - [ ] Nothing is registered in `flashinfer/aot.py`, and no experimental backend is reachable from `backend="auto"` without `FLASHINFER_ALLOW_EXPERIMENTAL_AUTO_BACKENDS=1`. (Calling an `@flashinfer_experimental_api` or naming a backend explicitly is itself the opt-in and needs no environment variable.)
  - [ ] **Test scope declared below.** The experimental CI lane runs exactly these targets, so keep them as narrow as the change allows.

<!-- Required for experimental PRs. Replace the commented lines below with your targets.
     Do not delete the fence or change its `experimental-tests` tag — the experimental-track
     watcher reads it verbatim to decide which targets to ask CI for. -->

```experimental-tests
# One target per line: a directory or a file. (A pytest ::selector is not
# supported -- the sharding runner cannot consume one.) Must be under
# tests/experimental/ and must exist. Delete these comment lines and add yours, e.g.
#
#   tests/experimental/test_my_backend.py
#   tests/experimental/my_backend/
#
# Declaring the whole tree (tests/experimental/) is allowed but means every
# experimental PR pays for every other feature's tests, in every matrix cell.
```

## Reviewer Notes

Please focus on initialization capacity versus live length; cache separation by workspace/capacity; and ownership of metadata retained by captured calls. The refresh preserves main's LSE safety checks and fixes an existing mock that did not implement the graph workspace query. The review follow-up additionally repairs runtime scales and retained external-table transitions; details above.

Remaining qualification: the actual stable FE1.32 release/native pair, exact-head upstream CI/review, and SM100 measurements of plan + completed eager chains as well as GPU replay. Historical small/host-bound chains and lower-SM configurations are not covered by a universal speedup claim. The capacity benefit requires an initialized graph-mode capacity; ordinary vLLM integration still needs its own serving validation.

The PR is currently Ready for review; it is not being merged while those qualification gates remain open.

title: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash: default to 1017, install from the 0.31.0 pip wheel
body:
## Summary

Adds [deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017) (2026-10-17 weight update) to the DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash recipe and makes it the default variant, mirroring how DeepSeek-V4-Pro rolled its 0813 release forward.

- `default` → `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017`, pill **FP8 (1017)**
- new `fp8` variant → the 2026-09-09 launch checkpoint (recipe's own repo), pill **FP8 (0909)**, kept for reproducing earlier results
- Both variants share the H100 (Engram CPU offload) and DGX Station (expert offload) per-GPU overrides via a YAML anchor
- Guide: new *Checkpoints* section; client examples (reasoning snippet, Verifying curl) use the 1017 model id; 1017 model card added to References
- `date_updated: 2026-10-17`

## Why a variant swap is safe

Compared the two HF repos:
- `config.json`, `tokenizer_config.json`, `encoding/` and `inference/config.json` are byte-identical
- `model.safetensors.index.json`: same 96,085 tensors, same 510.3 GB total
- 1017 ships no `chat_template.jinja` — not needed, since `--tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41` (already in `base_args`) encodes prompts in vLLM's Python encoder

So the generated commands are identical apart from the model id (checked on H100, GB200, DGX Station GB300, MI355X).

## Install: pip wheel, no nightly

vLLM 0.30.0 registers `DeepseekV41ForCausalLM` and the `deepseek_v41` tokenizer; 0.31.0 adds the KV-offload fix (#57145) and the ROCm Engram host-memory gate (#57491). Checked against the `v0.31.0` tree: every flag the NVIDIA commands emit (`--engram-config`, `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV41` / `FLASHMLA_MEGA_ATTN_DSV41`, `--kernel-config`, `--prefill-schedule-interval`, `--offload-backend`/`--cpu-offload-params`, the DSpark adaptive-verification config) is present, and the Rust frontend registers the `deepseek_v41` parsers.

- `min_vllm_version: "0.31.0"`; drop `nightly_required` and `install.pip: false` → pip tab + `vllm/vllm-openai:latest` on NVIDIA
- AMD Docker stays on `nightly-rocm100` (the verified image). **MI355X hides pip** (`install.pip: false` per GPU): `--monokernel` (#60397/#61082), the ROCm MXFP4 indexer (#58671) and Gluon sparse MLA (#53492) are on main but not in 0.31.0. title: Add reflection/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B recipe
body:
## Add `reflection/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B` recipe

Beam is Reflection's 501B-total / 23B-active MoE (52 layers, 256 routed experts with top-8 routing, hybrid 512-token sliding window plus NoPE full attention, 1M context, Harmony chat format). Beam support hasn't shipped in any vLLM release or nightly yet, so the recipe is Docker-only on the `vllm/vllm-openai:reflection-beam` image.

### What the builder renders

| Hardware | Default command | Status |
|---|---|---|
| B300 (page default) | NVFP4, TP4, `--attention-backend FLASHINFER --moe-backend flashinfer_trtllm` | ✅ verified, release checkpoint |
| B200 / GB200 / GB300 | NVFP4, TP4 (same flags) | eligible, not run |
| H200 | NVFP4 via Marlin, TP8. **Recommended: the FP8 variant, TP8** | ✅ verified (FP8 and NVFP4), proto checkpoints |
| H100 | NVFP4 via Marlin, TP8 | 80 GB budget simulated on H200 |

- Variants: `default` = NVFP4 (`reflection/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B-NVFP4`), `fp8` (`-FP8`), `bf16` (base repo, only on 8x B200/B300).
- The site has no per-GPU default variant, so H200 also opens on NVFP4. The guide tells H200 users to switch to FP8, the same approach as vllm-project/recipes#1012.
- Features: the `beam` reasoning and tool-call parsers are on by default. DFlash2 (`reflection/Beam-1.0-501B-A23B-DFlash2`, `num_speculative_tokens: 7`) is opt-in.
- Strategies: single-node TP / TEP / DEP.
- Install: Docker only, `vllm/vllm-openai:reflection-beam`. No pip path: the nightly wheels don't carry the Beam implementation.
- Hardware: NVIDIA only. The four AMD profiles are marked `unsupported` (CUDA-only kernels, CUDA-only image).
- `date_added`: 2026-10-16, the launch day.

### Evidence

Each verified run passed: `/health`, `/v1/models`, chat with `finish_reason: stop`, `reasoning_content`, parsed `tool_calls`.

The numbers below stay out of the recipe, following the repo convention: few recipes publish measured throughput, and upstream held back such a PR as premature (#58). Workload: 8 chat prompts (code, math, prose, translation) × 8 runs, up to 1,500 output tokens, temperature 0.6, reasoning on. Output tok/s:

| Config | GPUs | c=1 | c=16 | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| B300 NVFP4 TP4 | 4 | 285 | 1,769 | 17.1M KV tokens; first start ~30 min (one-time FlashInfer MoE autotune) |
| B300 NVFP4 TP4 + DFlash2 | 4 | 517 | 2,347 | 20% acceptance, ~3.8 tokens/step |
| B300 FP8 TP8 | 8 | 217 | 1,300 | 36.1M KV tokens |
| H200 FP8 TP8 (proto) | 8 | 156 | 1,059 | 14M KV tokens |
| H200 FP8 TP8 + DFlash2 (proto) | 8 | 307 | 1,781 | 21% acceptance, ~3.7 tokens/step |
| H200 FP8 TEP8 / DEP8 (proto) | 8 | 129 / 73 | 1,018 / 761 | both pass; slower than TP at c≤16 |
| H200 NVFP4 Marlin TP8 (proto) | 8 | 210 | 1,487 | Humming (auto-selected): 202 / 1,315 |

### B300 functional matrix (2026-10-11)

Run on 8x B300 with a vLLM build that includes the Beam tool-calling fix. Every command is the one the site generates. Each run passed a 12-check suite:
- health, chat, and reasoning-effort levels
- single, parallel, streamed, `required` and round-trip tool calls
- a ~24K-token prompt
- prefix-cache reuse
- 16 concurrent requests

KV-offload runs also passed a reload check: clear the GPU cache, resend the ~32K-token prompt, and the hit must come from the offload tier with the same answer at temperature 0.

| Area | Configs | Result |
|---|---|---|
| NVFP4 | TP4, TEP8, DEP8, each ± DFlash2 | ✅ |
| NVFP4, Rust frontend | TP4 ± DFlash2 | ✅ |
| FP8 | TP8, TEP8, DEP8, TP8 + DFlash2 | ✅ |
| BF16 | TP8, TEP8, DEP8, TP8 + DFlash2 | ✅ (140 GiB of weights per GPU) |
| 1M context | 1,034,106-token prompt, needles at 2% / 50% / 97% | ✅ all recalled |
| KV offload | Simple, Offloading CPU, Offloading CPU+FS (also reloads from disk after a restart), LMCache | ✅ |
| KV offload | Mooncake (both topologies) | ⛔ not tested: this pod caps memlock at 8 MB, so RDMA can't register memory |

Notes:
- **Tool calling needs the fix.** On builds without it, the Rust frontend returns 500 and Python silently drops the grammar.
- **Site issues found during the runs.**
  - The Mooncake install line pulls the CUDA 12 wheel; `mooncake-transfer-engine-cuda13` is needed here.
  - The Offloading CPU default of 512 GiB needs that much `/dev/shm`. It passed at 32 GiB.
- **Startup.** It took 160–820 s with caches warm, and no run hit the engine-ready timeout.

### Before merge

- [ ] Confirm the parameter counts: the recipe says 501B / 23B, the early card said 502B / ~24B.
- [ ] When a vLLM release carries Beam support and the tool-calling fix, restore the pip install path and re-run the B300 default on it.
- [ ] Re-run H200 FP8 on the release checkpoint (the badge currently rests on proto checkpoints).
- [ ] Mooncake on a pod with `--ulimit memlock=-1`.
- [x] ~~BF16, Rust frontend, KV offload (Simple / Offloading / LMCache), TEP / DEP on B300~~ (see the matrix above)
- [ ] Not run: GPUs other than B300/H200, FP8 KV cache, multi-node.

title: [Perf][MRV2] Share GDN, Mamba and Kimi-K3 KDA batch metadata across KV cache groups
body:
## Overview

Move MRV2 cross-group metadata reuse into GDN, Mamba and Kimi-K3 KDA builders, extending merged #58762 to KDA and speculative Mamba.
Explicitly avoiding the MRV1 code reuse from the interim solution in #58762 

## Claims

- Share batch metadata while preserving group-local state, checkpoints and CUDA graph buffers. Every group, the first included, derives those in one per-group function; cross-group tests compare every metadata field with an independent build.
- Extend Mamba aligned-index precompute from plain GDN and nvidia KDA to Mamba1, Mamba2, ShortConv, PLE short-conv and ROCm KDA, and remove redundant slices. No MRV1 features restored.
- PLE short-conv, for non-speculative batches, and ROCm KDA now also share metadata; neither is GPU-tested.
- Move Mamba2's per-group checkpoint regather from #57329 into `_update_state_indices`, so the V1 `update_block_table` path and the MRV2 cross-group path both use it.
- Works with MRV1 fully removed: MRV2 no longer calls `update_block_table` or reads `supports_update_block_table`. With `gpu_model_runner.py` and that API deleted, the 13 Mamba test modules still pass on `eb206ad240` (CPU).

## Validation

Two GB10 nodes, CUDA 13, full Python sources with compatible precompiled binaries. Measured `8abc56f46c` against main `710ac56e69`.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/v1/attention/test_{gdn,mamba,replayssm}_metadata_builder.py \
  tests/models/kimi_k3/test_kda_metadata.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_mamba_hybrid_model_state.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_attn_utils.py \
  tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_target_dependent_ar_speculator.py::test_pcp_draft_metadata_keeps_graph_padding_in_decode
```

- Focused: **204 passed, no failures/skips**. Wider: **1194 passed / 5 failed / 188 skipped**, versus main **1189 / 4 / 188**.
- Four failures reproduce on main (CUPTI/Proton). Final `b2f2182ce8` fixes the remaining string-device constructor failure; the GPU reproducer passes with MRV2 on/off. No full-suite or benchmark rerun after that one-line fix.
- **103 metadata scenarios match; 279 CUDA captures and 837 changing-input replays per revision pass.** All eight serving synchronization checks pass.
- Serial greedy tokens/logprobs match on all four models. Mixed-batch variation also occurs on main. Kimi uses dummy weights; no quality claim.

Output-interval change with paired 95% intervals: five independent main/PR pairs, four for TP2. CUDA API counts use separate 200-step profiles.

| Model | c1 | c16 | CUDA APIs/step, main→PR |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Granite-4.0-H-micro, align | −0.45% [−0.58, −0.31] | −0.47% [−0.59, −0.36] | 130.98→68.98 |
| Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8 + DFlash | −0.12% [−0.56, +0.33] | −0.24% [−0.95, +0.48] | 122.05→122.05 |
| Reduced Kimi-K3, align/RecoverSSM | −0.53% [−1.37, +0.33] | −0.30% [−1.10, +0.50] | 103.08→99.08 |
| Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8, TP2/MTP | −0.06% [−1.40, +1.30] | −0.41% [−1.06, +0.24] | 144.97→144.95 / 143.94→143.94 |

Intervals measure engine output timing, not GPU execution time. ROCm, SM100 and single-host multi-GPU cases remain untested. The GPU results above predate the rebase and the per-group function; on CPU, the metadata of 630 two-group scenarios (values and buffer aliasing) is unchanged from the previous revision `01607f5869`. `eb206ad240` on main `02e55d2af3`, Mac CPU: 13 Mamba test modules **260 passed / 86 skipped** versus main **240 / 86**, no failures; pre-commit and mypy pass. No regression means it maintains the performance improvement from #58762 

## Details

Cache lifetime is one metadata build, including capture; keys include cache spec and builder class. #58818 targets FlashMLA and shares cache plumbing; whichever lands second must deduplicate it.

title: [Core][DSV4] Compact MXFP4 indexer KV cache and packed group overlays
body:
## Context

When DeepSeek V4 uses MXFP4 indexer K values, engine reserves the larger FP8 row for them. Its packed KV planner also buckets layers by page size, leaving avoidable holes when different cache groups have different mixtures of page sizes.

This PR:

- sizes MXFP4 indexer K rows from their packed values and UE8M0 scales (`head_dim / 2 + head_dim / 32` bytes), reducing the 128-dimensional row from 132 to 68 bytes;
- lays out every packed cache group densely in one per-block slab and overlays the group layouts, while keeping layers within each group disjoint; and
- removes cross-group SWA page padding that the dense planner no longer needs.

The packing change is generic to the existing packed-cache path. DeepSeek V4 uses that path by default; other hybrid models retain the existing opt-in via `enable_cross_layers_blocks`.

## Memory results

Matched DeepSeek-V4-Pro DEP8 startup measurements on GB200:

| Backend / KV budget | Baseline blocks | This change | Increase |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| FlashInfer sparse / 26.46 GiB | 21,709 | 23,120 | +6.50% |
| FlashMLA sparse / 26.09 GiB | 19,015 | 21,306 | +12.05% |

For the FlashInfer layout, physical block stride decreases from 1,308,672 to 1,228,800 bytes (-6.10%). For the FlashMLA `fp8_ds_mla` layout, it decreases from 1,473,408 to 1,315,008 bytes (-10.75%).
