title: [Perf][DSv4.1] Share the FlashMLA decode plan across KV cache groups
body:
## Purpose

`DeepseekSparseSWAMetadataBuilder.build()` creates one empty `FlashMLASchedMeta` per DeepSeek-V4 layer type. The first `flash_mla_with_kvcache` call of each type runs FlashMLA's tile-scheduler planner, and the later layers of that type reuse the plan (the comment calls it "shared across all ~60 layers of that type within a decode step").

However, the builder runs once per KV cache group. With the packed KV cache layout, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash's sliding-window caches are spread over 8 groups, and each group builds its own holders. So the planner runs once per (group, layer type). A torch-profiler trace of one TP8 decode step shows 18 planner launches in the target model (before layers 0-9 and 20-27) and 3 in the DSpark drafter (one per draft layer), where 4 are enough.

`get_mla_metadata_kernel` is a single 32-thread block with a serial loop over the SM partitions, and every launch sits in front of its layer's attention. On H20 it takes 16.6 µs per launch at 1 request and about 41 µs at 64 requests.

A plan depends on the batch shape and on the values of the decode `topk_length` / `extra_topk_length`. FlashMLA's interface allows reuse only while those values stay the same, but it asserts only shapes and config. Across the KV cache groups of one metadata build pass the values do match:
- The SWA lengths come from the same query and sequence lengths, window, valid-token mask and `replay_start`. Each group builds the mask from its own slot mapping, but every sliding-window group writes each scheduled token, so the masks agree; `replay_start` is one tensor passed to every builder.
- The top-k lengths count the valid entries each index layer writes. Every decode top-k path fills the entries past a row end derived from `seq_lens` and `next_n` alone with -1 (for example `rowEnd` in `csrc/libtorch_stable/sampler.cu`), under the same valid-token mask. So each index layer of a compress ratio yields `min(rowEnd, topk)`.

That second point is also why a group's same-type layers can already share one plan today, though they take their top-k from different index layers.

This PR lets the groups share the holders:
- MRV2's `build_attn_metadata` passes one dict to every group's `CommonAttentionMetadata`, next to the existing `_token_to_req_indices_cache`.
- The sliding-window builder takes its plan holders from that dict, keyed by its block size, causality and index width.

What stays as before:
- Callers that do not pass the dict (the V1 runner, the draft metadata refresh of the autoregressive speculator) keep one plan per group.
- DBO micro-batches and the DSpark drafter build in separate passes, so they never share a plan.
- SM100 does not take this path: it defaults to FlashMLA mega attention, which does not use these plan holders.

Planner launches per decode step drop from 21 to 4.

**Duplicate check.** `gh pr list --repo vllm-project/vllm --state all --search` for `tile_sched`, `FlashMLASchedMeta`, `get_mla_metadata`, `tile scheduler` and `planner flashmla` shows no PR that shares the plan across KV cache groups.

Related: #58762 (RFC #58638) reuses Mamba/GDN metadata across KV cache groups in the same `build_attn_metadata` loop. This PR does the same for DeepSeek-V4's FlashMLA plans, which are built per group however many groups there are.

## Test Plan

**Setup**
- Hardware: 8× H20 (SM90, 96 GB, NVLink).
- Model: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, HF revision `dba1be0a40aa45a94ad051997016db3960a90277`.
- vLLM: "main" is the nightly wheel `0.30.1rc1.dev85+g8b84e1506` as installed; "this PR" is the same wheel with this diff applied as a Python overlay. The three changed files are identical between that nightly and current `main`.

**Server.** TP8 + EP8. DSpark uses synthetic acceptance with a configured mean acceptance length of 3.51, the same distribution in both arms, so acceptance does not depend on the model's outputs:

```bash
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --revision dba1be0a40aa45a94ad051997016db3960a90277 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 --enable-expert-parallel \
  --language-model-only --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --max-model-len 262144 \
  --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 --max-num-seqs 128 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 \
  --no-enable-prefix-caching --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":false}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,"draft_sample_method":"probabilistic","rejection_sample_method":"synthetic","synthetic_acceptance_length":3.51,"enable_adaptive_verification":false}' \
  --profiler-config '{"profiler":"torch","torch_profiler_dir":"<dir>","torch_profiler_activities":["CUDA"],"torch_profiler_with_stack":false,"ignore_frontend":true,"max_iterations":20}'
```

**Load.** One `vllm bench serve` call per point, with these values:

| Point | ISL | OSL | C | N |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 8K prompt TTFT | 8192 | 1 | 1 | 5 |
| 1K in / 1K out, C1 | 1024 | 1024 | 1 | 6 |
| 1K in / 1K out, C64 | 1024 | 1024 | 64 | 192 |


```bash
vllm bench serve --backend openai --endpoint /v1/completions --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len <ISL> --random-output-len <OSL> --random-range-ratio 0 --ignore-eos \
  --max-concurrency <C> --num-prompts <N> --num-warmups <C> --seed 1
```

**Arms.** Five fresh servers, run in the order B1, A1, A2, B2, B3:
- main (A1, A2);
- a prototype that shared the plans at forward time (B1, B2);
- this PR's metadata-level sharing (B3).

B3, the profile and this PR's GSM8K runs used the diff before `non_causal` joined the cache key. In every measured path the target groups are causal and the drafter builds in its own pass, so that key element changes nothing there. Every arm passes the same `--profiler-config`, which stays idle while the benchmarks run.

**Profile.** 20 decode steps under the torch profiler (`/start_profile`), 1K in / 1K out, at C1 and C64.

**Accuracy.** Full GSM8K (1,319 questions) through `/v1/chat/completions`: 5-shot multi-turn chat, thinking off (`chat_template_kwargs: {"thinking": false}`), temperature 0, seed 123, `max_tokens` 1024, 32 concurrent requests; 

## Test Result

**Serving.** The last column compares B3 with the mean of the main arms. Higher output throughput and lower ITL and TTFT are better.

| Point | Metric | main A1 | main A2 | this PR B3 | Change |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1K in / 1K out, C1 | output tok/s | 317.3 | 318.9 | 326.0 | **+2.5%** |
| 1K in / 1K out, C1 | median ITL (ms) | 10.42 | 10.36 | 10.12 | **−2.6%** |
| 1K in / 1K out, C64 | output tok/s | 1937.6 | 1942.7 | 1949.2 | +0.5% |
| 1K in / 1K out, C64 | median ITL (ms) | 84.15 | 83.84 | 83.51 | −0.6% |
| 8K prompt, C1 | TTFT (ms) | 1216.5 | 1220.0 | 1216.6 | −0.1% |

B3 is a single run. The main arms differ by 0.5% at C1 and 0.3% at C64, so the C64 change is small. The gain is largest at low concurrency, where the planner is a larger share of a short step. Prefill does not plan decode tiles, so TTFT is unchanged. The forward-time prototype, which also launches the planner 4 times per step, measured 325.2 and 329.2 tok/s at C1 and 1957.9 and 1952.6 tok/s at C64.

**Profile** (rank 0, 20 decode steps, B3's code):

| | main | this PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| Planner launches per step (target + drafter) | 21 | 4 |
| Planner time per step, C1 | 348 µs | 66 µs |
| Planner time per step, C64 | 868 µs | 161 µs |

**Accuracy.** Two full GSM8K runs per side, each on a fresh server:

| GSM8K, 5-shot chat, greedy (1,319 questions) | main | this PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| Run 1 | 96.97% (1279) | 96.44% (1272) |
| Run 2 | 96.51% (1273) | 96.74% (1276) |
| Mean | 96.74% | 96.59% |
| DSpark acceptance length (runs 1 / 2) | 3.863 / 3.851 | 3.865 / 3.851 |

main's own two runs differ by 6 questions, more than the 2-question gap between the means. Greedy decoding at concurrency 32 varies with how requests are batched, so this rules out a large accuracy change but cannot show identical outputs.

**What covers the new path.** The unit tests below construct `CommonAttentionMetadata` directly, so `_cross_group_cache` stays `None` and they never take the sharing branch. They only show nothing else changed. The new path is covered on H20 by:
- the profile: 4 planner launches per step, so the groups do share;
- the serving runs;
- GSM8K with real DSpark verification.

The serving numbers use synthetic acceptance to measure speed and say nothing about accuracy.

**Tests.** `tests/v1/attention/test_deepseek_v4_swa_visible.py` and `tests/v1/attention/test_dspark_noncausal_sparse_mla.py` give 38 passed and 31 skipped on one H20, with and without this diff. The pinned `ruff` (0.14.0) and `typos` checks pass on the changed files.

```bash
pytest tests/v1/attention/test_deepseek_v4_swa_visible.py tests/v1/attention/test_dspark_noncausal_sparse_mla.py
```

AI assistance: Claude Code helped profile and run the benchmarks. I reviewed every changed line and checked the results above.

title: [CI][Test] GLM-5.3-Flash layer-pruned checkpoint tests (e2e, KV offload, NIXL PD)
body:
## Purpose

Give the GLM-5.3-Flash serving stack (hybrid KDA + DeepSeek-sparse-MLA with the kpool indexer / tail
scratch group, fp8 MoE, mHC, MTP, PD disaggregation, KV offload) CI coverage that does not need a
4-GPU node holding the 328 GB checkpoint.

The asset is a **layer-pruned real checkpoint**, `JaredforReal/GLM-5.3-Flash-4L`: original layers 0-3
(one 3x KDA + 1x DSA-MLA period, dense MLP on 0-2, MoE on 3) plus the MTP layer, with **every width
unchanged** (288 routed experts, 64 KDA heads, MLA/indexer dims, vision tower). Only whole layers were
removed, so kernel selection and the KV cache layout match the 300B model: the same
`{MLA+indexer}`, `{kpool tail}` and Mamba groups aliasing the MLA slot, and the same auto block size
(4352 / 2176 / 1152 tokens at TP1 / TP2 / TP4). 18.5 GiB, loads in ~8 s. Derivation and the exact config
edits are documented in the model card.

New tests (SM90/SM100 only: the DeepGEMM paged-MQA indexer and FlashMLA/FlashInfer sparse MLA do not run on L4):

| test | GPUs | guards |
|---|---|---|
| `tests/models/glm5next/test_pruned_e2e.py` | 1 | KV groups = {MLA + indexer}, {kpool tail}, 3 Mamba groups aliasing the MLA tensor; greedy reproducibility across a block boundary with a prompt longer than `index_topk`; MTP drafter loads and agrees with target-only greedy. A strict xfail documents the `fused_recurrent_kda` gridDim.z overflow at 64 heads x 1024 seqs (#56973, fixed by #56974; the marker must be dropped once that lands).; **prefill checkpoint pages**: a prompt crossing a block boundary leaves, in every Mamba group, a cached checkpoint page equal to a cold prefill ending at that boundary (relative error <= 0.03 observed, >= 1 when a group's checkpoint goes to another group's page, the #59536 regression that the greedy repeat test does not notice) |
| `tests/v1/attention/test_gdn_metadata_builder.py::test_update_block_table_matches_fresh_build` | 1 | `update_block_table()` for a sibling Mamba group equals a fresh `build()` on that group's block table in every metadata field (recursively over nested dataclasses), so a per-group field added later cannot stay pointed at the source group; fails before #59536 on `checkpoint.state_indices` |
| `tests/v1/kv_offload/test_glm5next_pruned_e2e.py` | 1 | SimpleCPUOffloadConnector / OffloadingConnector round trip through `reset_prefix_cache`, asserting CPU hits and identical tokens. Fails on main today because the kpool tail group (block 4, not prefix-cacheable) is not skipped (`resolve_block_hashes` assert / `tokens_per_block=4 not divisible by tokens_per_hash`); SimpleCPUOffload passes with #56810. |
| `tests/v1/kv_connector/nixl_integration/run_glm5next_pd_test.sh` + `test_hybrid_pd_consistency.py` | 2 | NixlConnector 1P1D with `VLLM_SSM_CONV_STATE_LAYOUT=DS`; reuses `test_mamba_prefix_cache.py` (its ~9000-token prompt spans two 4352-token blocks) and checks P-only vs P->D top-1 logprobs within a tolerance. Hybrid PD recomputes the last prompt token on D (`_prefill_backoff`), so exact text equality as in `test_edge_cases.py` is not the right assertion for this model. |

Buildkite: single-GPU jobs on `h200_35gb` (models_language.yaml, lm_eval.yaml), the PD job on 2x `h100`
(disaggregated.yaml); MIG slices cannot do cross-device NIXL and the existing PD sweeps run on L4. The
Pruned E2E step also depends on `vllm/v1/attention/backends/gdn_attn.py`, `vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/`,
`vllm/v1/worker/gpu/` and `vllm/v1/core/`: #58762 (cross-group metadata reuse) changed only those paths and
would not have triggered a step keyed on `vllm/models/glm5next/` alone.

Known interactions: #55219 (draft) replaces `KpoolTailSpec` with a `CircularBufferSpec` tail, which
would change the spec names asserted in `test_kv_cache_layout`.

## Why this is not duplicating an existing PR

Searched open PRs/issues for "GLM-5.3-Flash CI", "glm5next test", "pruned checkpoint", "GLM-5.3-Flash nixl"
(2026-09-18): no PR adds a reduced GLM-5.3-Flash checkpoint or e2e/PD/offload tests for it. Related but
different: #56974 (KDA grid.z fix; the kernel still launches `grid.z = num_seqs * heads`, but the TP1
startup at `max_num_seqs=1024` no longer reaches it on current main, so `test_default_max_num_seqs_tp1` is a
plain test now), #56810 (SimpleCPUOffload tail-group skip, the offload test's expected fix), #55219 (tail spec
rework), #59536 (the checkpoint-page regression the new test guards; merged 2026-10-01).

## Test Plan

```bash
# 1 GPU (SM90+)
pytest -v -s tests/models/glm5next/test_pruned_e2e.py
pytest -v -s tests/v1/kv_offload/test_glm5next_pruned_e2e.py
pytest -v -s tests/v1/attention/test_gdn_metadata_builder.py -k update_block_table
# 2 GPUs
bash tests/v1/kv_connector/nixl_integration/run_glm5next_pd_test.sh
```

`GLM5_PRUNED_MODEL` / `MODEL` override the checkpoint path for local runs.

## Test Result

GB300 x4, main 18553c5c9f, `enforce_eager`:

| run | result |
|---|---|
| `test_pruned_e2e.py` (TP1) | 3 passed + 1 xfailed (strict) on main 18553c5c9f; **5 passed** on main b538d807ff (2026-10-01, includes #59536). Checkpoint-page relative errors per layer (conv / recurrent): 4e-4 / 2e-3, 1e-2 / 9e-3, 2e-2 / 2e-2; with #59536's two files reverted the same test fails with 2.4 / 4.3, 1 / 1, 1 / 1 |
| `test_gdn_metadata_builder.py -k update_block_table` | 4 passed on main b538d807ff; the new equivalence test fails on the pre-#59536 tree at `checkpoint.state_indices` |
| `test_glm5next_pruned_e2e.py` on main | 2 failed as designed (tail-group asserts above) |
| same, SimpleCPUOffloadConnector on the #56810 branch | passed (CPU prefix-cache hits > 0 after `reset_prefix_cache`, cold == warm tokens) |
| `run_glm5next_pd_test.sh` (1P1D, `--max-num-seqs 256`) | 2 passed: D-side prefix hits cut NIXL transfer 26.8 MB -> 22.2 MB, outputs equal; P-only vs P->D first-4 max logprob delta 0.20 / 0.07 / 0.61 (short / mid / 6.5k-token) with P-only vs D-only 0.00 / 0.00 / 0.06 |

Notes from the local runs: all tests are text-only (`limit_mm_per_prompt={"image":0,"video":0}`) because
cold encoder profiling of the 24-block vision tower took ~25 min of cuDNN/CUTLASS JIT; the fp8 MoE was
forced to `deep_gemm` on this SM100 node because the FlashInfer TRT-LLM MoE module was re-JIT-compiled on
every engine start (not relevant on the H100/H200 CI targets).

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for the analysis, the checkpoint builder and the test drafts; all
runs above were executed by the author.

Single-node H20-3e report: vision CP + DSpark, long-prefill improvements, and three upstream PRs
Thanks for maintaining this roadmap and for the kernel/CP work behind it. We have been integrating and testing DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on
one 8× NVIDIA H20-3e server
, with text, image+text, tool calling, streaming, and cache reporting as requirements.
Our October 5–7 experiments started from
unmodified SGLang v0.5.21
and ended with a production deployment of a pinned integration build. The strongest paired comparisons were:
524,032-token cold TTFT: 323.261 → 25.531 s
, a
92.1% reduction / 12.66× speedup
.
C64 aggregate output: 877.01 → 2,534.61 token/s (+189.0%)
; per-request streaming decode:
15.69 → 49.10 token/s (+213.0%)
.
These are
whole-deployment improvements
, not the isolated effect of any one PR. We have contributed
#39306
,
#42922
, and
#42924
; their narrower validation and attribution are described below.
1. Setup and measurement scope
Hardware: 8× H20-3e, SM90, approximately 140 GiB visible memory per GPU, NVLink/NVSwitch (NV18 topology), 2 TiB host RAM, two NUMA nodes.
Baseline: v0.5.21 at
e00930c5489053f26d86b179cee0d087f846acbb
,
TP8/EP8, DSpark block size 5 already enabled
, no CP, no decoder bounded replay, GPU-resident Engram, no HiCache.
Final:
TP8/EP4, CP8 interleave, CP decode-attention TP, DSpark5, decoder SWA bounded replay
, FlashInfer MXFP4 MoE with FP8 precision; Engram host table in
per_rank
layout, NUMA binding, HiCache ratio 1.5 /
write_through
.
Both use a 524,288-token context limit, static memory fraction 0.8, chunk size 8192 and max-running-requests 64. Prefill CUDA graphs remain disabled; decode CUDA graphs are enabled.
Final local integration revision:
79b468a7435e1bd29ad0d377587ff10b3c214ba3
(
not an upstream release/commit
). Runtime: PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, Triton 3.7.1, FlashInfer 0.6.18; the final DeepGEMM integration uses
sgl-deep-gemm 0.2.2
. This is a backported integration, not a claim that stock v0.5.21 supports this configuration.
The baseline and final integration use the same V4.1 model weights on the same hardware. No P/D disaggregation is used. All performance below is from a single eight-GPU server. These results describe the pinned October 5–7 snapshots, not the latest heads of every roadmap PR.
Comparison boundary:
the near-512K and C64 baseline measurements were supplemented using exactly the final workload construction, warmup and three measured rounds. Input hashes, token counts, output lengths and zero-cache-hit conditions match. Other baseline cells are historical references: cold-prefill nonces differ, and the early natural-generation prompts/warmup procedure differ from the final protocol. The tables explicitly mark the paired supplements with †. Runs were sequential, on different dates, not randomized interleaved A/B trials.
2. Optimization path and what we retained
Use vision-compatible CP as the foundation.
We chose
model: DeepSeek V4.1 vision CP and single-owner image encoding
#40219
for its merge-before-shard multimodal preparation and single-owner image encoding. We adapted the owner callback API and fixed physical request-pool row mapping in the Torch prefill indexer. We borrowed the replay-tail idea from
[DSV4.1] DeepSeek-V4.1 support prefill CP
#40161
later, rather than importing its entire P/D integration.
Integrate the Hopper paths and H20 configurations.
This included
[Perf] Optimize DeepSeek V4.1 Flash Hopper paths and Blackwell prefill selection
#41251
,
[DSV4.1] Add H20 block-FP8 tuned configs
#41098
and the relevant
[DSV4.1] Enable Hopper decode optimizations for TP8
#39114
path, plus scorer/Top-K, compression, RoPE, dispatch and preparation changes listed below. We checked actual dispatch and added tables for six further missing matrix shapes encountered in this integration; small tuning differences below 3% retained the default. These additional local tables are distinct from the original six tables in
[DSV4.1] Add tuned H20-3e block-FP8 GEMM configs
#39306
.
Enable Engram host storage and HiCache together, then tune EP.
The
per_rank
layout shards the host Engram table across ranks rather than replicating the entire table eight times. The combined memory configuration increased the engine-reported KV token-pool capacity by about 31.25% relative to our preceding GPU-Engram/HiCache-ratio-2/memory-fraction-0.88 configuration, with essentially unchanged near-512K TTFT. This is a combined memory-layout result, not a standalone offload speedup.
Add decoder bounded replay while preserving image requests and DSpark.
After the last KV-source layer, replay shortens the late-layer token rows. We added tail-aware CP gather, global token indices for logits/DSpark, original CP-owner mapping, and preservation of canonical image IDs. This became
[DSV4.1] Support decoder SWA bounded replay with vision CP and DSpark
#42924
, with
[DSV4.1] Fix Torch prefill indexer request-pool rows under CP
#42922
as a separate row-mapping fix.
Add fused prefill scoring and native SM90 block32 FP8 GEMM.
[DSV4.1] Fuse Hopper prefill indexer scoring into one Triton kernel
#42365
fuses indexer score/ReLU/weighting/head reduction;
[SM90] Use native block32 DeepGEMM for DeepSeek-V4.1
#42604
enables the supported native DeepGEMM linear paths. We retained the existing compact-candidate path and fallbacks. Routed MXFP4 experts still use FlashInfer.

title: [Perf] Optimize DeepSeek V4.1 Flash Hopper paths and Blackwell prefill selection
body:
## Motivation

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on Hopper spends substantial decode time in group32 dense GEMMs, capacity-sized indexer work, mHC statistics, and padded Marlin MoE projections. This PR tunes those paths. On Blackwell, flattened prefill selection also launches separate mask, sort, slot-map and raw-offset operations; the added integer kernel combines them.

## Changes

- Tune Hopper group32 GEMMs and reuse exact BF16 expansions of eligible FP8 weights, preserving activation quantization boundaries and the original fallbacks.
- Use live paged indexer lengths and variable-length top-k; fuse masking, sorting and slot mapping.
- Enable guarded Hopper mHC combine/norm and compensated BF16 projection paths, with decode statistics overlap.
- Preserve intermediate activation rounding in fused clipped SwiGLU; defer MXFP4 padding until Marlin repacking.
- On SM100-family CUDA GPUs, fuse flattened prefill selection into one integer kernel. Keep the changing visible slot count as a non-specialized runtime argument, so new context lengths do not create new JIT variants. Hopper retains its existing Torch selection path.

## Pinned validation

Checkpoint `dba1be0a40aa45a94ad051997016db3960a90277`; PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130 and sgl-kernel 0.4.8; sgl-bench commit `a9da34ad1f997ca05878d858d3d01970e4a49af9`; sgl-eval 0.1.2. Both machines were allocated exclusively for these comparisons. All paired datasets, request counts, input/output lengths and API errors were validated from the request records. Timings exclude profiling and correctness instrumentation.

### H200: upstream main versus original PR runtime

8×H200, TP8/EP1, Marlin MoE, static memory fraction 0.8, bounded SWA replay, decode graph maximum batch64, Engram host table disabled. Main `ef867fa40d` versus PR `22e352d873`; `94d21e3162` differs from the measured PR only by a test mock accessor. Random8192 input /1024 output, seed42, temperature0, thinking disabled,64 warmup requests and cache flush. Request counts30/40/80/80/160/320 at concurrency1/4/8/16/32/64; three alternating paired sweeps. Ratios below are medians of the three paired ratios.

|Concurrency|User-speed ratio|Output-throughput/GPU ratio|TTFT speedup|
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
|1|2.2067×|2.1515×|1.3398×|
|4|2.4842×|2.3498×|1.5062×|
|8|2.3599×|2.2322×|1.5551×|
|16|2.1674×|2.0574×|1.5555×|
|32|2.2540×|2.1077×|1.5658×|
|64|2.3975×|2.1929×|1.5583×|

The final Blackwell addition was checked separately against the original PR on the same H200 node: one complete paired six-point sweep and full GSM8K/AIME24 at4096/32768 output caps. User-speed ratios are0.9990–1.0029 and output-throughput/GPU ratios0.9989–1.0013. This additional check is one paired sweep, not the three-sweep main comparison above. Full GSM8K is1277/1319 on both arms; AIME24 is456/480→457/480, with23 truncations each. Hopper continues to use its Torch fallback; equal aggregate scores do not imply identical generations.

### GB300: added flattened prefill fusion versus ordinary PR

4×NVIDIA GB300/SM103, ARM64, TP4/EP1, flashinfer_mxfp4 MoE and flashinfer_cutedsl FP8 GEMM. Ordinary PR `94d21e3162` versus candidate `179b1ab2d3` (identical tested file hashes). Both arms use16384 for chunked-prefill-size and max-prefill-tokens. Three rotated paired sweeps; seed42, temperature0, thinking disabled,16 warmups and cache flush. Each shape uses64 requests at concurrency1 and128 at concurrency16.

|Input tokens|Output tokens|Concurrency|Median TTFT speedup|Individual paired ratios|
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
|8192|32|1|1.0170×|1.0227×, 1.0170×, 0.9902×|
|8192|32|16|1.0277×|1.0266×, 1.0485×, 1.0277×|
|32768|32|1|1.0209×|1.0209×, 1.0282×, 0.9794×|
|32768|32|16|1.0200×|1.0200×, 1.0239×, 1.0168×|

Both concurrency16 shapes improve in all three pairs. Each concurrency1 shape has one regressing pair, so this is a small prefill improvement, not a claim of universal or statistically proven acceleration. In the8192-input/1024-output suite, median output-throughput/GPU ratios are only1.0009–1.0081. The standalone selection helper improves5.45–14.33×; that microbenchmark is not an end-to-end speedup.

### Accuracy

Full GSM8K1319 problems, thinking disabled; full AIME24 is30 problems×16 repeats, thinking enabled. Seed42, temperature0,32 evaluation threads, no API errors. Repeats are not480 independent questions. Results are paired by question ID, problem text and expected answer.

|Machine|Dataset/output cap|Upstream main|Ordinary PR|Blackwell candidate|
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
|H200|GSM8K/2048|1278/1319|1278/1319|Not rerun at this cap|
|H200|AIME24/16384|440/480|437/480|Not rerun at this cap|
|H200|GSM8K/4096|1276/1319|1274/1319|See fresh paired run below|
|H200|AIME24/32768|451/480|454/480|See fresh paired run below|
|H200, fresh paired run|GSM8K/4096|Not rerun|1277/1319|1277/1319|
|H200, fresh paired run|AIME24/32768|Not rerun|456/480|457/480|
|GB300|GSM8K/2048|1277/1319|1278/1319|1279/1319|
|GB300|AIME24/16384|438/480|437/480|434/480|
|GB300, fresh paired run|GSM8K/4096|Not rerun|1279/1319|1277/1319|
|GB300, fresh paired run|AIME24/32768|Not rerun|456/480|453/480|

GB300 accuracy uses2048 prefill budgets, because upstream main's FlashMLA scheduling metadata exceeds its48KB shared-memory implementation limit on a GSM8K batch at the default16K budget. Performance comparisons use the same16K budget on every arm and are kept separate. AIME24 candidate versus ordinary PR changes by−0.625 percentage points; truncations40→42,14 correct→wrong and11 wrong→correct. There is also one additional wrong nontruncated answer. The higher-cap paired run still has AIME24 −0.625 percentage points (456→453 correct; truncations22→24;7 correct→wrong,4 reverse), and GSM8K −0.1516 percentage points (1279→1277; neither arm truncated). These scores do not prove identical generation or statistical accuracy equivalence.

### Correctness coverage

- Existing H200 focused regression:582 passed,60 skipped,16 subtests passed on the rebased runtime.
- New integer selection/CUDA Graph/cache-reuse cases:34 passed on real GB300 SM100 dispatch, and34 passed on H200 with the SM100 entry mocked to exercise the integer helper.
- Full GB300 indexer test file:133 passed,2 skipped.
- Real-model8K/32K prefill audit at concurrency1/16:1908 calls across four ranks, with both page and raw indices exactly equal to the original Torch operations. Rows1–16384, visible slots1–48900. This is integer-mapping evidence, not a substitute for generation-quality evaluation.
- A second actual-model audit dispatches fusion before any reference GPU work:1908 calls,477 per rank, with exact page/raw index agreement. Padding is separately covered by the unit tests.
- Actual model GPU traces contain40 `_finish_flat_indexer_topk_kernel` events per rank; all four original trace files are retained with source hashes.
- Pinned pre-commit and diff whitespace checks passed. CI is not fully green: the existing AMD raw-draft-metadata test still needs alignment with main's deferred metadata API; no ROCm validation is claimed.

## Memory and weight updates

The Hopper derived caches trade GPU memory for throughput. In the original weight-load measurement, memory increased72.71→75.43GB/GPU and max_total_num_tokens fell16,012,800→14,223,104 at the same static memory fraction. These are the original configuration's measurements, not newly measured final-commit memory numbers.

Online weight updates require disabling both derived caches with `SGLANG_OPT_HOPPER_BLOCK_FP8_BF16=0` and `SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_HC_PRENORM=0`; otherwise updates fail before writing weights. Other TP/EP layouts are not covered by the reported serving comparisons.

title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] deepseek-v4.1: Reuse dequantized compressed KV in PD CP prefill (7/N)
body: issue:https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/39700 base pr: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/40179 ## Summary DeepSeek V4.1 consumer layers can share the same compressed KV storage, but sparse prefill currently dequantizes that storage into a BF16 workspace on every layer. Reuse the dequantized compressed KV within a forward to avoid repeated reads, dequantization, and workspace writes. ## Changes - Limit reuse to CP sparse BF16 prefill with compression ratios 1 and 2. - Keep separate workspaces per compression ratio. - Track validity by source layer and workspace address within the per-forward gather cache. - Refresh on producer execution, source changes, workspace reallocation, or a new forward. - Continue updating SWA and top-k inputs for every layer. This retains additional scratch memory for the separate workspaces. ## Validation - GPU regression tests cover shared sources, source updates, ratio interleaving, consecutive forwards, and workspace resizing. - All 16 short/long-context smoke-test outputs match the baseline. - In a six-step trace, compressed KV dequantization calls decrease from 228 to 24 (89.5% fewer). ### Performance DeepSeek V4.1 Flash on 8×B200 with PD disaggregation; prefill uses TP4/EP4, CP, BCG, MegaMoE, and DSpark. Results are medians of three unprofiled runs using the unchanged benchmark script, with 512 requests and an output length of 500, which is 60k unprefix cache of 64k all input length. ### precision gsm8k test result ## trace comparison before after --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #39416278022](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39416278022) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #39416278250](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39416278250) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 10): :hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #39416278223](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39416278223)

title: [SM120] Field report: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash in production on 8x RTX PRO 6000 (PCIe, no NVLink) - working config, measured throughput, rejected topologies
body:
## Summary

Field data from running **DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash** as a production SGLang backend on **8× RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Max-Q (SM120, 96 GB, PCIe-only — no NVLink)**, including the *only* topology we could get to start, measured prefill/decode, a speculative-decoding A/B, and the configuration traps that cost us real experiments. Posting because SM120 + V4.1-Flash users currently have to rediscover all of this from scratch.

Full write-up (with methodology and reproduction artifacts): https://github.com/Lei-010/hermes-agent/blob/main/docs/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-SM120-Performance-and-Production-Config.md

Related: vLLM field report https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/56700 (same hardware, vLLM side), vLLM https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/56892 (SM120 bug/perf tracker).

## What works

```bash
docker run --gpus all -d --name dsv41 \
  --shm-size=64g --ipc=host --network host \
  --restart unless-stopped \
  -e TP_SIZE=8 -e DP_SIZE=1 -e EP_SIZE=8 \
  -e SPEC_ALGORITHM=dspark -e DSPARK_BLOCK_SIZE=6 \
  -e CHUNKED_PREFILL_SIZE=2048 \
  -v /ssd/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash:/model \
  <sglang image>
```

Effective `server_args` (verified at runtime via `/get_server_info`):

| Parameter | Value |
|---|---|
| `tp_size` / `ep_size` / `dp_size` | 8 / 8 / 1 |
| `speculative_algorithm` | DSPARK, `speculative_dspark_block_size = 6` |
| `chunked_prefill_size` | 2048 |
| `context_length` | 1,048,576 |
| `kv_cache_dtype` | `fp8_e4m3` |
| `mem_fraction_static` | 0.72 |
| `max_running_requests` | 16 |
| `attention_backend` / `moe_runner_backend` | `dsv4` / `flashinfer_mxfp4` |
| CUDA graph decode / prefill | full (max_bs 16) / **disabled** |

**TP8/EP8 is not a preference — it is the only layout that starts** (see "Topologies SGLang rejects" below).

## Measured throughput (cold, single stream, tokens from `usage`, not SSE chunk counts)

128K cold prefill:

| Config | tok/s |
|---|---|
| `chunked_prefill_size=2048` (production) | **6,853** |
| same config re-run | 6,765 (−1.3%) |
| flashmla prefill backend | 6,845 |
| fused-MoE all-reduce | 6,828 |
| `chunked_prefill_size=4096` | 6,301 |
| `chunked_prefill_size=1024` | 6,012 |

32K prompt: ≈7,196 tok/s. GPU util ≈87% at 220 W of 600 W → **communication-bound on PCIe**, not compute-bound. ~7K tok/s looks like the ceiling for this board without NVLink.

Radix/prefix cache is the only large multiplier: cache-hit prefill **0.34 s for a 112K-token prefix ≈ 325K tok/s (≈39×)**.

Decode (client path over SSH tunnel, production config): prose 93.9 tok/s, structured/JSON 134.1 tok/s, TTFT 143–169 ms.

## DSPARK A/B (block_size=2, clean legs, each verified via `server_info` + acceptance length)

| Prompt class | DSPARK ON | DSPARK OFF |
|---|---|---|
| prose | 76.5–78.9 tok/s | 36.4–36.5 tok/s |
| structured | 120.3–120.5 tok/s | 36.5 tok/s |
| `accept len` | 3.0 tokens/step | 1.0 |

With DSPARK off the model flattens to ~36.5 tok/s regardless of prompt class — speculation is the difference between usable and unusable latency on this hardware. Production ships `block_size=6` (structured ≈237–252 tok/s vs 120 at block 2).

## Traps that cost us experiments (SGLang-specific)

1. **`--enable-expert-parallel` is a vLLM flag** — SGLang takes `ep_size`; the vLLM spelling is rejected outright.
2. **`docker run` must pass `TP_SIZE`/`DP_SIZE`/`EP_SIZE` explicitly.** Without `-e`, the container silently serves TP8 defaults and your "new" config never happens (we recorded a full sweep of false data this way before adding a config gate).
3. **`ep_size ≤ tp_size`** or the MoE rank computation divides by zero: `moe_ep_rank = tp_rank % (tp_size // moe_dp_size) // (tp_size // moe_dp_size // ep_size)`.
4. **DSPARK + DP attention requires `--enable-dp-lm-head`** — but is unreachable on this model anyway (next section).

## Topologies SGLang rejects on this model

| Attempt | Result |
|---|---|
| DP2 × TP4 (any EP) | `ValueError: V4.1 vision currently supports TP/EP without DP, CP, PP or MoE A2A` — both replicas die within ~70 s |
| prefill context-parallel | same class of rejection |
| `--enable-dp-attention` alone | silently no DP group (`dp_size: 1`) — looks fine, isn't |

Other SM120 gaps we hit: MSCCL++ (`_tune` kernel crash), FlashInfer all-reduce fusion, `flashmla_sparse_q8`, and CUDA-graph capture for **prefill** (crashes even with DSPARK off, i.e. unrelated to speculation).

## Operational notes

- A defunct container can survive a single `docker rm -f`; the next `docker run` then fails on the name conflict while an orphaned engine process keeps the port and answers health checks — which silently mislabels the next experiment. Loop `docker rm -f` until the container is gone **and** nothing listens on the port.
- A parse failure must never satisfy an "expected config" assertion, or a server that has not started yet gets recorded as "spec disabled".
- Verify intended config from the server (`/get_server_info`) before timing anything; discard legs that fail the gate rather than recording them.

## Not established

No 24 h soak (numbers come from a working day of production use), block sizes 4/8/12 not re-measured with the fixed sweep tool, and >32K prefill/long-context degradation not characterised.

title: [Feat] dsv4: Support deterministic inference for DeepSeek-V4
body:
## Motivation

Closes #36174.

`--enable-deterministic-inference` rejects DeepSeek-V4 at startup, and because the
model's config-time overrides pin `--attention-backend dsv4`, there is no backend to
fall back to — the flag is unusable on V4 in every configuration:

```
ValueError: Currently only ['ascend', 'fa3', 'fa4', 'flashinfer', 'intel_xpu', 'triton']
attention backends are supported for deterministic inference, but you explicitly
specified 'dsv4'.
```

Allowlisting the backend alone is not enough: with it allowlisted but nothing else
changed, DeepSeek-V4-Flash-FP8 still produces 3 distinct outputs over 20 batch sizes.
The V4 path has four separate dispatches that key off the token count.

## Modifications

Each site below picks a kernel, a tile size, or a split-K count from the number of
tokens in the batch, which is exactly what deterministic inference must not do.

1. **mHC pre-norm split-K** — `_compute_num_split_for_mhc_pre` derives `n_splits`
   from `n_sms // ceil(num_tokens / 64)`, and `n_splits` is the number of partial
   sums the K reduction is folded from, so it fixes the summation order. This is the
   first op of every layer, so a prompt prefilled alongside two others differs from
   the same prompt prefilled alone in *every* token's logprob by ~1e-2. Pinned to the
   token-independent `num_block_k // 4`. `mhc_fused_post_pre` carries the same term
   plus a `num_tokens <= 32` FMA-kernel switch, and
   `_flashinfer_mhc_pre_num_splits` is a third copy.
2. **FlashMLA sparse decode tile scheduler** — `sparse_attn_decode_interface`
   computes `payload = ceil(total_num_blocks / num_sm_parts)` over the whole batch,
   so where a request's KV range is cut depends on its co-batched requests.
   Deterministic mode issues one launch per request, which makes the schedule a
   function of that request alone.
3. **Non-paged indexer** — taken only when `batch_size == 1 and query_rows >= 8192`.
4. **Router GEMM** — `MoEGate` switches to `dsv3_router_gemm` at
   `hidden_states.shape[0] <= 16`, and `linear_bf16_fp32`'s HPC-Ops path at `M >= 8`.
   Fixing the first also fixes a startup crash: the deterministic branch of `MoEGate`
   returned bf16 router logits, and V4's fused `hash_topk` kernel requires fp32
   (`Dtype value [bfloat16] not in the allowed options: [float32]`).

Also probed and ruled out on H200, so left alone: the DeepGEMM fp8 block GEMM is
M-invariant at every V4 shape, `flash_mla_sparse_fwd` (prefill) is s_q-invariant,
and the MoE runner choice makes no difference.

Deterministic inference on `dsv4` is rejected on SM120, whose attention kernel is an
autotuned Triton kernel that picks its tile size — and with it the softmax rescaling
order — from measured timings.

Everything above is gated: with the flag off, the only changes are an extracted
`_use_sparse_prefill` predicate, two algebraically identical `max_splits` locals and
a `use_fma` local. Verified below.

## Accuracy Tests

DeepSeek-V4-Flash-FP8, 4xH200, TP=4.

**The feature.** Distinct outputs over 32 batch sizes,
`sglang.test.test_deterministic --test-mode single`:

| | distinct outputs / 32 |
| --- | --- |
| without the flag | 6 |
| with `--enable-deterministic-inference` | **1** |

All three harness modes pass with radix cache and CUDA graphs on: `single` (n=32),
`prefix` + logprobs (temperature 0.5, shared prefixes of 1 / 511 / 2048 / 4097), and
`radix_cache`. Chunked prefill was checked separately at
`--chunked-prefill-size 512` over 4097-token prompts.

**No regression with the flag off.** Same box, arms run back to back, benchmark client always from `main` so only the
server tree varies.

The strongest check pins the batch at one request, which removes batch-composition
noise entirely: 150 GSM8K completions issued serially are **150/150 byte-identical**
between `main` and this branch, as are 8/8 fixed greedy prompts.

GSM8K, 400 questions, 5-shot, greedy, `--parallel 64`:

| tree | runs |
| --- | --- |
| `main` | 0.965, 0.965, 0.968, 0.968, 0.968 |
| this branch | 0.960, 0.963, 0.970, 0.960 |

Repeats within one warm server span 0.960-0.970 on this branch, bracketing every
`main` number; at 400 questions the harness cannot resolve better than about +/-4
questions. That spread is DeepSeek-V4's own batch-composition non-determinism -- the
thing the new flag removes.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

**With the flag off** — `sglang.benchmark.serving`, random 1024/512, 200 prompts,
concurrency 32: 

| order | tree | output tok/s | total tok/s | mean TPOT |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1st | `main` | 1849.80 | 5549.39 | 14.01 ms |
| 2nd | this branch | 1919.93 | 5759.80 | 13.99 ms |
| 3rd | `main` | 1919.67 | 5759.01 | 13.99 ms |

This branch lands within 0.01% of the warm `main` run. The first run is the cold
outlier (JIT and autotune caches), and that cold-start effect (+3.8%) is far larger
than anything between the trees. `MHC prenorm prewarm: 21 n_splits buckets` is logged
by both trees with the flag off, i.e. the split-K schedule is untouched there.

**With the flag on**, decode throughput (fixed batch, 128 output tokens, best of 3):

| | bs=1 | bs=16 | bs=32 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| no flag | 131 | 1611 | 3045 tok/s |
| deterministic | 50 | 354 | 444 tok/s |

Deterministic inference costs ~2.1-2.5x on its own (batch-invariant matmul/rmsnorm,
pytorch sampling, NCCL tree with pinned channels, pinned MoE and mHC split-K), flat
in batch size. The per-request FlashMLA launch adds a further 2.3x at bs=16 and 3.2x
at bs=32, and is free at bs=1. It is not optional: an ablation that keeps the single
batched launch and everything else is still non-deterministic (2 distinct outputs
over 32 batch sizes).

That ablation is also the opening for a follow-up. `sparse_decode_fwd` accepts
`tile_scheduler_metadata` and `num_splits` as inputs and only computes them when
absent, so a supplied no-split schedule would recover the single launch. This PR
takes the loop instead: it is 15 lines, obviously correct, and carries no coupling to
a pinned third-party struct layout — and its bit-exact output is the oracle a
schedule builder would be validated against.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

title: github:vllm-project/FlashMLA:26 fetched implementation patch
Knowledge Grafting of Large Language Models
body:
Cross-capability transfer is a key challenge in large language model (LLM)
research, with applications in multi-task integration, model compression, and
continual learning. Recent works like FuseLLM and FuseChat have demonstrated
the potential of transferring multiple model capabilities to lightweight
models, enhancing adaptability and efficiency, which motivates our
investigation into more efficient cross-capability transfer methods. However,
existing approaches primarily focus on small, homogeneous models, limiting
their applicability. For large, heterogeneous models, knowledge distillation
with full-parameter fine-tuning often overlooks the student model's intrinsic
capacity and risks catastrophic forgetting, while PEFT methods struggle to
effectively absorb knowledge from source LLMs. To address these issues, we
introduce GraftLLM, a novel method that stores source model capabilities in a
target model with SkillPack format. This approach preserves general
capabilities, reduces parameter conflicts, and supports forget-free continual
learning and model fusion. We employ a module-aware adaptive compression
strategy to compress parameter updates, ensuring efficient storage while
maintaining task-specific knowledge. The resulting SkillPack serves as a
compact and transferable knowledge carrier, ideal for heterogeneous model
fusion and continual learning. Experiments across various scenarios demonstrate
that GraftLLM outperforms existing techniques in knowledge transfer, knowledge
fusion, and forget-free learning, providing a scalable and efficient solution
for cross-capability transfer. The code is publicly available at:
https://github.com/duguodong7/GraftLLM.

title: Kamera: Unified Position-Invariant Multimodal KV Cache for Training-Free Reuse
body: Multimodal agents repeatedly re-examine the same video frames, UI screenshots, and rendered artifacts as their context window slides and reasoning iterates, yet every look-back re-encodes from scratch, because prefix caches serve reuse only at a fixed leading position. We show this recompute is avoidable, and identify exactly what naive KV reuse loses: the cross-chunk conditioning a chunk absorbs from its neighbours. This loss is asymmetric. The direct readout of a cached chunk is recovered exactly and for free by the standard state-merge. What remains is a diffuse, low-rank residue concentrated in deep layers, invisible to single-hop retrieval but precisely what multi-hop reasoning binds on. Blind reuse therefore leaves single-hop recall intact while halving multi-hop accuracy; this is the failure mode prior position-independent caches, designed for single-context or single-image reuse, do not address. We repair it with a small, training-free low-rank conditioning patch stored alongside each position-free chunk. Reuse reduces to one operator across MLA, GQA, and MHA: exact RoPE re-rotation to any target position, plus the patch that restores cross-chunk binding. This makes three window operations cheap: reorder (one patch serves every ordering of a cached set), sliding-window survival (surviving chunks relocate via rotation only, zero re-encode), and recall (an evicted chunk is rehydrated by its patch, never re-encoded). A rank-m patch recovers full task accuracy on cross-chunk-binding benchmarks, MM-NIAH across two attention families and two-page doc-QA, at a fraction of the KV footprint, and reconstructs re-prefill KV to within bf16 rounding in a production SGLang kernel across six backbones. The conditioning signal is strongest in redundant vision and video streams, making our solution most impactful where multimodal agents spend their recompute budget.

title:
Mutual Enhancement of Large and Small Language Models with Cross-Silo
  Knowledge Transfer
body:
While large language models (LLMs) are empowered with broad knowledge, their
task-specific performance is often suboptimal. It necessitates fine-tuning LLMs
with task-specific data, but such data may be inaccessible due to privacy
concerns. In this paper, we propose a novel approach to enhance LLMs with
smaller language models (SLMs) that are trained on clients using their private
task-specific data. To enable mutual enhancement between LLMs and SLMs, we
propose CrossLM, where the SLMs promote the LLM to generate task-specific
high-quality data, and both the LLM and SLMs are enhanced with the generated
data. We evaluate CrossLM using publicly accessible language models across a
range of benchmark tasks. The results demonstrate that CrossLM significantly
enhances the task-specific performance of SLMs on clients and the LLM on the
cloud server simultaneously while preserving the LLM's generalization
capability.

title: [AMD][MI355X] DSv4.1-Flash vLLM: enable sparse-MLA Gluon kernel / DSv4.1-Flash vLLM：启用 sparse-MLA Gluon kernel
body:
## Description

Add `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_TRITON_SPARSE_MLA=True` to
`dsv41flash-fp4-mi355x-vllm-agentic-dspark` to force
[vllm-project/vllm#53492](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53492)'s
Gluon sparse-MLA kernel path (matches what was actually set in the local
validation runs referenced below).

Unpins `image`/`model.container` to `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-TBD`
(only the trailing hash needs updating later): the current pin predates this
recipe's cherry-picked AMD vLLM PRs and is unrelated to them. A maintainer
should fill in the hash once these land upstream and are released in a
nightly image:

- [vllm-project/vllm#58208](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58208) — faster DSA candidate block-selection topk
- [vllm-project/vllm#58655](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58655) — fused mHC Triton kernel for the delayed seams
- [vllm-project/vllm#53492](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53492) — sparse MLA Gluon kernel from Aiter (this PR's env var)

Together these bring better topk/mHC/MLA kernels with better
compute/communication stream overlap for DSv4.1-Flash on MI355X.

This PR previously also added `--attention-config
'{"indexer_kv_dtype":"mxfp4","indexer_sparse_logits":true}'` and a
`--block-size 128` workaround to exercise
[vllm-project/vllm#58671](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58671)'s
ROCm paged MXFP4 sparse-logits indexer kernel. Both are dropped: #58671 isn't
merging in time, and the `--block-size 128` pin's entire justification (vLLM's
block-size auto-resolution otherwise picking 64 across this model's 4+
attention backends) was specifically about the 128 that
`DeepseekV4ROCMAiterMLASparseBackend.get_preferred_block_size` requests once
the fp4 indexer is active — moot without it. A live A/B test (TP2, conc=16,
matched 900s profiling window, `#58208` reverted upstream via
[vllm-project/vllm#59125](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59125) so
the dense fallback path doesn't crash) measured the dense fp8 indexer path
that `#58671` would otherwise replace: interactivity p50/p90 -14.7%/-14.9%,
e2e latency p50/p90 +9.5%/+10.8% worse, throughput/GPU unchanged (+0.5%,
within noise), TTFT unchanged. So `#58671` is a meaningful interactivity/tail-
latency win, not just a config toggle, but it's still not ready to merge, so
this recipe leaves it out for now.

This PR does not touch `--max-num-batched-tokens`: the existing TP2 c64 (8192)
/ c128 (4096) values in this recipe already avoid the KV-headroom regression
that a separate, since-closed draft (#3451) flagged as unvalidated.

Duplicate-check: searched open PRs for `dsv41flash mi355x`, `attention-config`,
`indexer_kv_dtype`, `mxfp4 indexer`, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_TRITON_SPARSE_MLA`
and `block-size 128` on this repo; no open PR adds this env var or touches
this recipe's image pin.

title: feat(matrix): budget decode GPUs for P/D-shared DRAM offload pools / feat(matrix): 为 P/D 共享的 DRAM 卸载池计入解码 GPU 预算
body:
Disaggregated AgentX entries budget `total-cpu-dram-gb` from one prefill replica's GPUs on its node, so DRAM beside the decode workers is never counted, even when the KV offload pool lives there. This PR adds an opt-in `dram-budget-scope: all-workers` for a pool shared by prefill and decode. Every prefill and decode GPU claims its node share, the same GPUs that normalize per-GPU throughput. The default stays `prefill`, and no config, recipe or benchmark point changes here. Closes #4103.

### What changes

- `AgenticCodingConfig` gains `dram-budget-scope: prefill | all-workers`, default `prefill`. `all-workers` requires `prefill` and `decode` workers and rejects per-worker `hardware`, because the budget reads one runner's node DRAM.
- Under `all-workers`, `agentic_dram_offload_gb` counts `num-worker × tp × pp × pcp-size × dwdp-size` for both roles, with the same node-tiling rules as today. The per-GPU share is unchanged: capped node DRAM × `dram-utilization` / `gpus-per-node`.
- `configs/CONFIGS.md` documents `dram-utilization` and the new field. The total may span the deployment's nodes, but each node holds at most the share of the deployment's GPUs on it, so idle GPUs claim nothing. The budget caps what a recipe may use; nodes still need DRAM for hugepage reservations, page cache and processes.

| 8-GPU nodes, `dram-utilization: 1.0` | GPUs | `prefill` (default) | `all-workers` |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1P1D: 4-GPU prefill + 4-GPU decode | 8 | 1,499 GB | 2,999 GB |
| 1P2D | 12 | 1,499 GB | 4,499 GB |
| 1P3D | 16 | 1,499 GB | 5,999 GB |

### Our design: P/D with a Mooncake Store over RDMA

Our GLM-5.2 MI355X points (#4045) run ATOM with a Mooncake Store as prefill's second-tier prefix cache, implemented in [ROCm/ATOM#2464](https://github.com/ROCm/ATOM/pull/2464).

- **Roles.** Prefill is one ATOM worker with PP4 × TP1: four pipeline stages, one per GPU, and each GPU uses its own RDMA NIC. Decode is one ATOM worker with TP4 and DCP4. atomesh routes requests.
- **Cache tiers.** Prefill keeps a paged KV prefix cache in HBM (L1). The Mooncake Store (L2) is a DRAM pool: masters hold object metadata, leases and LRU eviction, and owner processes pin hugepage DRAM and register it with an RDMA NIC. Owners lend memory, not compute; the NICs move the bytes.
- **KV moves over RDMA**, numbered as in the diagram below:
  1. **Lookup.** On admission, the prefill scheduler asks the masters over TCP which 256-token chunks every PP stage holds. The hit is the shortest prefix all stages hold. Only metadata moves.
  2. **Put.** As prefill computes, each stage packs its new chunks in place into a Store-registered slot pool in HBM. Its NIC writes them into an owner's DRAM (`batch_put_from`, GPUDirect RDMA).
  3. **Get.** On a hit, the NIC reads the chunks from whichever node's owner holds them straight into the slot pool (`batch_get_into`). The stage unpacks them into the paged KV instead of recomputing them.
  4. **P/D.** Finished KV reaches the decode GPUs over the mooncake P/D connector, also by RDMA. The decode path never reads the Store.
  5. **Decode-side DRAM.** Owners also run beside decode, on the decode node or on the decode half of a shared node, and mount on the same masters. Their DRAM joins the pool that prefill reads and writes over RDMA, at no cost to the decode GPUs. In ATOM's two-node test they held 836 of their 960 GiB at the end of a c96 run.
- **Rails.** A stage on `rdmaN` uses pool N, whose owners on every node use `rdmaN`. This fits rail-isolated fabrics such as `mi355x-amds`.

At AgentX c112, this pool's capacity sets throughput. Conversations that idle for the trace's 300 s cap return just as a 1,499 GB Store evicts them, and prefill must recompute their prefixes. #4103 has the measurements.

### Design diagram

From ROCm/ATOM#2464. It shows a two-node cell; in a single-node 1P1D, the node's two NUMA halves play node A and node B.

![mooncake_store: one Mooncake Store pool shared across nodes and P/D instances](https://github.com/ROCm/ATOM/blob/61ac476f998d818a2a1f27fc0bd1475d401a90ca/pr2464/mooncake_store_architecture.svg?raw=true)

<details>
<summary>中文</summary>

分离式 AgentX 条目目前只按一个预填充副本在其节点上占用的 GPU 计算 `total-cpu-dram-gb`，因此即使 KV 卸载池就部署在解码 worker 旁边，那部分内存也永远不会计入预算。本 PR 为预填充和解码共享的内存池新增一个需显式开启的 `dram-budget-scope: all-workers`：每张预填充和解码 GPU 都按其节点份额计入，与每 GPU 吞吐量归一化所用的 GPU 一致。默认值仍为 `prefill`，本 PR 不改动任何配置、配方或基准测试点。Closes #4103。

### 改动内容

- `AgenticCodingConfig` 新增 `dram-budget-scope: prefill | all-workers`，默认 `prefill`。`all-workers` 要求条目同时有 `prefill` 和 `decode` worker，并且不支持按 worker 指定 `hardware`，因为预算只读取一个 runner 的节点内存。
- 在 `all-workers` 下，`agentic_dram_offload_gb` 对两个角色都按 `num-worker × tp × pp × pcp-size × dwdp-size` 计数，节点切分规则与现在相同。每 GPU 的份额不变：封顶后的节点内存 × `dram-utilization` / `gpus-per-node`。
- `configs/CONFIGS.md` 补充了 `dram-utilization` 和新字段的说明。总预算可以跨越部署所用的多个节点，但每个节点最多只能承载该节点上属于本部署的 GPU 的份额，空闲 GPU 不计入。预算只限制配方最多能用多少；节点仍需为 hugepage 预留、page cache 和各进程留出内存。

| 8 卡节点，`dram-utilization: 1.0` | GPU 数 | `prefill`（默认） | `all-workers` |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1P1D：4 卡预填充 + 4 卡解码 | 8 | 1,499 GB | 2,999 GB |
| 1P2D | 12 | 1,499 GB | 4,499 GB |
| 1P3D | 16 | 1,499 GB | 5,999 GB |

### 我们的方案：基于 RDMA 的 Mooncake Store 分离式推理

我们的 GLM-5.2 MI355X 测试点（#4045）使用 ATOM，并以 Mooncake Store 作为预填充的第二级前缀缓存，实现见 [ROCm/ATOM#2464](https://github.com/ROCm/ATOM/pull/2464)。

- **角色。** 预填充是一个 PP4 × TP1 的 ATOM worker：四个流水线 stage，每个 stage 一张 GPU，每张 GPU 使用自己的 RDMA 网卡。解码是一个 TP4 + DCP4 的 ATOM worker。请求由 atomesh 路由。
- **缓存层级。** 预填充在 HBM 中保留分页 KV 前缀缓存（L1）。Mooncake Store（L2）是一个内存池：master 管理对象元数据、lease 和 LRU 淘汰；owner 进程锁定 hugepage 内存并注册到 RDMA 网卡上。owner 只出借内存、不参与计算，数据由网卡直接搬运。
- **KV 全程通过 RDMA 传输**，编号与下方示意图一致：
  1. **查询（lookup）。** 请求准入时，预填充调度器通过 TCP 向 master 查询每个 PP stage 持有哪些 256 token 的 chunk，命中长度取所有 stage 共同持有的最短前缀。只传元数据。
  2. **写入（put）。** 预填充计算过程中，每个 stage 把新算出的 chunk 原地打包到 HBM 里一个已注册到 Store 的 slot 池中，再由网卡写入 owner 的内存（`batch_put_from`，GPUDirect RDMA）。
  3. **读取（get）。** 命中时，网卡从持有这些 chunk 的任意节点的 owner 直接读入 slot 池（`batch_get_into`），stage 再把它们解包到分页 KV 中，不再重算。
  4. **P/D。** 算完的 KV 通过 mooncake P/D 连接器送到解码 GPU，同样走 RDMA。解码路径从不读取 Store。
  5. **解码侧内存。** owner 也部署在解码旁边：解码节点上，或同一节点的解码那一半，并挂载到同一组 master 上。它们的内存加入预填充通过 RDMA 读写的同一个池，不占用解码 GPU。在 ATOM 的双节点测试中，c96 运行结束时它们占用了 960 GiB 中的 836 GiB。
- **Rail。** 使用 `rdmaN` 的 stage 只访问第 N 个池，该池在每个节点上的 owner 都使用 `rdmaN`，因此适用于 `mi355x-amds` 这类按 rail 隔离的网络。

在 AgentX 并发 112 下，这个池的容量决定了吞吐量：在 trace 300 s 空闲上限后回来的会话，正好赶上 1,499 GB 的 Store 把它们淘汰，预填充只能重算它们的前缀。具体数据见 #4103。

### 设计示意图

示意图见上方，来自 ROCm/ATOM#2464。图中是双节点部署；在单节点 1P1D 中，节点的两个 NUMA 分别对应图中的 node A 和 node B。

</details>

<details>
<summary>AI model disclosure</summary>

- Claude Opus 5.5 (`claude-opus-5-5`), in Claude Code: analyzed the GLM-5.2 c112 runs, wrote the code, tests and docs, and drafted this description and #4103. No delegated agents.
- The architecture diagram is reused from ROCm/ATOM#2464.

</details>

* config(dsv41flash): disable SWA bounded replay on MI355X

Every TP=2 and TP=4 point of run 35567570539 died with
HSA_STATUS_ERROR_MEMORY_FAULT, taking the worker and then the engine core
down and aborting AgentX warmup. The fault follows the first launch of
_pad_replayed_slots_kernel in all 16 server logs, which is the first
prefix hit carrying a replay start.
vllm-project/vllm#56227
added SWA bounded replay, default on, after the
eed1f3d0 pin and before nightly-rocm100-3df4ae153. It pads the replayed
tokens' slots in the prefix-cacheable groups, but the window clamp it
relies on landed in the FlashInfer and FlashMLA kernels; the ROCm sparse
SWA path only gained the replay_start kwarg, and consumes it on the
decode path while the fault is in prefill. Pass --no-swa-bounded-replay
until ROCm clamps too. Prefix caching itself stays on.

运行 35567570539 的所有 TP=2 与 TP=4 数据点都以
HSA_STATUS_ERROR_MEMORY_FAULT 崩溃，先后带崩 worker 与 engine core，
并中止 AgentX warmup。16 份 server 日志中，该故障均紧随
_pad_replayed_slots_kernel 的首次启动，即首个带 replay start 的前缀命中。
vllm-project/vllm#56227
在 eed1f3d0 与 nightly-rocm100-3df4ae153 之间
引入了默认开启的 SWA bounded replay。它会填充被重放 token 在可前缀缓存
分组中的 slot，但其依赖的窗口钳制只落在 FlashInfer 与 FlashMLA 内核中；
ROCm 稀疏 SWA 路径仅新增了 replay_start 参数，且只在 decode 路径消费它，
而故障发生在 prefill。在 ROCm 同样实现钳制之前传入
--no-swa-bounded-replay。前缀缓存本身保持开启。

* config(dsv41flash): change the MI355X memory split only where KV ran short

The previous commit applied one memory split per TP across every
concurrency. Concurrency 1-32 never ran short of KV, so it paid for
changes it did not need: offloaded Engram lookups go to pinned host
memory over UVA, and a smaller prefill chunk costs TTFT. Scope each
change to the points that were actually starved, which also leaves
concurrency 1-32 and TP=4 c64 byte-identical to the settings run
35574132719 already measured on this image and flag set, so those
points are combined with this sweep rather than re-run.

Dividing measured KV tokens by concurrency gives the per-request budget
and separates the failures cleanly. Every point that held had 232K or
more; TP=2 c64 collapsed at 122K.

  TP=4 c1-c64   resident, 16384   14.83M tokens   232K and up
  TP=4 c128     offload,   8192   49.63M           388K
  TP=2 c1-c32   offload,  16384    7.84M           245K and up
  TP=2 c64      offload,   8192   24.68M           386K
  TP=2 c128     offload,   4096   33.34M           260K

Probing the configurations directly also turned up two things. TP=2 c128
at 4096 with the API-server default of 1024 sequences faults during
profiling with HSA_STATUS_ERROR_EXCEPTION at M=1024, N=129280, K=256,
reproduced on two GPU pairs: DSpark verifies 1+5 tokens per sequence, so
a decode batch of max_num_seqs needs six times that many token slots and
4096 leaves four. Cap max_num_seqs at the graph-capture shape wherever
the chunk falls below that bound, which is TP=2 c128 alone. And the
reason c128 never completed before is that at 16384 with capture at
2048, TP=2 c128 held 7.72 GiB, 3.02M tokens, 23.6K per request.

Six changes to the MiniMax-M3 MXFP4 ATOM agentic recipe, all measured on
8xMI355X against the same cc-traces replay:

- gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 -> 0.95.

The per-CONC case set MAX_NUM_SEQS, MAX_NUM_BATCHED_TOKENS and GPU_MEM_UTIL in

attention with no SSM layers, so the value never reached anything.

variable.

* refactor(minimaxm3-atom): one table per concurrency, and drop the tier M3 cannot use

The hybrid offload tier is unreachable for this model. ATOM's M3 connector is
PAGE-only -- the docstring says MiniMax-M3 has no recurrent state and no SLOT
sidecar, and it raises if slot_regions is non-empty -- so OFFLOAD_STATE and the
staging knobs behind STATE_OFFLOAD_CPU_GIB never applied. Its LMCACHE_CHUNK_SIZE
is justified by "block-size(128) x dcp(8)", but this model's search space sets
no dcp-size at all. Removed, along with the comment claiming M3 carries a
per-request recurrent state. An unlisted concurrency now fails instead of
silently taking a tier that does not fit.

CONC=56 is removed for the same reason: nothing in the matrix runs it here (the
56 in this file's neighbourhood belongs to Kimi K3, which has its own script),
and it was the only band that disabled the draft model. With it gone
NUM_SPEC_TOKENS is constant, so the guard around SPEC_ARGS goes too.

The remaining per-concurrency facts now live in one table. Previously the CP
gate was a numeric comparison and the offload tier an enumeration, so adding a
concurrency above 24 would silently enable indexer CP on a point nobody
measured, while forgetting the tier failed loudly. Both are declared per band
now: the loud failure is kept, the silent one becomes a missing speedup.

Verified the same way as the previous cleanup: all 19 matrix points replayed
through a stubbed benchmark_lib, server argv and every exported env var
byte-identical.

* perf(minimaxm3-atom): extend indexer CP down to CONC=15 on TP4

The gate was CONC > 24, chosen from a kernel microbenchmark over uniform
contexts. Three same-commit A/B pairs (1800 s per arm, TP4 + EAGLE3) put the
real crossover below 15:

  CONC 15   interactivity p90 +3.7%    ISL-normalised throughput +0.67%
  CONC 24                    +12.3%                              +0.24%
  CONC 28                    +16.7%                              +2.7%

Monotone and never negative. Throughput is neutral everywhere (only CONC=28
clears the 0.6% noise floor) while interactivity rises with the running batch,
which is what CP actually shortens. Prefix hit rates are identical within each
pair (96.7/96.7, 97.5/97.5, 97.2/97.3), so the gain is not a caching artifact.

CONC=20 is interpolated between the two measured points, not run on its own.
Nothing below 15 is measured and the microbenchmark is negative at batch ~2,
so the band stops there.

CONC=20 appears in both search-space rows, so it is split out of the offload
enumeration: TP4 gets CP without a tier, and the tp_size == 4 gate keeps CP off
the TP2 offload curve. 25 and 30 are TP2-only and stay without a CP
declaration, which would never take effect but would misreport the point.

Verified with the 19-point argv+env replay: the only difference against the
previous revision is ATOM_M3_INDEXER_CP="1" on tp4_c15, tp4_c20 and tp4_c24.

_pad_replayed_slots_kernel in all 16 server logs, which is the first
prefix hit carrying a replay start.

vllm-project/vllm#56227 added SWA bounded replay, default on, after the
eed1f3d0 pin and before nightly-rocm100-3df4ae153. It pads the replayed
tokens' slots in the prefix-cacheable groups, but the window clamp it
relies on landed in the FlashInfer and FlashMLA kernels; the ROCm sparse
SWA path only gained the replay_start kwarg, and consumes it on the
decode path while the fault is in prefill. Pass --no-swa-bounded-replay
until ROCm clamps too. Prefix caching itself stays on.

运行 35567570539 的所有 TP=2 与 TP=4 数据点都以
HSA_STATUS_ERROR_MEMORY_FAULT 崩溃，先后带崩 worker 与 engine core，
并中止 AgentX warmup。16 份 server 日志中，该故障均紧随
_pad_replayed_slots_kernel 的首次启动，即首个带 replay start 的前缀命中。

vllm-project/vllm#56227 在 eed1f3d0 与 nightly-rocm100-3df4ae153 之间
引入了默认开启的 SWA bounded replay。它会填充被重放 token 在可前缀缓存
分组中的 slot，但其依赖的窗口钳制只落在 FlashInfer 与 FlashMLA 内核中；
ROCm 稀疏 SWA 路径仅新增了 replay_start 参数，且只在 decode 路径消费它，
而故障发生在 prefill。在 ROCm 同样实现钳制之前传入
--no-swa-bounded-replay。前缀缓存本身保持开启。

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

* config(dsv41flash): fix the MI355X KV split at high concurrency

Concurrency 64 collapsed on both arms of run 35574132719 because the KV
pool was too small to hold the AgentX working set. TP=2 fell to a 17.6%
prefix cache hit rate, 187 s TTFT and 150 tok/s, against 94.8%, 1.3 s and
957 tok/s at c32.

Two settings were spending device memory that the KV pool needed.

The Engram tables stayed resident at TP=4. vllm-project/vllm#57491
widened the two ROCm is_cuda() gates to is_cuda_alike(), so gfx950 can
now offload them to pinned host memory as every NVIDIA arm has since
 #2963. Measured here at TP=4 with 16384 batched tokens, resident tables
leave 37.96 GiB of KV cache and 14.15x maximum concurrency at 1M
context, against 84.54 GiB and 31.52x offloaded.

The sparse-attention indexer and its companion per-rank buffers scale at
roughly 4.4 MiB per batched token, so the upstream 16384 was the larger
cost. Size it per TP instead, 4096 at TP=2 and 8192 at TP=4, and cap
max_num_seqs at the shape graph capture already covers rather than the
MI355X API-server default of 1024. TP=2 then keeps 79.34 GiB (39.44x)
and TP=4 keeps 121.03 GiB (54.15x), against the B300 arm's 132.48 GiB
(60.17x). B300 runs 8192 at TP=4 and the Blackwell TP=2 arms run 4096
(#3320, #3321).

Sweep concurrency 64 and 128 to confirm the high end first. Concurrency
1-32 is backfilled once those land, since every point now runs the new
memory split.

Co-authored-by: Cursor Agent <cursoragent@cursor.com>
Signed-off-by: Fangzhou Ai <fangzhou.ai@amd.com>

* config(dsv41flash): change the MI355X memory split only where KV ran short

The previous commit applied one memory split per TP across every
concurrency. Concurrency 1-32 never ran short of KV, so it paid for
changes it did not need: offloaded Engram lookups go to pinned host
memory over UVA, and a smaller prefill chunk costs TTFT. Scope each
change to the points that were actually starved, which also leaves
concurrency 1-32 and TP=4 c64 byte-identical to the settings run
35574132719 already measured on this image and flag set, so those
points are combined with this sweep rather than re-run.

Dividing measured KV tokens by concurrency gives the per-request budget
and separates the failures cleanly. Every point that held had 232K or
more; TP=2 c64 collapsed at 122K.

  TP=4 c1-c64   resident, 16384   14.83M tokens   232K and up
  TP=4 c128     offload,   8192   49.63M           388K
  TP=2 c1-c32   offload,  16384    7.84M           245K and up
  TP=2 c64      offload,   8192   24.68M           386K
  TP=2 c128     offload,   4096   33.34M           260K

Probing the configurations directly also turned up two things. TP=2 c128
at 4096 with the API-server default of 1024 sequences faults during
profiling with HSA_STATUS_ERROR_EXCEPTION at M=1024, N=129280, K=256,
reproduced on two GPU pairs: DSpark verifies 1+5 tokens per sequence, so
a decode batch of max_num_seqs needs six times that many token slots and
4096 leaves four. Cap max_num_seqs at the graph-capture shape wherever
the chunk falls below that bound, which is TP=2 c128 alone. And the
reason c128 never completed before is that at 16384 with capture at
2048, TP=2 c128 held 7.72 GiB, 3.02M tokens, 23.6K per request.

Co-authored-by: Cursor Agent <cursoragent@cursor.com>
Signed-off-by: Fangzhou Ai <fangzhou.ai@amd.com>

SM90 MSA kernels for MiniMax M3
body:
<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

Adds SM90 (Hopper) backends for the four MiniMax Sparse Attention ops: proxy score, top-k select, sparse prefill and sparse decode. `flashinfer/msa_ops/` previously required SM120/SM121, so every entry point raised on H100. This adds CuTe DSL kernels plus an `_sm90_dispatch.py` router, wired into the existing public entry points behind `is_sm90a_supported()`.

Motivation is MiniMax-M3 serving on H100, where the MSA path otherwise falls back to Triton.

**Scope.** 
SM90 implements the *serving* surface rather than the full SM12x surface, and every narrowing raises instead of silently returning wrong numbers:

| | SM90  Support Surface|
|---|---|
| KV layout | paged only (`page_table` + `seqused_k`); ragged varlen raises |
| K/V allocation | must be interleaved in one buffer (`v` is the second half of `k`'s last dim) |
| KV dtype | fp8 e4m3 only |
| `topk` | 16 only |
| LSE / temperature LSE | not returned |
| per-tensor `k_scale`/`v_scale`/`k_global_scale` | not supported (`softmax_scale` and `v_global_scale` *are*, folded into q and the output) |
| indexer (proxy score) | fp8 : prefill and decode; bf16 :decode only, prefill support to be added later |

The packed-KV and paged requirements are free on the serving path — vLLM already stores MSA K and V interleaved in one paged allocation and hands out the halves, so the view is a reinterpretation, not a copy. Materializing either otherwise would copy the whole cache per call, so the dispatcher refuses instead.

Sparse prefill routes on `max_pages_per_seq`: a per-CTA page-union kernel at or below 800, and a one-query-token-per-CTA kernel above it. The union kernel's tile budget is correct only up to mpg 960 (measured: OK ≤ 960, wrong ≥ 1024), so 800 keeps margin. All four ops are CUDA-graph capturable, including across multiple captured batch sizes.

**Preliminary end-to-end numbers.**
MiniMax-M3 MXFP8, TP8 on 8×H100 80GB, vLLM
v0.27.1 with EAGLE3 (K=3) speculative decoding, agentic-coding trace replay.
Both arms are the same server configuration and differ *only* in which kernels
serve MSA — same node, same FlashInfer build, same flags, same KV cache dtype:

| concurrency | ITL (Triton MSA) | ITL (FlashInfer MSA) | Δ | output tok/s (Triton) | output tok/s (FlashInfer) | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 73.6 ms | 33.0 ms | **−55.2%** | 24.9 | 35.0 | **+40.5%** |
| 2 | 82.4 ms | 36.0 ms | **−56.3%** | 25.8 | 48.1 | **+86.8%** |
| 4 | 142.2 ms | 66.6 ms | **−53.2%** | 44.0 | 67.8 | **+54.1%** |
| 5 | 134.9 ms | 57.4 ms | **−57.5%** | 40.9 | 82.1 | **+100.9%** |

Geometric mean: **ITL −56%**, **output throughput +69%** (ITL p50: −61%).

Both arms pin `--attention-backend TRITON_ATTN`, so the dense attention layers (3 of 60) are identical and the delta comes from the 57 MSA layers only; the arms differ by a single environment switch on one node. The trace corpus was filtered to requests of ≤256k tokens to fit a 262144-token server, giving a mean sampled context of 64k–95k tokens across the four points

title: [SDSA 3/7] Add paged MQA logits for an indexer with one head (BF16 keys)
body:
DSA-style sparse attention uses an indexer to pick each query token's Top-K keys. `fp8_paged_mqa_logits` scores keys for an indexer with many heads. This PR adds `single_head_paged_mqa_logits` for an indexer with one head. Its score is the dot product of a query row and a key, with no head weights and no ReLU.

The keys are BF16, with 128 dimensions, in pages of 64 keys. Each request has 1 to 8 query rows, such as a decode token and its draft tokens. The kernel is a warp-specialized SM100 kernel. Its grid size comes from the context capacity, not the lengths, so the call can be captured in a CUDA graph.

On GB200 (NVFP4 keys, 16-128 requests, 32K-1M keys), this grid was up to 15% faster than a grid sized from the actual lengths. It was 3% slower in the worst case.

Part 3 of 7 of SDSA. SDSA is sparse attention with a one-head indexer that picks each query token's Top-K keys, and an MQA core that attends to them. This stack adds it in 7 PRs: token-sparse attention for MQA/GQA (1-2), then the single-head indexer (3-7).

Previous: #6421 (2/7) Add key unions and masks so dense attention kernels can run token-sparse attention. Only this PR's last commit is new.

Next: #6423 (4/7) Support NVFP4 keys in the one-head paged MQA logits, and write them to the paged cache.

title: [SDSA 4/7] Support NVFP4 keys in the one-head paged MQA logits, and write them to the paged cache
body:
`single_head_paged_mqa_logits` scores BF16 keys. Indexer keys are often stored in NVFP4 to save memory and bandwidth. This PR adds NVFP4 queries and keys: E2M1 values, two to a byte, with an E4M3 scale per 16 values.

The scales are keyword-only arguments (`query_scales`, `key_scales`), so BF16 calls do not change. The kernel uses the block-scaled tcgen05 MMA. Keys and scales share one block table, and can be views of one cache.

`quantize_write_index_k_nvfp4` writes the keys: it quantizes BF16 or FP16 keys to NVFP4 and writes them at their cache slots, in the layout that the scorer reads. The caller quantizes the queries.

Part 4 of 7 of SDSA. SDSA is sparse attention with a one-head indexer that picks each query token's Top-K keys, and an MQA core that attends to them. This stack adds it in 7 PRs: token-sparse attention for MQA/GQA (1-2), then the single-head indexer (3-7).

Previous: #6422 (3/7) Add paged MQA logits for an indexer with one head (BF16 keys). Only this PR's last commit is new.

Next: #6424 (5/7) Add Top-K key selection by threshold, without writing all indexer scores.

title: [SDSA 5/7] Add Top-K key selection by threshold, without writing all indexer scores
body:
An indexer picks each query token's Top-K keys. In a long prefill, it is expensive to write a score for every query and key, and then take the Top-K.

`single_head_paged_mqa_threshold_select` keeps only the keys that score above a threshold, for each query row. It does one pass over the paged keys, and does not write all the scores. It writes the kept keys, with their scores, to per-row candidate and tie slots, and counts them. If a row's counts fit its slots and reach its Top-K, its exact Top-K is in its slots.

Part 5 of 7 of SDSA. SDSA is sparse attention with a one-head indexer that picks each query token's Top-K keys, and an MQA core that attends to them. This stack adds it in 7 PRs: token-sparse attention for MQA/GQA (1-2), then the single-head indexer (3-7).

Previous: #6423 (4/7) Support NVFP4 keys in the one-head paged MQA logits, and write them to the paged cache. Only this PR's last commit is new.

Next: #6425 (6/7) Make threshold Top-K selection exact for any threshold.
