title: perf(cake_deepgemm_dense_mqa): fused metadata routes -- one launch for single-query and small-Q FP4/FP8 indexer logits on short KV (SM100a, SM103a)
body:
## Summary

Regenerates the dense MQA lightning-indexer family `flashinfer.experimental.deepgemm_dense_mqa` (public API
`flashinfer.dense_mqa.prepare_dense_mqa_logits` / `flashinfer.dense_mqa.fp8_mqa_logits`) for SM100a (B200) and SM103a (GB300) at
FlashInfer `a7103ae2a`, adding fused metadata routes so that the single-query shapes (K <= 131072) and the small-Q shapes of at most 32 query blocks (K <= 1048576) run one launch instead of a
metadata producer followed by the logits program:

- FP4 fused single-query route `fp4:q1:short` (Q = 1, K <= 131072): the FP4 logits program writes the closed-form
  single-query schedule metadata itself, as the FP8 program already did on `fp8:q1:short` (K <= 131072). Beyond that KV
  length the two-stage `fp4:q1` route is unchanged.
- Small-Q fused routes `<precision>[:full|:partial]:<le16|le128>:short` (<= 4 query blocks (le16) and <= 32 query blocks (le128), both up to K = 1048576): the logits program builds the schedule metadata
  of up to 32 query blocks itself (warp scan over the per-block work, partial last block supported); the prefix extent, the scan offsets and the boundary-search steps of that prologue are compile-time constants of the route's tier ceiling (4 query blocks for le16, 32 for le128: the metadata producer's own tier ceilings), one program text per tier and per precision / block kind; the query count stays a runtime argument (lanes past it carry no work, so the prefix at the ceiling is the total), and the window guard and the boundary rule at the total cost stay runtime, so the metadata words are bitwise the two-launch producer's. They replace the
  former `fp8:q128:short` route (fixed 32 full blocks at K <= 4096) with one generalized path per precision, block kind and tier
  (6 fused small-Q program texts); the fp8 Q = 128 / K = 4096 row keeps its per-tier le128 program and its single launch (unchanged by this head: in the paired A/B against the previous head it read 1.0001x on sm_100a and 1.0000x on sm_103a, a flat control row); the previous head's tier-constant prologue had recovered the 2-tick (0.064 us, sm_100a) and 1-tick (0.032 us, sm_103a) cost that the runtime-count prologue of the head before it had added relative to the former fixed-32 fp8:q128:short program. In this revision's acceptance pass the row reads 1.3394x native/source on sm_100a (6.208 us) and 1.3707x on sm_103a (6.560 us): this row keeps the previous head's readings (its program is byte-identical and was not re-measured), so the values equal the previous pass's. This head raises the admission of these fused small-Q routes from K <= 131072 (le16) and K <= 4096 (le128) to K <= 1048576 on both tiers -- a policy-value change of the catalog (`fp8_fused_small_q_max_kv` and `fp4_fused_small_q_max_kv` = {4: 1048576, 32: 1048576}) with no program text change: every generated program is byte-identical to the previous head's (32 renders over the two architectures). The fused prologue does not depend on the KV length -- K enters only through the min(.., seq_len_kv) clamps and the split counts (at most 4096 per block, so the 32-block cost prefix stays at most 131104, inside the producer's u32 guard) -- and the logits text is the one the shorter KV lengths already run, so the metadata words and every logit stay bitwise the two-launch route's. Six cohort rows become single-launch (fp8 and fp4 at Q = 128 / K = 32768, Q = 128 / K = 131072 and Q = 16 / K = 1048576); the two-launch le16 / le128 twins stay in the route table for KV lengths beyond the bound (the export's holdout rows at K = 1048832, the first 256-multiple beyond it, exercise every one of them). Paired A/B against the previous head (old arm: the previous head's tree; new arm: this tree; the programs are byte-identical, only the route selection differs; two ABBA rounds on one B200 for all twelve rows, four rounds on GB300 with the rows split over three GPUs of one node): B200 fp8 Q = 128 / K = 32768 13.312 -> 12.288 us (1.083x), Q = 128 / K = 131072 31.488 -> 30.656 us (1.027x), Q = 16 / K = 1048576 45.584 -> 44.239 us (1.030x), fp4 14.128 -> 13.728 us (1.029x), 37.904 -> 37.440 us (1.012x), 43.584 -> 42.992 us (1.014x); GB300 fp8 13.312 -> 11.968 us (1.112x), 27.744 -> 26.944 us (1.030x), 44.384 -> 43.488 us (1.021x), fp4 14.048 -> 13.216 us (1.063x), 33.536 -> 33.088 us (1.014x), 37.552 -> 36.704 us (1.023x); every target row faster in every round, the six unchanged-route control rows flat within 0.3 %.
- Catalog `dense_mqa.v7` (was `dense_mqa.v6`): 22 32-head dense routes (7 added: `fp4:le128:short`, `fp4:le16:short`, `fp4:q1:short`, `fp8:full:le128:short`, `fp8:full:le16:short`, `fp8:partial:le128:short`, `fp8:partial:le16:short`;
  1 removed: `fp8:q128:short`) over 16 program texts, each serving both architectures with the SM count
  as a compile-line definition. On every exercised launcher row of both precisions (fp8: Q = 1 / 3 / 16 / 33 / 128 / 130 at K = 4096 .. 1048832 with uneven and mixed windows; fp4: Q = 1 / 7 / 16 / 33 / 128 / 130 at K = 4096 .. 1048832 with uneven and random windows; both architectures, on this revision's tree) the fused routes' metadata words are bitwise equal to the reference metadata routine's -- on the small-Q rows, the six newly admitted shapes among them, with the metadata producer's own tier ceiling selected -- and a repeated launch of the prepared plan (outputs reset to NaN in between) is bitwise equal to the first launch; the fused single-query route and every program text are unchanged by this head (the in-tree indexer GPU slice of 24 tests, the single-query empty-window cases among them, passes on both architectures). The delivered test module's route expectations pin the fused routes up to K = 1048576 and the two-launch twins at K = 1048832 for both precisions, and its case list mirrors the export's twenty holdout rows; the delivered module contains no fused-vs-two-launch comparison.

The two-stage routes (the le16 / le128 twins of the fused small-Q routes among them, serving KV lengths beyond their fused bound), the 64-head dense routes (1 route record, program texts regenerated) and
the paged routes (5 route records, program texts regenerated) keep their schedules. This
change adds no fast-math flag, approximate intrinsic, reduced accumulation precision, sampling or output-changing skip (the fused
single-query route's empty-window path writes the complete all -inf result and the empty partition's metadata, bitwise equal to the
two-launch route's); inputs, outputs,
quantization formats, scale layouts, the kernels' operand lists and the delivered FlashInfer prepare/run API are unchanged.

## What changed in the generated package (vs FlashInfer `a7103ae2a`)

- `csrc/experimental/deepgemm_dense_mqa/generated/`: 22 new programs (22 `*_kernel.cu` + 21 `*_binding.cu` with content-hashed names),
  16 removed (16 kernels + 15 bindings), 0 modified in place. 5 prepared FP4 sequence bindings (`*_seq_<hash>_binding.cu`, one per multi-stage FP4 route) regenerated (5 removed). 1 of the new kernels has no standalone binding (every route launches it through a prepared sequence).
  The family now has 22 kernel programs (27 catalog records including the 5 prepared FP4
  sequence bindings) instead of 16 (21).
- `csrc/cake_device_helpers/`: 6 new and 2 modified content-hashed helper headers (shared with the other
  Cake export families). The two modified ones, `cake_elect_commit_8131fdc67daf4d23.cuh` and `cake_make_warp_uniform_26e432f3ff129648.cuh`, reached main through #6104 without the SPDX line and the two DeepGEMM-notice comment lines this export stamps (+3 header lines each, bodies byte-identical).
- Modified host files: `flashinfer/experimental/deepgemm_dense_mqa/README.md`, `flashinfer/experimental/deepgemm_dense_mqa/dense_mqa.py`, `flashinfer/experimental/deepgemm_dense_mqa/dense_mqa_catalog.json`, `tests/experimental/test_dense_mqa_generated.py`. The runtime's route selection (`route_name`) applies the fused-route
  bounds above from the catalog policy; the catalog JSON carries the new records; the generated test grows from 10 to 11
  test functions (the single-query empty-window cases). Added under `csrc/experimental/deepgemm_dense_mqa/generated/`: `cake_deepgemm_dense_mqa_device_common.cuh` and `cake_deepgemm_dense_mqa_host_common.cuh` -- the family's common device-side and host-side headers (included by every `*_kernel.cu` and by the standalone `*_binding.cu` files respectively; new on main, delivered byte-exact with their SHA-256 digests recorded in the run manifest).

## Per-shape speedup (native DeepGEMM / this revision), cohort indexer rows

The 118-row cohort is the fixed benchmark set of DeepGEMM-family rows this harness tracks on both architectures; its indexer rows are listed here. CUPTI medians of the whole call (every launch of the route), cold L2, paired ABBA interleaving against native DeepGEMM `39d8c4ca` (its `fp8_fp4_mqa_logits` call, for both precisions) in one process. This revision's six re-measured rows (the rows this head newly admits to the fused small-Q routes): B200 12 readings per row, one per shard, on four distinct GPUs of one node (four GPUs read three times); GB300 12 readings per row, one per shard, on four distinct GPUs of one node (four GPUs read three times); on both architectures each shard pairs this revision against native DeepGEMM on its own GPU. The six rows this head newly admits to the fused small-Q routes (fp8 and fp4 at Q = 128 / K = 32768, Q = 128 / K = 131072 and Q = 16 / K = 1048576) were measured on this revision's tree, the sealed export run's commit; every other row keeps the readings of the latest acceptance pass that measured it (the previous head's pass for the eight rows that head regenerated, the pass before it for the rest), taken on trees whose generated programs are byte-identical to this revision's (this head changes no program text: all 32 renders over the two architectures are byte-identical to the previous head's). "previous" = the routes FlashInfer main carries (the two-launch routes and the former fixed 32-block fp8:q128:short route), measured with the same harness in the pass that preceded this PR's first fused-route head: B200 12 readings per row on 12 GPUs, GB300 16 readings per row on 8 GPUs (each carried row keeps the readings of the latest acceptance pass that measured it, on programs byte-identical to this revision's). "launches" = kernel launches per call, FlashInfer main's routes -> this revision; model-indexer_fp8-q128-k4096-scheduled was a single launch already (that pass's table listed 2) and moves to the generalized small-Q path.

native/source is the median over the readings of the per-reading ratio; the us columns are each arm's own median, so their quotient differs slightly from it.

title: perf(cake_deepgemm): SM120 paged MQA-logits indexer: one kernel launch for the DeepGEMM-shaped entry
body:
The SM120 paged MQA-logits indexer ships in one data type, FP8 e4m3, and has 18 routes plus one shared scheduler program. The routes are the (heads, page size) pairs (32, 128), (32, 64) and (64, 64), each with next_n 1 to 6. Every route has two forms: the prepared two-kernel sequence (metadata + logits) and the standalone one-launch logits form. This PR adds the one-launch form of the DeepGEMM-shaped entry `fp8_paged_mqa_logits` for all 18 routes. When the caller passes the schedule from `get_paged_mqa_logits_metadata`, built once per decode step, the call runs the logits kernel alone. It no longer rebuilds the (metadata, logits) sequence on every call. The baseline is the previous shipped version of the same entry, which always ran the two-launch (metadata + logits) sequence. Against it, the one-launch form is 1.21x faster by geomean over the 37 shapes below, with a range of 1.02x to 1.45x.

Measured on NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Server Edition (sm_120a, 188 SMs), CUDA 13.0, driver 595.84.01, as GPU time per call from CUPTI activity records with a cold L2 before every sample, median of 400 samples per arm. Two-launch is `fp8_paged_mqa_logits` with `schedule_meta=None` and one-launch is the same call with the schedule from `get_paged_mqa_logits_metadata`, with operands built as in the FlashInfer test module (random context lengths within 0.7 to 1.3 of the listed average, permuted block tables).

Why the offload
The Engram tables are 183 GiB of the checkpoint. Row-sharded in HBM on 141 GB cards they crowd out the KV pool at TP4. Moving them to pinned host DRAM, read through UVA with unchanged output, frees 23.6 GiB per rank, 94 GiB across the replica.

title: [ROCm][Perf] Candidate-only paged MQA scorer for DSA sparse indexer decode on gfx950
body:
## Purpose

Adds a paged SHUFFLE-layout candidate-only Triton scorer for the DSA sparse indexer **decode** path on AMD gfx950 (MI355X), along with the prefill scorer from the sibling PR.

Decode consumer layers (4 of them at positions 24/28/32/36) score candidates from a paged KV cache in SHUFFLE layout. The current code runs dense score → mask → full-width top-k. The new `paged_candidate_mqa_logits` Triton kernel reads only the live candidate pages per row, computes logits directly over the candidate set, and feeds a compact top-k + remap step (`remap_decode_compact_indices`). A device-side `live_slots` length gate and `_decode_candidate_scoring_admits` guard the fast path. A varctx schedule integration (`_varctx_schedule`) passes schedule metadata to the paged logits kernel for cache-line-aligned access on variable-context batches.

Also eliminates the 25 MB/layer hot-path allocation (full-width logits buffer) on the 4 affected consumer decode layers.

This also includes the prefill `candidate_mqa_logits` scorer (see sibling PR) since the decode and prefill paths share `candidate_blocks.py`.

This is not a duplicate of any open PR. No open PR implements `paged_candidate_mqa_logits` or decode-path candidate-only scoring. AI assistance was used; every changed line has been reviewed and verified.

## Test Plan

```bash
# Correctness: selected scores 143.8 dB SNR vs AITER reference kernel
# FULL-graph replay verified at changed contexts
python eval/eval_b1_decode_candidate_scoring.py

# Variable-context graph crossover verification
python eval/eval_b1_varctx_graph_crossover.py

# E2e benchmark (MI355X, TP=4, C=32, agentic-coding, 600 s):
python bench.py --scenario agentx --conc 32 --duration 600
```

## Test Results

**Component (gfx950, 4 consumer decode layers):**

| Batch geometry | Dense | Candidate-only | Speedup |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 66 rows, ctx 72.1k (p50 C32) | — | — | **3.28×** |
| 192 rows, ctx 88.5k (C32 max) | — | — | **4.85×** |

Correctness: 143.8 dB cell SNR vs AITER reference kernel. FULL-graph replay verified at changed contexts.

**End-to-end (MI355X, TP=4, C=32, agentic-coding, 600 s — this change in isolation, decode scorer only):**

| Metric | Before | After | Δ |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| Output throughput | 305.46 tok/s/chip | 323.20 tok/s/chip | **+5.80%** |
| p90 interactivity | 59.95 tok/s/user | 63.01 tok/s/user | **+5.11%** |
| p90 TPOT | 16.7 ms | 15.9 ms | **−4.9%** |

yeshihai
opened
on Oct 15, 2026
Issue body actions
🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch
Scope:
this is a CUDA / SM90 (Hopper) request. ROCm is referenced only as prior art — the bot CC'd ROCm maintainers on keywords, apologies for the noise.
DeepSeek-V4.1's two-level indexer publishes candidate blocks at
candidate_source_layer_id
; later consumer indexers are meant to select their top-k
inside those candidate blocks only
. On SM100 this is implemented with DeepGEMM's sparse MQA-logits kernels (
fp8_fp4_(paged_)sparse_mqa_logits
). On SM90 there is no equivalent, so the consumers fall back to dense scoring over the full context followed by a mask.
vLLM currently implements candidate-consuming indexers in one of two ways:
SM100
—
fp8_fp4_sparse_mqa_logits
/
fp8_fp4_paged_sparse_mqa_logits
via
DeepseekV41SparseIndexerBackend
. Opt-in through
AttentionConfig.indexer_sparse_logits
and hard-gated on SM100-class hardware (
vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/sparse_indexer.py
, the
is_device_capability_family(100)
check), the MXFP4 indexer cache, DeepGEMM >= 2.8, and the DeepSelect extension.
ROCm (gfx950)
— candidate-only MQA scorers reading the candidate pool in place, in review as
[ROCm][Perf] Candidate-only MQA scorer for DSA sparse indexer prefill on gfx950
#57858
(prefill) and
[ROCm][Perf] Candidate-only paged MQA scorer for DSA sparse indexer decode on gfx950
#57859
(decode).
SM90 (H20)
— neither. The consumers run the full-width
fp8_fp4_paged_mqa_logits
in
vllm/model_executor/layers/sparse_attn_indexer.py
and then mask the scores down to the candidate blocks with
_apply_candidate_mask
(
vllm/model_executor/kernels/attention/dsa/candidate_blocks.py
). The candidate mechanism keeps the semantics but not the compute saving.
Measured on H20 (SM90), TP8, 1M context, decode, FP8 indexer cache, torch profiler:
Concurrency
Per consumer layer
4 consumer layers
Share of a step
~10
2.067 ms
8.28 ms
20% of 40.75 ms
1
196 µs
0.78 ms
6%
Layers 24/28/32/36 each make one full-context
fp8_fp4_paged_mqa_logits
call per step. With
candidate_topk_blocks
= 2048 and
candidate_block_size
= 8, the candidate set is 16 384 positions against a 1 048 576-position compressed context —
1.6% of the scored columns
— so roughly 98% of each consumer's scoring work is discarded by the mask. The cost scales linearly with both concurrency and context length.
The requested feature is a CUDA/SM90 way to score only the candidate blocks.
The MXFP4 coupling blocks SM90 today
indexer_sparse_logits
cannot be enabled on SM90 at all, and not only because of the GPU-family check. The flag also requires the MXFP4 indexer cache (
sparse_indexer.py
, and again in
models/deepseek_v41/attention.py
), and MXFP4 itself is rejected before that:
# vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/indexer.py
if
use_fp4
and
not
current_platform
.
is_device_capability_family
(
100
):
raise
ValueError
(
"indexer_kv_dtype='mxfp4' requires Blackwell datacenter GPUs "
"(sm_10x, e.g. B200/GB200); sm_120 (consumer Blackwell) and "
"earlier architectures are not supported."
)
Hopper has no FP4 datapath, so SM90 necessarily runs the FP8 indexer cache (the
auto
default, one float32 scale per token). MXFP4 is an input requirement of the SM100 DeepGEMM kernels, not part of the "score only the candidate blocks" semantics — the ROCm path, for instance, scores the candidate pool with fp32 logits. So enabling candidate-only scoring on SM90 means letting that semantic flag be satisfied by an FP8 implementation.
Question for maintainers:
should candidate-only scoring on SM90 reuse
indexer_sparse_logits
(relaxing its MXFP4 requirement to a per-platform one), or should it be a separate opt-in with its own builder type? The former keeps one user-facing knob and makes a future SM100 migration a no-op; the latter keeps each platform's preconditions self-contained.
Alternatives
A. Gather + reuse the existing dense kernel (preferred).
Consumers gather their candidate K from the index cache (~2 MB per request) and score the gathered candidate set with the existing dense logits kernel, dropping the mask pass. No new scoring kernel. The scored K set and the query are identical to the dense-then-mask path, so the resulting logits should be bit-identical. A relevant primitive already exists on CUDA:
cp_gather_indexer_k_quant_cache
(
torch.ops._C_cache_ops
, added in
Add gather_indexer_k_quant_cache kernel
#25931
/
[Deepseek-V3.2][Kernel] Integrate cuda indexer k cache gather
#26456
) gathers paged indexer K — FP8 values plus the 4-byte scale — into a contiguous workspace, and the prefill path uses it today. It gathers contiguous ranges addressed by
cu_seq_lens
, so it is a starting point rather than a drop-in: candidate-block gathering needs scattered block IDs.
B. Native SM90 sparse MQA-logits kernel.
Mirrors the SM100 DeepGEMM semantics with a new SM90 kernel, removing the gather hop. Better ceiling, substantially more implementation and validation cost.
C. Two-level selection inside the consumer (HISA-style).
Block-level coarse pass plus a refined pass inside the candidates. Extends the saving to the candidate-source layer and the ratio-2 layers, but changes the scoring semantics and needs accuracy re-validation. Better treated as a follow-up.
Both A and B need a profitability gate, because gathering loads more per key than the dense walk.
#57858
measured the crossover at ~1.0–1.5×
span/capacity
and gates at 2.0×. This workload sits at 62.5×, well above the gate, so the gate should not engage in the target scenario.
Additional context
Relationship to existing work.
This is the SM90/CUDA counterpart of the ROCm candidate-only scorers.
#57858
(prefill) and
#57859
(decode, open) implement candidate-only scoring on gfx950, with measured operator speedups of 3.28× (66 rows, ctx 72.1k) and 4.85× (192 rows, ctx 88.5k), and +5.80% end-to-end output throughput with −4.9% p90 TPOT at TP=4, C=32. They list the same consumer layer positions (24/28/32/36). Those PRs are ROCm-only and touch
rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py
; the CUDA path is unimplemented. This is not a duplicate of them, though all three would touch
candidate_blocks.py
, so ordering matters.
Related, and deliberately out of scope here:
[DSA] Wire DeepGEMM sparse MQA logits into the DeepSeek V4.1 indexer
#56254
wired the DeepGEMM sparse MQA-logits kernels into the V4.1 indexer. Its stated scope is SM100-class GPUs, and it documents "there is no PyTorch fallback anywhere on the path". That is the scoring path this issue proposes to extend to SM90, not to replace.
[Kernel] Enable DeepSelect sparse indexer top-k on sm90
#59204
(draft, conflicting) enables the DeepSelect sparse-indexer
top-k
on sm90. That covers the selection stage, not the scoring stage, and does not touch the SM100 gate on the sparse-logits backend.
[Perf][DSv4.1] Length-aware candidate block selection in the decode indexer
#61039
(merged 2026-10-14) made candidate selection length-aware in the decode indexer, removing ~850 µs/step of full-width work at 1M. It explicitly keeps the full-width path as the fallback when DeepSelect is unavailable, so
SM90 does not benefit from it
:
has_deep_select()
is SM100-only, so
select_candidate_blocks
keeps
FULL_WIDTH=True
on Hopper and still runs
torch.topk(2048)
over the full width. SM90 does have usable top-k backends (
cooperative
,
persistent
), so the same length-awareness looks portable. That is a separate, much smaller item (2.1% of a step at conc≈10, but ~6.5% at conc≈1) and would most naturally ride along with the scoring work rather than be filed on its own.
The DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash kernels tracker (
[Feature]: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash Kernels Integration & Optimization Tracker
#56217
) has no discussion of non-SM100 hardware.
Open items to validate.
Candidate block alignment:
candidate_block_size
= 8 vs the kernel page sizes (32/64).
Bit-identical results between the gather path and the current dense-then-mask path, to be confirmed by measurement rather than assumed.
The profitability threshold tuned for SM90 rather than copied from the ROCm measurements.
Whether the FP8 indexer record (
head_dim
+ one float32 scale) gathers efficiently into the layout the dense kernel expects on SM90, where
mqa_logits_use_mx_scales()
is False.
Environment (target).
GPU: H20 (SM90, Hopper)
TP: 8
Context: 1M
Model: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash
Indexer K cache: FP8 (MXFP4 is unavailable on SM90, see above)
Status.
Happy to implement the SM90 candidate-only scoring path (alternative A), but the flag question above decides where the code lands, so filing this first to get direction. The measurements above predate
#61039
; they will be re-taken on current main before any PR.
Reactions are currently unavailable

title: [Perf][Attention] Candidate-only FP8 indexer decode scoring on SM90
body:
> **Status: draft.** Opened early to get direction feedback before investing in
> the long-term version. The optimization itself works and is measured; the
> path-selection policy is deliberately provisional and will be reworked (see
> [Roadmap](#roadmap)). Comments on the approach are more useful than comments
> on the gating details, which are expected to change.

## Overview

On SM90 the DSv4.1 candidate-consuming indexers have no paged sparse scoring
kernel, so they score the entire compressed context per decode row and then
mask down to the candidate blocks. This adds an opt-in path that gathers the
candidate K from the paged FP8 indexer cache and scores only the candidates.
Implements the alternative-A direction of #61830.

Not a duplicate: #57858 and #57859 implement candidate-only scoring for ROCm
(gfx950); this is the SM90/CUDA counterpart called for in #61830.

## Claims

Claiming only what is measured at this stage:

- At ~1M context, 9 concurrent requests on 8x H20 (TP8): the four
  candidate-consuming indexer layers drop from **9.57 ms to 3.05 ms** per step,
  and per-step time from **39.04 ms to 31.53 ms** (profiler-derived).
- Selected top-k sets are equivalent to the existing dense score-then-mask
  path.
- Default behaviour is unchanged: the feature is off by default, and
  unsupported shapes or platforms fall back to dense rather than failing.
- Known cost: a single-request step is about **11.6% slower** than dense, since
  the candidate path carries a per-step fixed cost. The provisional workload
  gates exist to avoid that region until a better policy lands.

## Validation

Setup: 8x H20, TP8, DSv4.1, `num_speculative_tokens=5`, ~1M token context.
With `1 + 5 = 6` tokens per request the SM90 paged kernel takes the flatten
path, so one active request contributes roughly 6 decode rows.

**Kernel / unit**

```bash
pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_candidate_gather_cudagraph.py
pytest tests/model_executor/layers/test_mla_short_prefill_indexer.py
```

- `test_candidate_gather_cudagraph.py` (new): gather + scoring + remap under
  CUDA graph capture and replay.
- `test_mla_short_prefill_indexer.py` (extended): dense vs. candidate-only
  equivalence of the selected top-k set.

**Equivalence**

With `VLLM_DSA_CANDIDATE_GATHER_FORCE=1`, the selected top-k index set matches
the dense path on identical inputs. Note that #61830's alternative-A hoped for
bit-identical results; this verifies set equivalence instead, since the
gather-then-score path uses a different scoring kernel and top-k tie-breaking
can differ (documented in the module docstring).

**Server-level**

Real `vllm serve` at ~1M context, torch profiler traces collected with the
feature off and on:

| Configuration | Per step | Four consumer indexer layers |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Dense (feature off) | 39.04 ms | 9.57 ms |
| Candidate-only (feature on) | 31.53 ms | 3.05 ms |

at 9 concurrent requests (~54 decode rows).

To reproduce, enable on an SM90 FP8-cache deployment:

```bash
export VLLM_DSA_CANDIDATE_GATHER_DECODE=1
export VLLM_DSA_CANDIDATE_GATHER_MIN_ROWS=16
```

**Validation still in progress** — explicit about what the numbers above do
*not* yet cover, and queued in this order:

1. A profiler-free end-to-end throughput/latency A/B (current timings are
   profiler-derived).
2. Model-level accuracy evaluation plus an independent numerical reference
   (correctness evidence so far is top-k set equivalence against vLLM's own
   dense path).
3. Cross-hardware validation on SM90 parts other than H20 — the reason no
   crossover constant is hardcoded.

I will keep appending results to this PR as they come in.

## Details

**Why the dense path is wasteful here.** The candidate-consuming indexers are
handed a small, fixed-width candidate set, but SM90 lacks a paged sparse
scoring kernel, so they score the whole context and discard everything outside
the candidate blocks. The discarded work grows linearly with context length
(~98% of the scoring work at 1M context, per #61830).

**What the new path does.**

1. Gather each candidate block's K from the paged FP8 indexer cache into a
   compact per-row buffer.
2. Score only the gathered candidates with the existing non-paged FP8 scoring
   kernel.
3. Remap the selected columns back to request-local token positions, so the
   output is identical in meaning to the dense path.

**Scope kept narrow on purpose.** Only the candidate-consuming indexers take
the new path; the candidate-source and pre-candidate indexers stay dense, as
they have no candidate set to exploit. Restricted to SM90 with an FP8 indexer
cache and no context parallelism — SM100 already has native sparse kernels,
and all other platforms keep today's behaviour.

**Tradeoff, and why the current gating is provisional.** Dense cost scales
with `rows x context`, while candidate scoring is dominated by a per-step
fixed cost, so the crossover tracks scanned work relative to the candidate
width rather than context length alone. Since the profitable threshold is
hardware-dependent, this PR does not bake in a device-specific constant and
instead exposes host-side gates (details collapsed below), treating them as a
**stopgap, not the intended final interface**. Defaults impose only
shape-level lower bounds, and the H20 values above are reported as
measurements, not recommended defaults.

**Known structural limitation.** Path selection is host-side per step and is
*not* graph-aware: a fully-captured CUDA graph fixes whichever path was active
at capture time. `FORCE` exists to make that behaviour testable. This is the
main reason the feature ships disabled by default.

<details>
<summary>Workload gates (provisional)</summary>

| Env var | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `VLLM_DSA_CANDIDATE_GATHER_DECODE` | `0` | Master switch. |
| `VLLM_DSA_CANDIDATE_GATHER_MIN_ROWS` | `1` | Minimum decode rows in the step (speculative rows included). |
| `VLLM_DSA_CANDIDATE_GATHER_MIN_WORK_RATIO` | `1` | Requires `rows * context >= ratio * candidate_width`. |
| `VLLM_DSA_CANDIDATE_GATHER_FORCE` | `0` | Validation only: bypass the workload gates. |

</details>

## Roadmap

This PR is a reviewable first increment, not the finished design:

1. **Graph-aware path selection**, so the choice is not frozen by full CUDA
   graph capture. This is the blocker for enabling the feature by default.
2. **Replace the manual env gates** with an automatic, device-independent
   decision (calibration or a cost model), with proper small-batch protection
   instead of a hand-set row threshold.
3. **Longer term**, a native paged sparse scoring kernel for SM90 is the
   cleaner fix than gather-then-score — a much larger change. This PR first
   establishes whether the candidate-only direction is worth it, which the
   numbers above suggest it is.

Happy to run specific concurrency levels, context lengths, or accuracy
benchmarks on request.

On SM100 this is implemented with DeepGEMM's sparse MQA-logits kernels (`fp8_fp4_(paged_)sparse_mqa_logits`). On SM90 there is no equivalent, so the consumers fall back to dense scoring over the full context followed by a mask.

vLLM currently implements candidate-consuming indexers in one of two ways:

1. **SM100** — `fp8_fp4_sparse_mqa_logits` / `fp8_fp4_paged_sparse_mqa_logits` via `DeepseekV41SparseIndexerBackend`. Opt-in through `AttentionConfig.indexer_sparse_logits` and hard-gated on SM100-class hardware (`vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/sparse_indexer.py`, the `is_device_capability_family(100)` check), the MXFP4 indexer cache, DeepGEMM >= 2.8, and the DeepSelect extension.
2. **ROCm (gfx950)** — candidate-only MQA scorers reading the candidate pool in place, in review as #57858 (prefill) and #57859 (decode).
3. **SM90 (H20)** — neither. The consumers run the full-width `fp8_fp4_paged_mqa_logits` in `vllm/model_executor/layers/sparse_attn_indexer.py` and then mask the scores down to the candidate blocks with `_apply_candidate_mask` (`vllm/model_executor/kernels/attention/dsa/candidate_blocks.py`). The candidate mechanism keeps the semantics but not the compute saving.

Measured on H20 (SM90), TP8, 1M context, decode, FP8 indexer cache, torch profiler:

| Concurrency | Per consumer layer | 4 consumer layers | Share of a step |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ~10 | 2.067 ms | 8.28 ms | 20% of 40.75 ms |
| 1 | 196 µs | 0.78 ms | 6% |

Layers 24/28/32/36 each make one full-context `fp8_fp4_paged_mqa_logits` call per step. With `candidate_topk_blocks` = 2048 and `candidate_block_size` = 8, the candidate set is 16 384 positions against a 1 048 576-position compressed context — **1.6% of the scored columns** — so roughly 98% of each consumer's scoring work is discarded by the mask. The cost scales linearly with both concurrency and context length.

The requested feature is a CUDA/SM90 way to score only the candidate blocks.

### The MXFP4 coupling blocks SM90 today

`indexer_sparse_logits` cannot be enabled on SM90 at all, and not only because of the GPU-family check. The flag also requires the MXFP4 indexer cache (`sparse_indexer.py`, and again in `models/deepseek_v41/attention.py`), and MXFP4 itself is rejected before that:

```python
# vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/indexer.py
if use_fp4 and not current_platform.is_device_capability_family(100):
    raise ValueError(
        "indexer_kv_dtype='mxfp4' requires Blackwell datacenter GPUs "
        "(sm_10x, e.g. B200/GB200); sm_120 (consumer Blackwell) and "
        "earlier architectures are not supported."
    )
```

Hopper has no FP4 datapath, so SM90 necessarily runs the FP8 indexer cache (the `auto` default, one float32 scale per token). MXFP4 is an input requirement of the SM100 DeepGEMM kernels, not part of the "score only the candidate blocks" semantics — the ROCm path, for instance, scores the candidate pool with fp32 logits. So enabling candidate-only scoring on SM90 means letting that semantic flag be satisfied by an FP8 implementation.

**Question for maintainers:** should candidate-only scoring on SM90 reuse `indexer_sparse_logits` (relaxing its MXFP4 requirement to a per-platform one), or should it be a separate opt-in with its own builder type? The former keeps one user-facing knob and makes a future SM100 migration a no-op; the latter keeps each platform's preconditions self-contained.

### Alternatives

- **A. Gather + reuse the existing dense kernel (preferred).** Consumers gather their candidate K from the index cache (~2 MB per request) and score the gathered candidate set with the existing dense logits kernel, dropping the mask pass. No new scoring kernel. The scored K set and the query are identical to the dense-then-mask path, so the resulting logits should be bit-identical. A relevant primitive already exists on CUDA: `cp_gather_indexer_k_quant_cache` (`torch.ops._C_cache_ops`, added in #25931 / #26456) gathers paged indexer K — FP8 values plus the 4-byte scale — into a contiguous workspace, and the prefill path uses it today. It gathers contiguous ranges addressed by `cu_seq_lens`, so it is a starting point rather than a drop-in: candidate-block gathering needs scattered block IDs.
- **B. Native SM90 sparse MQA-logits kernel.** Mirrors the SM100 DeepGEMM semantics with a new SM90 kernel, removing the gather hop. Better ceiling, substantially more implementation and validation cost.
- **C. Two-level selection inside the consumer (HISA-style).** Block-level coarse pass plus a refined pass inside the candidates. Extends the saving to the candidate-source layer and the ratio-2 layers, but changes the scoring semantics and needs accuracy re-validation. Better treated as a follow-up.

Both A and B need a profitability gate, because gathering loads more per key than the dense walk. #57858 measured the crossover at ~1.0–1.5× `span/capacity` and gates at 2.0×. This workload sits at 62.5×, well above the gate, so the gate should not engage in the target scenario.

### Additional context

**Relationship to existing work.** This is the SM90/CUDA counterpart of the ROCm candidate-only scorers. #57858 (prefill) and #57859 (decode, open) implement candidate-only scoring on gfx950, with measured operator speedups of 3.28× (66 rows, ctx 72.1k) and 4.85× (192 rows, ctx 88.5k), and +5.80% end-to-end output throughput with −4.9% p90 TPOT at TP=4, C=32. They list the same consumer layer positions (24/28/32/36). Those PRs are ROCm-only and touch `rocm_aiter_mla_sparse.py`; the CUDA path is unimplemented. This is not a duplicate of them, though all three would touch `candidate_blocks.py`, so ordering matters.

Related, and deliberately out of scope here:

- #56254 wired the DeepGEMM sparse MQA-logits kernels into the V4.1 indexer. Its stated scope is SM100-class GPUs, and it documents "there is no PyTorch fallback anywhere on the path". That is the scoring path this issue proposes to extend to SM90, not to replace.
- #59204 (draft, conflicting) enables the DeepSelect sparse-indexer **top-k** on sm90. That covers the selection stage, not the scoring stage, and does not touch the SM100 gate on the sparse-logits backend.
- #61039 (merged 2026-10-14) made candidate selection length-aware in the decode indexer, removing ~850 µs/step of full-width work at 1M. It explicitly keeps the full-width path as the fallback when DeepSelect is unavailable, so **SM90 does not benefit from it**: `has_deep_select()` is SM100-only, so `select_candidate_blocks` keeps `FULL_WIDTH=True` on Hopper and still runs `torch.topk(2048)` over the full width. SM90 does have usable top-k backends (`cooperative`, `persistent`), so the same length-awareness looks portable. That is a separate, much smaller item (2.1% of a step at conc≈10, but ~6.5% at conc≈1) and would most naturally ride along with the scoring work rather than be filed on its own.
- The DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash kernels tracker (#56217) has no discussion of non-SM100 hardware.

**Open items to validate.**

1. Candidate block alignment: `candidate_block_size` = 8 vs the kernel page sizes (32/64).
2. Bit-identical results between the gather path and the current dense-then-mask path, to be confirmed by measurement rather than assumed.
3. The profitability threshold tuned for SM90 rather than copied from the ROCm measurements.
4. Whether the FP8 indexer record (`head_dim` + one float32 scale) gathers efficiently into the layout the dense kernel expects on SM90, where `mqa_logits_use_mx_scales()` is False.

**Environment (target).**

```text
GPU: H20 (SM90, Hopper)
TP: 8
Context: 1M
Model: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash
Indexer K cache: FP8 (MXFP4 is unavailable on SM90, see above)
```

**Status.** Happy to implement the SM90 candidate-only scoring path (alternative A), but the flag question above decides where the code lands, so filing this first to get direction. The measurements above predate #61039; they will be re-taken on current main before any PR.

title: [Roadmap] DeepSeek V4.1 Optimization
body:
Track optimization and feature support for DeepSeek V4.1 in SGLang.

## Refactor

- [x] mHC (DSV41 only) code clean up —  #42245
## General optimization

- [ ] Prefill optimizations
  - [ ] mHC SP + engram fusion — #43065
  - [x] Fold `q_rope_store` into `fused_q_norm_rope` — #41657
  - [x] Faster FP4 index-K gather and `combine_topk_swa_indices` — #41658
  - [x] Prefill indexer: raw selection, row-pair schedule IDs, and host synchronization removal — #41659
  - [x] Fused c1/c2 compression for eager extend and faster c2 decode — #41660
  - [x] Trim prefill model-entry overhead — #41704
- [ ] Decode optimizations
  - [ ] TP4 low latency attention layer #44933 
- [x] Add opt-in TRT-LLM sparse attention support — #41603 
- [ ] Integrate the MegaMoE update: locality-aware scheduling, epilogue prefetch, and shared-memory optimizations — [DeepGEMM #462](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM/pull/462)
- [x] Add MegaMHC support — #42808 
- [ ] Integrate DeepEP V2.5: migrate to dedicated buffer APIs and enable the new communication optimizations — [DeepEP #763](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepEP/pull/763)
- [ ] Packed BF16 prefill on B200/B300 — #41512
- [ ] Fuse source prefill Top-K and block maxima — #41627
- [ ] Use CUDA candidate selection in dense prefill — #40521
- [ ] Shard Engram WKV projections — #40508
- [x] Cache MXFP8 dispatch — #42156
- [ ] Persist FlashInfer autotune measurement policies with cached tactics — #42158
- [x] Reduce eager Engram extend preparation — #42159
- [ ] Replace the legacy topk-v2 with DeepSelect (need LL optimization) — #44051 

## Feature: bounded replay

Goal: both replay flags on by default — same accuracy, never slower than off, faster prefill.

### Encoder replay

- [x] Fix SWA page size with bounded replay — #42128
- [x] Bounded replay with sparse mla - #42273 
- [ ] Enable encoder bounded replay.
  - [x] Fold the replay into the extend forward (16 × 64K hits: 4.6 s → 1.0 s TTFT) — #43166, #43165
  - [ ] Cut decode request-window copies (+6–11 ms → +0.3 ms per step) — #42715
  - [ ] Cut prefill request-window overhead (cold prefill gap 26% → 2%) — #42921
  - [ ] Serve HiCache host-tier hits — #42716
  - [x] Keep the DSpark draft SWA from cutting prefix hits — #44673

### Decoder replay and prefill graph

- [ ] Enable decoder bounded replay.
  - [x] Serve prompt-logprob requests under decoder replay — #44850
  - [ ] Enable the prefill CUDA graph by default for DeepSeek-V4.1 (+19% cold prefill) — #43440 
  - [ ] Make both replay flags compatible with the prefill graph
  - [ ] Capture eager prefill layers as graphs (+54% cold prefill)
  - [ ] Lift the 16K prefill-graph cap; faster prefill all-reduce

### Compatibility and default

- [ ] Support decoder SWA bounded replay with prefill CP and static DSpark PD — #40161
- [ ] DP attention and PD disaggregation
- [ ] Turn both replay flags on by default

## Feature: PD

Original roadmap: #39700 (B200).

### Prefill

- [ ] Support context parallelism — #40323
- [ ] Support CP with breakable CUDA graphs — #40333
- [ ] Avoid host synchronization in CP prefill — #40335
- [ ] Support CP with multistream forward preparation — #40179
- [ ] Reuse shared compressed KV dequantization — #40421
- [ ] Fuse candidate selection and masking — #40436
- [ ] Capture indexer and compressor in breakable CUDA graphs — #40548

### Decode

- [x] Support DP attention — #40177
- [ ] Support MegaMoE — #40178

## Hopper optimization

- [x] Optimize dense GEMM, indexer, mHC, and MoE paths on Hopper — #41251
- [ ] Support candidate-only SM90 indexer scoring — #40860
- [ ] Skip invisible SM90 FP4 indexer tiles — #40503
- [ ] Add an FP8 Tensor Core path for the FP4 grouped indexer — #40160
- [ ] Use DeepSelect Top-K with fused page mapping for Hopper decode — #41561
- [ ] Enable Hopper decode optimizations for TP8 — #39114
- [ ] Add H20 block-FP8 tuned configurations — #41098
- [ ] Add and extend H200 block-FP8 tuned configurations — #40452

+        + row_base[:, None]
+        + page_size * INDEX_K_PAYLOAD_BYTES
+        + off[:, None] * INDEX_K_SCALE_BYTES
+        + sc_idx[None, :],
+        mask=valid[:, None],
+        other=127,
+    )
+    scale = tl.exp2(exps.to(tl.float32) - 127.0)
+    k_low = (low * scale).to(tl.bfloat16)  # [BLOCK_L, HALF_D] elements 2i
+    k_high = (high * scale).to(tl.bfloat16)  # elements 2i+1

+    )

+    logit = tl.where(valid, logit, float("-inf"))
+    return logit

+@triton.jit
+def _fp4_index_logits_paged_kernel(
+    q_ptr,
+    w_ptr,
+    req_ptr,
+    req_table_ptr,
+    lens_ptr,
+    table_ptr,
+    mask_ptr,
+    out_ptr,
+    L,
+    page_size,
+    row_stride,
+    req_stride,
+    mask_stride,
+    out_stride,
+    stride_qb,
+    stride_qh,
+    stride_wb,
+    H: tl.constexpr,
+    HALF_D: tl.constexpr,
+    RATIO: tl.constexpr,
+    HAS_MASK: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCK_L: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    b = tl.program_id(0)
+    n_vis = tl.minimum(tl.load(lens_ptr + b), L)
+    req = tl.load(req_ptr + b).to(tl.int64)
+    for tile in range(tl.program_id(1), tl.cdiv(n_vis, BLOCK_L), tl.num_programs(1)):
+        offs_l = tile * BLOCK_L + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_L)
+        valid = offs_l < n_vis
+        if HAS_MASK:
+            valid = valid & tl.load(
+                mask_ptr + b * mask_stride + offs_l, mask=offs_l < n_vis, other=False
+            )
+        slot = (
+            tl.load(
+                req_table_ptr + req * req_stride + offs_l * RATIO, mask=valid, other=0
+            ).to(tl.int64)
+            // RATIO
+        )
+        logit = _fp4_index_logits_tile(
+            q_ptr,
+            w_ptr,
+            table_ptr,
+            b,
+            slot,
+            valid,
+            page_size,
+            row_stride,
+            stride_qb,
+            stride_qh,
+            stride_wb,
+            H,
+            HALF_D,
+        )
+        tl.store(out_ptr + b * out_stride + offs_l, logit, mask=offs_l < L)
+
+
+def fp4_index_logits_paged(
+    q: torch.Tensor,
+    weights: torch.Tensor,
+    req: torch.Tensor,
+    req_table: torch.Tensor,
+    lens: torch.Tensor,
+    table: torch.Tensor,
+    page_size: int,
+    max_len: int,
+    ratio: int,
+    candidate_mask: torch.Tensor | None = None,
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Score visible compressed positions directly from the request table.
+
+    The output has graph-stable capacity, but only the first ``lens[b]`` values
+    are initialized. Consumers must use the current device-side lengths.
+    The FP4 decoding and BF16 rounding are shared with the dense-slot path.
+    """
+    assert q.dtype == torch.bfloat16 and q.shape[-1] == INDEX_HEAD_DIM
+    assert table.dtype == torch.uint8 and table.ndim == 2
+    assert ratio in (1, 2) and max_len <= req_table.shape[1] // ratio
+    assert req_table.stride(1) == 1
+    if candidate_mask is not None:
+        assert candidate_mask.shape[1] >= max_len and candidate_mask.stride(1) == 1
+    batch, heads, _ = q.shape
+    q = q.contiguous()
+    weights = weights.to(torch.bfloat16).contiguous()
+    req = req.contiguous()
+    lens = lens.contiguous()
+    # Existing candidate-amax needs rows aligned to eight floats.
+    out = torch.empty(
+        (batch, triton.cdiv(max_len, 8) * 8), device=q.device, dtype=torch.float32
+    )
+    if not batch or not max_len:
+        return out[:, :max_len]
+    num_sms = torch.cuda.get_device_properties(q.device).multi_processor_count
+    workers = min(triton.cdiv(max_len, 64), triton.cdiv(num_sms * 4, batch))
+    _fp4_index_logits_paged_kernel[(batch, workers)](
+        q,
+        weights,
+        req,
+        req_table,
+        lens,
+        table,
+        candidate_mask,
+        out,
+        max_len,
+        page_size,
+        table.stride(0),
+        req_table.stride(0),
+        candidate_mask.stride(0) if candidate_mask is not None else 0,
+        out.stride(0),
+        q.stride(0),
+        q.stride(1),
+        weights.stride(0),
+        H=heads,
+        HALF_D=INDEX_HEAD_DIM // 2,
+        RATIO=ratio,
+        HAS_MASK=candidate_mask is not None,
+        BLOCK_L=64,
+        num_warps=4,
+    )
+    return out[:, :max_len]

+import torch

+from sglang.kernels.jit.benchmark import marker

+
+register_cuda_ci(
+    est_time=15, stage="base-b-kernel-benchmark", runner_config="1-gpu-large"
+)
+
+
+def index_topk(q, weights, req, req_table, lens, table, capacity, paged):
+    if paged:
+        scores = fp4_index_logits_paged(
+            q, weights, req, req_table, lens, table, 64, capacity, 1
+        )
+        indices = torch.empty((q.shape[0], 512), dtype=torch.int32, device=q.device)
+        topk_transform_paged_v2(scores, lens, None, indices, 1, plan_topk_v2(lens))
+        return indices
+    positions = torch.arange(capacity, device=q.device)
+    slots = req_table[req[:, None], positions[None, :]].long()
+    slots.masked_fill_(positions[None, :] >= lens[:, None], 0)
+    scores = fp4_index_logits_decode(q, weights, slots, lens, table, 64)
+    return scores.topk(512, dim=-1, sorted=False).indices
+
+
+@marker.parametrize("batch", [1, 4, 64], [4])
+@marker.parametrize(
+    "length,capacity",
+    [(8192, 8192), (8192, 1048580), (32768, 1048580)],
+    [(8192, 1048580)],
+)
+@marker.benchmark("impl", ["slots", "paged"])
+def benchmark(batch, length, capacity, impl):
+    if torch.cuda.get_device_capability()[0] != 9:
+        marker.skip("Hopper decode indexer")
+    q = torch.randn(batch, 32, 128, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    weights = torch.randn(batch, 32, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    keys = torch.randn(batch * length, 128, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    locations = torch.arange(batch * length, device="cuda", dtype=torch.int64)
+    table = torch.empty(batch * length // 64, 64 * 68, device="cuda", dtype=torch.uint8)
+    store_fp4_index_k_cache(keys, table, locations, page_size=64, rne=True)
+    req = torch.arange(batch, device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32)
+    req_table = torch.full((batch, capacity), -1, device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32)
+    req_table[:, :length] = locations.view(batch, length).to(torch.int32)
+    lens = torch.full((batch,), length, device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32)
+    return marker.do_bench(
+        index_topk,
+        input_args=(q, weights, req, req_table, lens, table, capacity, impl == "paged"),
+        # Rotate layer-specific KV and query operands. The request mapping is
+        # shared between layers, as in serving; cloning its unused 1M capacity
+        # would incorrectly reduce the rotation count for the visible KV.
+        graph_clone_args=(0, 1, 2, 4, 5),
+        disable_log_bandwidth=True,
+    )
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    benchmark.run()

+++ b/python/sglang/kernels/ops/quantization/fp8_kernel.py
@@ -1392,3 +1392,27 @@ def per_group_transpose(
 # input  - [M, K]
 # weight - [K, N]
 # Adapted from https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/model_executor/layers/quantization/compressed_tensors/triton_scaled_mm.py
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _dequant_group_fp8_kernel(
+    X, S, Y, M, K: tl.constexpr, SS: tl.constexpr, BLOCK: tl.constexpr
+):
+    offsets = tl.program_id(0) * BLOCK + tl.arange(0, BLOCK)
+    rows, cols = offsets // K, offsets % K
+    value = tl.load(X + offsets, offsets < M * K, 0.0).to(tl.float32)
+    scale = tl.load(S + rows * SS + cols // 32, rows < M, 0.0)
+    tl.store(Y + offsets, value * scale, offsets < M * K)
+
+
+def dequant_group_fp8_to_bf16(x: torch.Tensor, scale: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Expand row-wise group32 FP8 values; UE8M0 scaling is exact in BF16."""
+    m, k = x.shape
+    assert x.is_contiguous() and k % 32 == 0
+    assert scale.shape == (m, k // 32) and scale.stride(1) == 1
+    out = torch.empty_like(x, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    if m:
+        _dequant_group_fp8_kernel[(triton.cdiv(m * k, 1024),)](
+            x, scale, out, m, k, scale.stride(0), 1024
+        )
+    return out

+import sys
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from sglang.kernels.ops.quantization.fp8_kernel import (
+    dequant_group_fp8_to_bf16,
+    sglang_per_token_group_quant_fp8,
+)
+from sglang.srt.layers.quantization.fp8_utils import (
+    block_quant_dequant,
+    triton_w8a8_block_fp8_linear,
+)
+from sglang.srt.utils import is_sm90_supported
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cuda_ci
+
+register_cuda_ci(est_time=15, stage="base-b-kernel-unit", runner_config="1-gpu-large")
+
+
+@pytest.mark.skipif(not is_sm90_supported(), reason="Hopper group32 path")
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "m,k", [(0, 288), (1, 1024), (63, 288), (64, 288), (65, 1024), (257, 5120)]
+)
+def test_cached_weight_linear(m, k):
+    torch.manual_seed(103 + m)
+    x = torch.randn(m, k, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    w = (torch.randn(576, k, device="cuda") * 32).to(torch.float8_e4m3fn)
+    scale = torch.exp2(torch.randint(-12, -5, (18, k // 32), device="cuda").float())
+    cached = block_quant_dequant(w, scale, [32, 32], torch.bfloat16)
+    bias = torch.randn(576, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    kwargs = dict(
+        weight=w,
+        block_size=[32, 32],
+        weight_scale=scale,
+        act_scale_ue8m0=True,
+        bias=bias,
+    )
+    if not m:
+        q = torch.empty_like(x, dtype=torch.float8_e4m3fn)
+        sf = torch.empty(0, k // 32, device="cuda")
+        assert dequant_group_fp8_to_bf16(q, sf).shape == x.shape
+        return
+    q, sf = sglang_per_token_group_quant_fp8(x, 32, scale_ue8m0=True)
+    ref_x = q.double() * sf.double().repeat_interleave(32, 1)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(
+        dequant_group_fp8_to_bf16(q, sf).double(), ref_x, rtol=0, atol=0
+    )
+    actual = triton_w8a8_block_fp8_linear(x, weight_bf16=cached, **kwargs)
+    if m < 64:
+        torch.testing.assert_close(
+            actual, triton_w8a8_block_fp8_linear(x, **kwargs), rtol=0, atol=0
+        )
+    else:
+        ref = ref_x @ cached.double().T
+        raw = triton_w8a8_block_fp8_linear(
+            x, weight_bf16=cached, **{**kwargs, "bias": None}
+        )
+        # Check GEMM rounding before a potentially cancelling bias addition.
+        torch.testing.assert_close(
+            raw.double(),
+            ref,
+            rtol=1 / 256,
+            atol=ref.square().mean().sqrt().item() * 1e-5,
+        )
+        torch.testing.assert_close(actual, raw + bias, rtol=0, atol=0)
+        # Capture the complete quantize/dequantize/GEMM path, then change inputs.
+        graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
+        with torch.cuda.graph(graph):
+            replay = triton_w8a8_block_fp8_linear(x, weight_bf16=cached, **kwargs)
+        x.neg_()
+        graph.replay()
+        torch.testing.assert_close(
+            replay,
+            triton_w8a8_block_fp8_linear(x, weight_bf16=cached, **kwargs),
+            rtol=0,
+            atol=0,
+        )
+
+
+@pytest.mark.skipif(not is_sm90_supported(), reason="Hopper group32 path")
+def test_cached_weight_refresh():

+            weight_block_size=[32, 32],
+            scale_fmt="ue8m0",
+        )
+    )
+    layer = torch.nn.Module()
+    layer.orig_dtype = torch.bfloat16
+    layer.weight = torch.nn.Parameter(
+        torch.ones(64, 288, device="cuda").to(torch.float8_e4m3fn), requires_grad=False
+    )
+    layer.weight_scale_inv = torch.nn.Parameter(
+        torch.ones(2, 9, device="cuda"), requires_grad=False
+    )
+    for scale in (1, 2):
+        layer.weight_scale_inv.data.fill_(scale)
+        method.process_weights_after_loading_block_quant(layer)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(
+            layer._block_fp8_bf16_weight,
+            torch.full((64, 288), scale, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16),
+            rtol=0,
+            atol=0,
+        )
+        assert "_block_fp8_bf16_weight" not in layer.state_dict()
+    layer.keep_plain_weight_layout = True
+    method.process_weights_after_loading_block_quant(layer)
+    assert layer._block_fp8_bf16_weight is None
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(pytest.main([__file__]))

+    references = {}

+        scale = torch.randint(

+        ).view(torch.float8_e8m0fnu)
+        prefix = "w2" if down else "w13"
+        load = FusedMoE._load_w2 if down else FusedMoE._load_w13
+        axis = 1 if down else 0
+        expected = []
+        for data, suffix in [
+            (raw.view(torch.int8), "weight"),
+            (scale, "weight_scale_inv"),

Part of
#41589
(DeepSeek-V4.1 prefill optimizations, split into smaller PRs).
Motivation
The low-ratio (ratio 1/2) prefill indexer ran many small kernels per layer, sorted and remapped its selection before attention, had a schedule that is quadratic in a request's rows, and synchronized with the host several times per step.
Modifications
Fused index-Q kernel in the prefill indexer
: prefill query and head-weight prep goes through
index_q_rope_pack_weights
(
_index_q_and_weights
), shared with decode.
Prefill top-k written straight into the raw selection
: the DeepGEMM prefill top-k emits request-local compressed positions directly into the buffer sparse prefill reads. Pool slots (
page_indices
) are only derived when this forward's attention reads them (trtllm, non-sparse extend, sm120, late-layer tail, request window, or
SGLANG_OPT_FLASHMLA_SPARSE_PREFILL
off).
Selection
is removed; the output buffers are fields of
PrefillInputs
/
DecodeInputs
/
CapturedPrefillInputs
.
write_selection
keeps only the CP dense-blocks path and no longer sorts.
Row-pair request ids for the paged sparse indexer schedule
: DeepGEMM's paged sparse-logits metadata walks back over equal request ids once per row. Ids unique per consecutive row pair of a request (never spanning two requests) bound the walk to one step; logits are unchanged.
No host syncs in the prefill forward
:
get_deep_gemm_prefill_data
builds the flattened-K layout for the whole batch from host lengths instead of a per-request loop indexing with device scalars.
New
async_h2d
in
srt/utils/common.py
(pinned, non-blocking; the counterpart of
async_d2h
), used for the request starts, row-pair ids, CP rows, tail rows, and the engram history.
Engram's
repeat_interleave
takes
output_size
from
extend_seq_lens_cpu
.
No
record_stream
on the mHC stats input
: the stats kernels read the residual on the side stream, and every consumer joins that stream on the main stream while the residual is still referenced, so
record_stream
only delayed the reuse of each freed residual. Without the host syncs the host runs further ahead, and those delayed frees piled up to several full residuals and exhausted the allocator.
Tests
:
test_dense_prefill_indexer.py
and
test_dsv4_nonpaged_indexer.py
follow the new interfaces.
Checklist / TODO
Add coverage for the row-pair ids and the batched flattened-K layout.

DeepGEMM's paged sparse-logits metadata walks back over equal request ids to a row's request start once per row, which is quadratic in a request's rows (~11 ms per call at 16384 rows on GB300). Prefill synchronized with the device ~20 times per step at bs=1: the flattened-K layout of the DeepGEMM prefill indexer indexed req_to_token per request with a device scalar and copied the request starts from pageable memory (twice per index layer), the row-pair ids and the CP rows copied pageable lists, engram's repeat_interleave sized its output from a device sum, and the engram history went up as a pageable copy before the forward. title: DoSA: Dots Sparse Attention
body: Sparse attention visits few keys, yet finding them can still require scoring every key with every indexer head. We introduce DoSA (Dots Sparse Attention), a lossless method for making this computation conditional while preserving exact token selection. Its central observation is that Top-K selection requires sufficient evidence to reject a candidate, not necessarily its full score. A seed set supplies a lower bound on the winning threshold. Nonnegative head projections and joint residual bounds upper-bound positive contributions, while activation-informed aggregation bounds the magnitude subtracted by negative heads. The certificate directs full scoring toward candidates that remain eligible; exact-score filtering further reduces writeback and selection work. We establish the certificate and its exact-selection conditions, and analyze how geometry and selection margins govern its effectiveness. Our GPU implementation accelerates the complete Indexer by up to 2.74 times over SGLang and 1.69 times over LiteTopK across English, Chinese, and code workloads. End-to-end evaluation on GLM-5.2 and DeepSeek-V3.2 achieves up to 1.94 times and 1.50 times time-to-first-token speedups over the two baselines, respectively.

title: PAGE-RAG: Provenance-Aware Graph Evidence Promotion for Fixed-Budget Multi-hop Retrieval-Augmented Generation
body: Multi-hop question answering in retrieval-augmented gener?ation (RAG) often benefits from retrieving beyond the few candidates that will finally be read: narrow retrieval can miss an indispensable hop, while expanded retrieval introduces topical distractors. This challenge is not tied to a particu?lar knowledge-base format. Candidate pools may come from standalone retrievers, standard RAG backends, or graph-based retrieval pipelines. What is needed is a query-aware selection layer that can use relational structure to filter candidates be?fore generation. PAGE-RAG addresses this setting by using a graph as a temporary selection structure, rather than assum?ing a graph-structured knowledge base. It builds a query-local graph over retrieved candidates, records why candidates are connected, and treats each connection as a support hypothe?sis rather than support itself. We identify the resulting failure mode as a connectivity-support gap: connected candidates do not necessarily support the answer. We propose PAGE-RAG, a Provenance-Aware Graph Evidence promotion method that scores candidate paths with relevance, source-tracing meta?data, specificity, hubness, noise, and coherence signals, and applies minimal sufficient selection to promote supporting facts into a compact reader context. PAGE-RAG can serve as a complete retrieval-to-reading pipeline, and the same promo?tion stage can be inserted after existing retrieval or RAG sys?tems without replacing their upstream retrieval logic. Across three multi-hop QA benchmarks under the same final bud?get, PAGE-RAG improves support F1 and answer F1 by 10.4 and 3.3 points on a weighted average over a strong retriever. As a plug-in, PAGE-RAG further improves all reported RAG backends, including reasoning-oriented, compression-based, graph-based, and document/chunk-level systems.

title: Agentic AI for Human Resources: LLM-Driven Candidate Assessment
body:
In this work, we present a modular and interpretable framework that uses Large Language Models (LLMs) to automate candidate assessment in recruitment. The system integrates diverse sources, including job descriptions, CVs, interview transcripts, and HR feedback; to generate structured evaluation reports that mirror expert judgment. Unlike traditional ATS tools that rely on keyword matching or shallow scoring, our approach employs role-specific, LLM-generated rubrics and a multi-agent architecture to perform fine-grained, criteria-driven evaluations. The framework outputs detailed assessment reports, candidate comparisons, and ranked recommendations that are transparent, auditable, and suitable for real-world hiring workflows.
  Beyond rubric-based analysis, we introduce an LLM-Driven Active Listwise Tournament mechanism for candidate ranking. Instead of noisy pairwise comparisons or inconsistent independent scoring, the LLM ranks small candidate subsets (mini-tournaments), and these listwise permutations are aggregated using a Plackett-Luce model. An active-learning loop selects the most informative subsets, producing globally coherent and sample-efficient rankings. This adaptation of listwise LLM preference modeling (previously explored in financial asset ranking) provides a principled and highly interpretable methodology for large-scale candidate ranking in talent acquisition.

title: perf(agentx): move Qwen3.8-Flash-Next H200 SGLang curve to v0.5.22 with TP2 points / 性能：将 Qwen3.8-Flash-Next H200 SGLang 曲线迁移到 v0.5.22 并新增 TP2 点
body:
[by Claude Code]

Moves `qwen3.8next-fp8-h200-sglang-agentic-mtp` from the model-branch image `lmsysorg/sglang:qwen38flashnext` to the `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.22-cu130` release, pinned by digest, and reshapes the H200 AgentX MTP curve:

- **Decode CUDA graphs cover the full admission.** The recipe admitted 2x the concurrency but captured decode graphs only up to the concurrency, so any decode step with more running requests than the concurrency ran eager. At every point `cuda-graph-max-bs-decode` now equals `max-running-requests` (2x concurrency).
- **Points.** TP2/EP2 at concurrency 1, 8, 12, 14 and 16 and TP4/EP4 at concurrency 1 and 8 replace the TP4/EP4 concurrency 1-16 curve.
- **ReplaySSM.** The TP2/EP2 points at concurrency 8, 12, 14 and 16 add `--enable-linear-replayssm-spec`.
- `SGLANG_ENABLE_SPEC_V2` is dropped; v0.5.22 does not read it.

Unchanged: the `Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8` checkpoint and its embedded NEXTN head served as shipped, with FP8 routed experts and BF16 other modules (3 steps, 4 draft tokens, top-k 1), chunked prefill 8192, `mem-fraction-static` 0.85, FlashInfer linear-attention prefill and decode backends, FP32 Mamba SSM state, no KV offloading, and synthetic acceptance selected by the driver from the committed golden curve.

**Validation:** full sweep [39109720946](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/39109720946) passed at head `0d749be1`: all seven points (TP2/EP2 c1, c8, c12, c14, c16; TP4/EP4 c1, c8) and the GSM8K eval at TP2/EP2 c16 (strict-match 0.9765, threshold 0.90). Results: [performance](https://inferencex.semianalysis.com/inference?unofficialRun=39109720946), [accuracy](https://inferencex.semianalysis.com/evaluation?unofficialRun=39109720946).

<details><summary>中文</summary>

将 `qwen3.8next-fp8-h200-sglang-agentic-mtp` 从模型分支镜像 `lmsysorg/sglang:qwen38flashnext` 迁移到按摘要固定的 `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.22-cu130` 正式版本，并调整 H200 AgentX MTP 曲线：

- **解码 CUDA graph 覆盖完整准入上限。** 原 recipe 的准入上限是 2 倍并发，但解码 graph 只捕获到并发数，运行请求数超过并发数的解码步骤都会以 eager 模式执行。现在每个点的 `cuda-graph-max-bs-decode` 都等于 `max-running-requests`（2 倍并发）。
- **测试点。** 用 TP2/EP2 并发 1、8、12、14、16 以及 TP4/EP4 并发 1、8 替换原来 TP4/EP4 并发 1-16 的曲线。
- **ReplaySSM。** TP2/EP2 并发 8、12、14、16 的点增加 `--enable-linear-replayssm-spec`。
- 移除 `SGLANG_ENABLE_SPEC_V2`；v0.5.22 不读取该变量。

保持不变：`Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-FP8` checkpoint 及其按发布形态运行的内置 NEXTN 头（路由专家为 FP8，其余模块为 BF16；3 步、4 个草稿 token、top-k 1）、chunked prefill 8192、`mem-fraction-static` 0.85、FlashInfer 线性注意力 prefill 与 decode 后端、FP32 Mamba SSM 状态、不使用 KV 卸载，以及由驱动从已提交的 golden 曲线中选取的合成接受率。

**验证：**完整扫描 [39109720946](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/actions/runs/39109720946) 在 head `0d749be1` 上通过：全部七个点（TP2/EP2 并发 1、8、12、14、16；TP4/EP4 并发 1、8）以及 TP2/EP2 并发 16 的 GSM8K 评测（strict-match 0.9765，阈值 0.90）。

</details>

</details>

title: [NVIDIA][AgentX] GB300 GLM-5.2 NVFP4 Dynamo+SGLang: PP4-prefill disagg and TP4/TP8 agg points / GB300 GLM-5.2 NVFP4 Dynamo+SGLang：PP4 prefill 分离式与 TP4/TP8 聚合配置点
body:
Moves both GB300 GLM-5.2 NVFP4 Dynamo + SGLang AgentX keys to `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-20261016-a93f16f0` (multi-arch digest pinned). The aggregated key runs the ai-dynamo `1.6.0.dev20261015` bundled in the image (`dynamo.install: false`). The disaggregated key installs the ai-dynamo `1.6.0.dev20261016` wheel. The disaggregated points move to one PP4 prefill worker per node (sgl-project/sglang#39378).

| Config key | Topology | Conc | Nodes | Key settings |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `glm5.2-fp4-gb300-dynamo-sglang-agentic-agg` | TP4 | 1 | 1 | MTP 4 steps, fp8 KV cache, cutedsl BF16 GEMM, 8 running requests and decode graphs, HiCache 100 GB/rank |
| | TP8 | 1 | 2 | MTP 5 steps, 2 running requests and decode graphs, HiCache 100 GB/rank |
| `glm5.2-fp4-gb300-dynamo-sglang-agentic-disagg` | 1x PP4 prefill + 5x TP4 decode | 30 | 6 | prefill HiCache 100 GB/rank, decode radix cache, 24 requests per decode worker |
| | 1x PP4 prefill + 3x TP4 decode | 40 | 4 | as c30 |
| | 1x PP4 prefill + 1x DEP8 decode | 56 | 3 | 8k prefill chunks, prefill mem-fraction 0.75, 32 requests per decode rank |
| | 3x PP4 prefill + 1x DEP8 decode | 216 | 5 | prefill layer split 20,20,20,18, 32 requests per decode rank |
| | 3x PP4 prefill + 1x DEP8 decode | 264 | 5 | as c216 with 8k prefill chunks, prefill mem-fraction 0.88, HiCache 185 GB/rank, decode mem-fraction 0.94 |
| | 4x PP4 prefill + 1x DEP16 decode | 256 | 8 | 32 requests per decode rank |

- Every point uses EAGLE MTP on the checkpoint's built-in NextN head with HiCache write_back DRAM KV offload. Prefill and decode use the same MTP settings (5 steps, top-k 1, 6 draft tokens; TP4 agg uses 4 steps and 5 draft tokens).
- Synthetic acceptance follows the golden GLM-5.2 thinking-on AL: 3.33 at 4 MTP steps and 3.61 at 5. No recipe sets `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_*` or `SGLANG_NVFP4_CKPT_FP8_NEXTN_MOE`.
- KV transfer uses NIXL; no recipe sets `UCX_*` variables. DEP decode workers set `expert-parallel-size` explicitly to match the master config's `ep`.
- Prefill workers advertise a 3600 s session-affinity TTL to the prefill router; decode workers advertise an active-request weight of 8192 to the decode router, so decode routing balances request counts.
- `dram-utilization` is raised to 0.85 for the disaggregated key so c264's 185 GB/rank prefill HiCache plus the DSA-indexer host pool fit; the aggregated key stays at 0.80.
- Tachometer and the Dynamo OTel collector are disabled.
- Removes the aggregated TP8 c2/c4 points, the DEP4-prefill 1P2D/1P4D/1P6D points, the DEP8/DEP16 2P1D c192 point, and `disagg-2p1d-p-dep8-d-dep16-c192-mtp.yaml`, which only that point used.

<details>
<summary>中文</summary>

将 GB300 GLM-5.2 NVFP4 Dynamo + SGLang AgentX 的两个 config key 迁移到 `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-20261016-a93f16f0`（固定 multi-arch digest）。聚合模式直接使用镜像自带的 ai-dynamo `1.6.0.dev20261015`（`dynamo.install: false`）；分离式模式安装 ai-dynamo `1.6.0.dev20261016` wheel。分离式配置点改为每个节点一个 PP4 prefill worker（sgl-project/sglang#39378）。

- `glm5.2-fp4-gb300-dynamo-sglang-agentic-agg`：
  - TP4 c1（1 个节点）：MTP 4 步，fp8 KV cache，cutedsl BF16 GEMM，8 个运行请求与 decode graph，HiCache 每 rank 100 GB。
  - TP8 c1（2 个节点）：MTP 5 步，2 个运行请求与 decode graph，HiCache 每 rank 100 GB。
- `glm5.2-fp4-gb300-dynamo-sglang-agentic-disagg`：
  - 1P5D c30（1 个 PP4 prefill + 5 个 TP4 decode，6 个节点）与 1P3D c40（4 个节点）：prefill HiCache 每 rank 100 GB，decode 启用 radix cache，每个 decode worker 24 个请求。
  - 1P1D c56（1 个 PP4 prefill + 1 个 DEP8 decode，3 个节点）：prefill chunk 8k，prefill mem-fraction 0.75。
  - 3P1D c216（3 个 PP4 prefill + 1 个 DEP8 decode，5 个节点）：prefill 层划分 20,20,20,18。
  - 3P1D c264（5 个节点）：同 c216，另使用 8k prefill chunk、prefill mem-fraction 0.88、HiCache 每 rank 185 GB、decode mem-fraction 0.94。
  - 4P1D c256（4 个 PP4 prefill + 1 个 DEP16 decode，8 个节点）。
  - DEP decode 每个 rank 32 个请求。
- 所有配置点均使用基于 checkpoint 内置 NextN head 的 EAGLE MTP，并启用 HiCache write_back DRAM KV offload。prefill 与 decode 使用相同的 MTP 设置（5 步、top-k 1、6 个 draft token；TP4 聚合为 4 步、5 个 draft token）。
- 模拟接受长度采用 GLM-5.2 thinking-on 的 golden AL：MTP 4 步为 3.33，5 步为 3.61。recipe 中未设置 `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_*` 或 `SGLANG_NVFP4_CKPT_FP8_NEXTN_MOE`。
- KV 传输使用 NIXL，recipe 中未设置任何 `UCX_*` 变量。DEP decode worker 显式设置 `expert-parallel-size`，与 master config 的 `ep` 一致。
- prefill worker 向 prefill router 声明 3600 秒 session affinity TTL；decode worker 向 decode router 声明 active-request 权重 8192，使 decode 路由按请求数均衡。
- 分离式 key 的 `dram-utilization` 提高到 0.85，以容纳 c264 每 rank 185 GB 的 prefill HiCache 与 DSA indexer 主机内存池；聚合 key 保持 0.80。
- 关闭 Tachometer 与 Dynamo OTel collector。
- 移除聚合 TP8 c2/c4、DEP4 prefill 的 1P2D/1P4D/1P6D、DEP8/DEP16 2P1D c192 配置点，以及仅被 2P1D 使用的 `disagg-2p1d-p-dep8-d-dep16-c192-mtp.yaml`。

The original revision of this PR pinned the 2026-09-15 build `nightly-rocm100-cd10ed6f…`. That tag is now five nightlies old, so the pin moved forward to the current one. `main` has also been merged into the branch, which moved this PR's `perf-changelog.yaml` entry to the physical end of the file; `main`'s changelog bytes are preserved byte-for-byte.

`d05da62e` is 294 upstream commits ahead of `cd10ed6f` and 352 ahead of the CSA merge commit. | Upstream PR | Change |

| [#57132](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57132) | Reverts the DeepSeek-V4 accuracy breakdown on ROCm (accuracy-relevant for the eval leg) |

title: [AMD] Enable triton DSA backends and top-k v2 path for glm5.2-fp4 in MI355X
body:
## Summary
- `--dsa-prefill-backend` / `--dsa-decode-backend`: `tilelang` → `triton` (requires sgl-project/sglang PR #30575, commit `8a6ab89bf0b90304b3b454a833fcdcaefb777c29`)
- `lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.16-rocm720-mi35x-20260728` → `lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.19-rocm10-mi35x-20260910`
- `SGLANG_OPT_USE_TOPK_V2`: `false` → `true` (sgl-project/sglang PR #36684, PR #36851 add the gfx950 path) No impact on performance because upstream SGLang already enable

Model, runner, and search space (TP4/EP4 HiCache vs TP8/EP1 GPU-resident arms), MTP speculative decoding with the committed golden acceptance length, and the concurrency grids are unchanged.

Unofficial local, MI355X TP4/EP4. Baseline is the `v0.5.19-rocm10-mi35x-20260908` image-only bump from #2917, not the CI curve. Δ = this PR / 0908 baseline (higher is better).


| conc | 0908 tput | this PR tput | Δ tput | 0908 intvty | this PR intvty | Δ intvty |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 3410.7 | 3659.4 | +7.3% | 152.8 | 166.4 | +8.9% |
| 2 | 3854.9 | 4032.8 | +4.6% | 120.2 | 135.8 | +12.9% |
| 4 | 5746.1 | 5989.9 | +4.2% | 122.9 | 125.3 | +2.0% |
| 8 | 10127.5 | 10571.9 | +4.4% | 75.5 | 87.4 | +15.8% |
| **10** | **12982.8** | **13099.8** | **+0.9%** | **64.1** | **71.6** | **+11.7%** |
| 12 | 12344.9 | 12875.7 | +4.3% | 57.5 | 67.8 | +17.9% |
| 16 | 10888.2 | 11599.8 | +6.5% | 23.3 | 24.9 | +6.8% |

No regression at any concurrency: throughput is +0.9% to +7.3% (mean +4.6%) and P90 interactivity +2.0% to +17.9% (mean +10.9%). The headline conc 10 point is throughput-neutral (+0.9%) and buys +11.7% on the interactivity tail, which is the shape you would expect if the change is mostly a decode-path win rather than a prefill one — at 90-210k input against a few hundred output tokens these points are overwhelmingly prefill-bound, so per-chip throughput barely moves while TPOT does.

The delta is not attributable to one switch. Top-k v2, the triton DSA backends, and a two-day image delta (0908 → 0910) all sit between the two columns; the sweep measures their sum, which is what the recipe ships.


## Test plan
- [x] `validate_perf_changelog.py` against `upstream/main`
- [ ] Single-arm smoke at TP4 conc 1 on the 0910 image (server starts, `--dsa-*-backend triton` accepted, no decode-time memory fault)
- [ ] Full AgentX sweep (`full-sweep-fail-fast`)
- [ ] Accuracy / eval run unchanged versus the 0908 baseline

## Risk

Low-to-moderate. This is a benchmark recipe change with no application logic, but unlike a pure image bump it flips three coupled switches at once: the top-k v2 kernel, the DSA prefill/decode backends, and the container. If the sweep regresses or crashes, bisect in that order — the DSA backend switch is the most likely culprit, since the previous attempt to move ROCm DSA decode off the default hit a GPU memory fault in the a8w8 qseqlen1 persistent kernel.

The `v0.5.19-rocm10-mi35x-20260910` tag uses a `rocm10` segment rather than the `rocm720` naming every other MI355X image in `configs/amd-master.yaml` carries; worth a reviewer confirming that is the intended tag family.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Benchmark-only, but it couples a container bump with DSA backend and kernel-path switches where prior ROCm DSA decode changes caused GPU faults; wrong image tag or silent fallback would skew CI sweeps.
> 
> **Overview**
> Updates the **GLM-5.2 FP4 MI355X SGLang agentic-MTP** benchmark recipe to align with newer upstream SGLang ROCm support, without changing TP/EP arms, HiCache sizing, MTP settings, or concurrency grids.
> 
> In `glm5.2_fp4_mi355x_sglang_mtp.sh`, **`SGLANG_OPT_USE_TOPK_V2`** flips from `false` to `true` now that gfx950 can use the fused DSA top-k v2 path (upstream PRs #36684 / #36851). **`--dsa-prefill-backend`** and **`--dsa-decode-backend`** move from `tilelang` to **`triton`**, which requires SGLang at or past PR #30575.
> 
> `configs/amd-master.yaml` bumps the pinned image from **`v0.5.16-rocm720-mi35x-20260728`** to **`v0.5.19-rocm10-mi35x-20260910`** so startup accepts the triton DSA flags and ships the ROCm top-k v2 build. **`perf-changelog.yaml`** records the same rationale for `glm5.2-fp4-mi355x-sglang-agentic-mtp`.
>

title: [DNM][Experimental] Add MI355X TP2 V4 Flash SGLang 8k1k MTP sweep / 新增 MI355X TP2 V4 Flash SGLang 8k1k MTP 扫描
body:
## Summary

- Add `dsv4flash-fp4-mi355x-sglang-mtp`: DeepSeek-V4-Flash on MI355X at TP2, 8k1k fixed sequence, concurrency 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128. Companion to [B300 #3516](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/3516) and [B200 #3517](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/3517).
- Bundled MTP through `EAGLE` with 2 steps, top-k 1, and 3 draft tokens, matching the other two PRs.
- CUDA/HIP graphs are disabled (`cuda-graph-backend-decode: disabled`, `cuda-graph-backend-prefill: disabled`), so decode, prefill, and EAGLE target-verify/draft all run eagerly; startup reports zero capture time for every graph phase.
- Image `lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.20-rocm720-mi35x-20260926`, the newest ROCm 7.2.0 MI35x build.
- Serving flags and ROCm env follow SGLang's [MI355X Flash FP4 low-latency recipe](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/8ca82118e0e1a0a1b49f85f675843b19ebb388ba/docs/src/snippets/configs/deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4.jsx) (`dsv4` attention, page 256, fp8 KV, shared-expert fusion, mem-fraction 0.90, SWA ratio 0.15, chunked prefill 16384), reduced from TP8 to TP2. Radix cache is disabled for the fixed-sequence workload; admission and the decode graph batch are pinned to each concurrency.
- Weights and KV stay on GPU, with real speculative verification. No engine patches, external draft, CPU offloading, or simulated acceptance.
- Includes the same `--dsv4` fixed-sequence client passthrough and test as #3516/#3517 (identical content), so this PR stands alone.

## Validation

- GPU sweep and evals: pending (`full-sweep-fail-fast`).

---

## 摘要

- 新增 `dsv4flash-fp4-mi355x-sglang-mtp`：DeepSeek-V4-Flash 在 MI355X 上以 TP2 运行 8k1k 固定序列，并发为 1、2、4、8、16、32、64、128，与 [B300 #3516](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/3516) 和 [B200 #3517](https://github.com/SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX/pull/3517) 配套。
- 通过 `EAGLE` 使用原生 MTP（2 steps、top-k 1、3 draft tokens），与另外两个 PR 一致。
- 关闭 CUDA/HIP graph（`cuda-graph-backend-decode: disabled`、`cuda-graph-backend-prefill: disabled`），decode、prefill 及 EAGLE 验证/draft 均以 eager 模式运行；启动日志中各 graph 阶段捕获耗时均为 0。
- 镜像为 `lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.20-rocm720-mi35x-20260926`。Serving 参数与 ROCm 环境变量沿用 SGLang MI355X Flash FP4 低延迟配方，由 TP8 改为 TP2；固定序列负载关闭 radix cache。
- 权重和 KV 保留在 GPU，采用真实验证；不修改引擎、不使用外部 draft、不卸载至 CPU、不模拟接受长度。
- 包含与 #3516/#3517 相同的 `--dsv4` 客户端参数透传及测试，可独立合并。

## 验证

- GPU 扫描与评测：待 CI（`full-sweep-fail-fast`）。
