DeepEP V2.5 introduces dedicated communication buffers for EP, PP, Engram, and bucket collectives, together with new primitives for redundant-expert load balancing. GPU kernels are now compiled through DeepJIT, while installation builds the host C++ extension.
This release also fully removes V1 and its NVSHMEM dependency.
New Features
Dedicated buffer APIs
@LyricZhao
Split ElasticBuffer into EPBuffer, EngramBuffer, PPBuffer, and BucketBuffer, sharing the BufferBase lifecycle.
Add BufferAllocator for planning symmetric tensor allocations before buffer construction.
Expert load balancing
@cqzhangyu
@LyricZhao
Add EPBuffer.lb_prefetch_weights to transfer expert weights and quantization scales to redundant expert slots over NVLink.
Add EPBuffer.lb_reduce_grads to accumulate redundant experts’ FP32 gradients into the original experts.
These primitives support the dynamic expert-replication approach explored by MoonEP and UltraEP. Replication planning and token rerouting are supplied by the integrating framework.
Bucket collectives for CP and DP
@jason-huang03
@bucket-xv
@cqzhangyu
@dromniscience
@sphish
Batched all-gather, reduce-scatter, and all-reduce across NVLink, RDMA, and hybrid domains.
Sessions for communicating ordinary PyTorch tensors through temporary bucket storage.
EP improvements
@LyricZhao
Deferred dispatch/combine epilogues for communication-computation overlap.
Cached expanded layouts and zero padding between experts.
Engram
@tianr22
@sphish
Multi-layer storage on GPU or CPU, with one completion hook per layer.
Build and runtime
@LyricZhao
Move GPU kernel compilation to DeepJIT.
Remove installation-time NVCC compilation and GPU architecture selection.
Notes
Migrate from ElasticBuffer to the dedicated buffer APIs.
V1 APIs, legacy documentation, and NVSHMEM support have been removed.
Bucket collectives, Engram, and PP remain experimental.
Requires NVIDIA Hopper or newer GPUs, CUDA 13.1+, NCCL 2.32.3+, PyTorch 2.10+ with CUDA support, Python 3.10+, and a C++20 compiler.

但存在几类需要在合并前处理的问题：(1) .gitmodules 使用 SSH 地址，匿名用户无法初始化子模块；(2) 新开启 ruff Q000 规则且几乎全部 .py 文件都在 diff 内，多处 Q000/F541/B904/B010/E722/W293 会让 format.yml CI 失败；(3) 测试中使用了 dist.all_gather_single / dist.reduce_scatter_single，需确认 PyTorch 是否提供；(4) EP_NIC_NAME 环境变量被静默删除且 BucketBuffer 硬性要求同时检测到 NVLink 和 RDMA 带宽，非 mlx5_0 NIC 或无 IB 机器上不可用；(5) do_handle_copy/sl_idx 默认值静默变更；(6) 托管 NCCL comm 与 Context::finalize 的析构顺序风险；(7) comm.get_comm_stream 模块级签名与方法绑定冲突。此外 deep_ep/include/deep_ep/impls/bucket/** 的设备内核（约 1.8k 行）只审阅了接口层，同步语义需由能在多机 GPU 上运行 tests/bucket/* 与 tests/ep/test_ep.py 的同学确认。本次为静态审阅，无法编译或运行 GPU 测试。
v4
DeepEP V2.5 是一个体量很大的重构 PR：删除 V1/legacy 与 NVSHMEM 依赖，把通信能力拆分为 EPBuffer / BucketBuffer / EngramBuffer / PPBuffer 四类 buffer，统一 BufferBase、comm::Context 与 DeepJIT 运行时，并新增 bucket 集合通信、冗余专家权重预取/梯度归约、延迟 epilogue、多 layer Engram 等能力。整体结构清晰、测试覆盖（尤其 tests/bucket/test_mixed.py）较充分；但本 PR 引入了一个明确的功能回归（EP_NIC_NAME 被删除），并存在若干接口安全性与文档一致性问题。

title: github:deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM:411 fetched implementation patch
[Fix][Einsum] Reject `c` in SM90 `fp8_einsum("bhr,hdr->bhd")` to prevent silent data corruption in `sm90_fp8_bmm`
body:
This PR fixes #476 .

## Summary

On SM90, `deep_gemm.fp8_einsum("bhr,hdr->bhd", a, b, d, c)` returns `a @ b.T` instead of `c + a @ b.T`: `c` is silently dropped.

- The host first copies `c` into `d`, expecting the kernel to add `a @ b.T` onto `d` ([gemm.hpp L49–L51](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM/blob/1fc9c66975ee322d628b3288534ca0e9ce12a64d/csrc/apis/gemm.hpp#L49-L51)).
- On SM90, `sm90_fp8_bmm` launches `sm90_fp8_gemm_1d2d_impl`, which cannot add onto `d`. It writes `d` with a plain TMA store ([sm90_fp8_gemm_1d2d.cuh L434](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM/blob/1fc9c66975ee322d628b3288534ca0e9ce12a64d/deep_gemm/include/deep_gemm/impls/sm90_fp8_gemm_1d2d.cuh#L434)), which overwrites `c`. `sm90_fp8_bmm` sets `with_accumulation` ([L300](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM/blob/1fc9c66975ee322d628b3288534ca0e9ce12a64d/csrc/jit_kernels/impls/sm90_fp8_gemm_1d2d.hpp#L300)), but never passes it to the kernel ([L36–L61](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM/blob/1fc9c66975ee322d628b3288534ca0e9ce12a64d/csrc/jit_kernels/impls/sm90_fp8_gemm_1d2d.hpp#L36-L61)).
- The other launcher of this kernel, `sm90_fp8_gemm_1d2d`, rejects `c` ([L81](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM/blob/1fc9c66975ee322d628b3288534ca0e9ce12a64d/csrc/jit_kernels/impls/sm90_fp8_gemm_1d2d.hpp#L81)). `sm90_fp8_bmm` does not ([L290](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM/blob/1fc9c66975ee322d628b3288534ca0e9ce12a64d/csrc/jit_kernels/impls/sm90_fp8_gemm_1d2d.hpp#L290)).

`"bhr,hdr->bhd"` is the only `fp8_einsum` expression that runs on SM90, and `tests/test_einsum.py` passes `c` to it only on SM100, which accumulates correctly. 

Reproduction: See Issue #476 .

## Fix

Add the missing `not c.has_value()` check to `sm90_fp8_bmm`, as in `sm90_fp8_gemm_1d2d`. Passing `c` on SM90 now raises an error instead of returning a wrong result. As with `sm90_fp8_gemm_1d2d`, `d` has already been overwritten with `c` when the error is raised.

```diff
--- a/csrc/jit_kernels/impls/sm90_fp8_gemm_1d2d.hpp
+++ b/csrc/jit_kernels/impls/sm90_fp8_gemm_1d2d.hpp
@@ -287,7 +287,7 @@ static void sm90_fp8_bmm(const torch::Tensor& a, const torch::Tensor& sfa,
                          const int& batch_size, const int& m, const int& n, const int& k,
                          const cute::UMMA::Major& major_a, const cute::UMMA::Major& major_b, const cute::UMMA::Major& major_sfb,
                          const std::string& compiled_dims) {
-    DG_HOST_ASSERT(d.scalar_type() == torch::kBFloat16);
+    DG_HOST_ASSERT(not c.has_value() and d.scalar_type() == torch::kBFloat16);
     DG_HOST_ASSERT(major_a == cute::UMMA::Major::K and major_b == cute::UMMA::Major::K);
 
     const auto desc = GemmDesc {
```

## Tests

`test_fp8_bhr_hdr_bhd` already checks `c` on SM100. This PR adds the SM90 counterpart: a call with `c` must raise. The accumulator has the layout of the SM100 check (`[h, b, d]` viewed as `[b, h, d]`), in BF16, the only `d` type `sm90_fp8_bmm` accepts.

```diff
                         assert_stochastic_bf16_matches_fp32_accumulation(
                             z_sr, launch_accumulated, f'{b=}, {h=}, {r=}, {d=}')
+                    else:
+                        # SM90's FP8 BMM kernel cannot add C into D, so C must be rejected
+                        acc = torch.zeros((h, b, d), device='cuda', dtype=torch.bfloat16).permute(1, 0, 2)
+                        try:
+                            deep_gemm.fp8_einsum('bhr,hdr->bhd', x_fp8, y_fp8, acc, c=acc)
+                        except RuntimeError:
+                            pass
+                        else:
+                            raise AssertionError(f'{b=}, {h=}, {r=}, {d=}: C must be rejected on SM90')
```

Tested on an H100 80GB HBM3 (driver 580.126.09, CUDA 13.0, torch 2.9.1+cu130), on `main` (1fc9c66) and on this branch, both built with `./develop.sh`. The test functions run in the order of `__main__`, after one warm-up `bench_kineto` call. Without the warm-up, `python tests/test_einsum.py` stops at its first benchmark with a `ZeroDivisionError` on both trees, because `bench_kineto` returns 0 on its first call in a process (#426).

`main` with the new test: the call with `c` does not raise, so the test fails.

```
Testing "bmk, bnk -> mn":
Testing "bhr, hdr -> bhd":
Testing "bhd, hdr -> bhr":
Testing "bhd, bhr -> hdr":
Testing FP8 "bhr, hdr -> bhd":
...
AssertionError: b=4, h=8, r=4096, d=1024: C must be rejected on SM90
```

This PR:

```
Testing "bmk, bnk -> mn":
Testing "bhr, hdr -> bhd":
Testing "bhd, hdr -> bhr":
Testing "bhd, bhr -> hdr":
Testing FP8 "bhr, hdr -> bhd":
test_fp8_bhd_hdr_bhr:
 > Filtered by <function <lambda> at 0x73748c055760>
test_fp8_bhd_bhr_hdr:
 > Filtered by <function <lambda> at 0x73748c055800>
ALL TESTS PASSED
```

Problem
deep_jit::cuda::Device::get_prop()
calls
cudaFree(nullptr)
once to make sure the CUDA context exists.
cudaFree
is prohibited while a stream is being captured in the global or thread-local mode. If the first device query happens inside a capture, it fails with
cudaErrorStreamCaptureUnsupported
(900), DeepJIT panics, and the capture is invalidated (
cudaErrorStreamCaptureInvalidated
, 901, at
cudaStreamEndCapture
).
Libraries hit this through lazy initialization: the runtime created by
create_lazy_jit
queries the device on first use. With DeepGEMM
main
(which pins DeepJIT
e5bdee2
), the first DeepGEMM call in a process fails if it happens inside
torch.cuda.graph
with the default capture mode:
Panic error (third-party/deep_jit/include/deep_jit/backend/cuda/device.hpp:15): cudaFree(nullptr) failed with CUDA error 900 (cudaErrorStreamCaptureUnsupported): operation not permitted when stream is capturing
  #0 deep_jit::cuda::Device::get_prop() at third-party/deep_jit/include/deep_jit/backend/cuda/device.hpp:15
  #1 deep_jit::cuda::CompilerOptions::default_options(deep_jit::Env const&, deep_jit::cuda::Device&) at third-party/deep_jit/include/deep_jit/backend/cuda/device.hpp:62
  #2 ... deep_gemm::init_jit(...)::{lambda} ...
  #3 deep_jit::LazyInit<deep_jit::Runtime<deep_jit::CUDA> >::operator->()

title: [SM90] Add optimized SM90 support.
body:
## Summary

This PR adds an optimized SM90 build and runtime path for Hopper GPUs such as H20 and H100, while preserving the existing SM100/SM103 defaults.

SM90 uses an 8-CTA cluster for small-batch, long-sequence BF16 Top-K workloads. The cluster path is enabled from a vocabulary size of 128K, based on measurements on an 8×H20 machine. SM100 and SM103 continue to use the existing 16-CTA cluster and 512K threshold.

## Changes

- Add `DEEP_SELECT_CUDA_ARCHS` to select `90a`, `100a`, and/or `103a` at build time.
- Keep the default build targets unchanged: `sm_100a` and `sm_103a`.
- Add eight SM90 cluster instantiations covering:
  - `int32` and `int64` output indices
  - `sorted_index` enabled and disabled
  - `return_value` enabled and disabled
- Dispatch SM90 BF16 workloads to an 8-CTA cluster when:
  - `batch_size <= 6`
  - `vocab_size >= 128K`
  - `topk <= 1024`
- Preserve the existing 16-CTA cluster and 512K threshold for SM100/SM103.
- Fall back to `nvidia-smi -L` for CUDA platform detection when `lspci` is unavailable in a container.
- Avoid the `std::format` dependency in the C++ binding so the extension builds with older host standard libraries commonly found in CUDA containers.
- Document the SM90 build command:

```bash
DEEP_SELECT_CUDA_ARCHS=90a pip install -v .
```

## Performance

Measured on NVIDIA H20 with BF16 input, `batch_size` 1 and 6, and `topk` 512 and 1024. Each result is the median of 100 cold-cache runs.

The improvement column compares the new 8-CTA cluster with the existing single-CTA path compiled for SM90.

| Vocabulary size | Improvement over single CTA | Speedup over `torch.topk` |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 128K | 25.2%–35.0% | 3.11×–3.83× |
| 256K | 36.5%–44.6% | 2.79×–3.57× |
| 512K | 52.4%–56.1% | 2.66×–3.75× |
| 1M | 61.5%–62.3% | 2.12×–4.11× |

Short-sequence and large-batch workloads continue to use the existing normal kernel. Their measured speedup over `torch.topk` remains 4.88×–6.27×.

## Validation

- Clean SM90 build with CUDA 13.0 and PyTorch 2.11.
- `cuobjdump` register-spill check passed with no spills.
- 20/20 targeted correctness cases passed.
- Coverage included:
  - normal and 8-CTA cluster paths
  - BF16 and FP32 inputs
  - `int32` and `int64` indices
  - `sorted_index`
  - optional value output
  - variable row lengths through `end`
  - per-row index offsets
- The final performance matrix passed Top-K value-set validation against `torch.topk` for every case.

title: V4.1-Flash native reasoning loops: prompt/history contract and model-team triage request
body:
## Summary and request for model-team triage

We observe DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash entering native-token reasoning loops during long, tool-enabled conversations. It repeatedly announces that it will emit an answer or tool call, but produces neither. Some outputs run to the token limit; others are stopped by our resource-protection observer.

We are asking for the canonical V4.1 prompt/history contract and help routing this report to the model/inference team. The official model card recommends deepseek-recipe and invites issues or contact at service@deepseek.com. Our failed runs used vLLM's V4.1 encoder, not deepseek-recipe itself; this is **not a claim that recipe caused the loops**. Please redirect us if another official tracker is preferred.

## Environment and workload

- Model: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash open weights. This is a local-inference report, not a demonstrated failure of the official hosted API.
- Engine in the reported Spark experiments: vLLM 0.28.1rc1.dev388+g8a728663c.
- Hardware: four NVIDIA DGX Spark / GB10 nodes forming one TP4/DCP4 model service.
- Recorded precision: BF16 engine dtype, MXFP4 routed-expert weights, fp8_ds_mla main attention KV. These refer to different objects.
- Main fixed replay input: 107 messages, 26 tool definitions, 74,657 actual input tokens.
- Sampling in the completed five-arm experiment: thinking enabled, numeric reasoning_effort=100, temperature=1.0, top_p=0.95, min_p=0, top_k=-1, max_tokens=8192, global concurrency 4.
- DSpark enabled in that experiment: num_speculative_tokens=5, probabilistic draft sampling, block rejection sampling, adaptive verification disabled.
- A thinking-budget sampler fix was present in the budget experiment; those results are implementation-specific mitigation evidence, not an unmodified-vLLM or official parameter recommendation.

## Expected vs. actual behavior

Expected: complete the reasoning phase and emit valid tool calls or a final answer.

Actual native output contains repeated procedural phrases, for example:

```text
Writing.
Let me output.
Go.
OK.
Writing.
Let me write.
Go.
Now.
```

For baseline seed 21020, the saved output contains 2,158 native generated tokens before observer cancellation, 8,262 reasoning characters, empty content, and no tool calls. An exact 20-token period starts at generated position 1,987 (one-based) and repeats for at least eight cycles. We rechecked equality directly against the saved token IDs:

```json
[339,46837,339,5718,678,5238,339,5188,339,11932,339,46837,339,5718,678,5085,339,5188,339,8197]
```

The five confirmed baseline loops were independently rechecked:

| Seed | Exact-cycle onset, generated token position (1-based) | Period, tokens | Consecutive cycles verified |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 21020 | 1987 | 20 | 8 |
| 21044 | 2418 | 15 | 10 |
| 21054 | 2308 | 12 | 10 |
| 21068 | 2916 | 15 | 8 |
| 21098 | 3438 | 13 | 9 |

These are engine-token loops within one generation. Client request repetition is not needed to produce these captured cycles.

## Controlled observations

### 1. Fixed-input, five-arm experiment

Each arm dispatched exactly 100 requests; sent failures were not replaced.

| Arm, single parameter change | Complete non-repeat responses | Confirmed repeats | Service/transport unknowns |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| A: no thinking budget or penalty | 88 | 5 | 7 |
| B: thinking budget 1536 | 92 | 0 | 8 |
| C: frequency_penalty=0.2 | 88 | 0 | 12 |
| D: presence_penalty=0.2 | 88 | 5 | 7 |
| E: repetition_penalty=1.05 | 92 | 2 | 6 |

Unknowns are not clean negatives. A complete response does not prove business-task success. A separate 100-task quality evaluation per arm scored A/B/C/D/E as 91/93/84/91/92 passes; service failures remain in the denominators, so these numbers do not establish quality-neutral mitigation.

### 2. Identical input IDs, different generation trajectories

We compared one normal baseline seed (21000), the five looping baseline seeds above, and their six budget-arm counterparts. All 12 captured prompt-token arrays were identical, length 74,657.

For the five looping baseline seeds, the corresponding budget-arm responses completed with tool calls. Their reasoning lengths were 1536, 175, 341, 299, and 286 tokens respectively. Only one reached the budget. The four early completions cannot all be explained by forcibly cutting off an existing loop at 1536. We have not established why these trajectories diverge before budget exhaustion.

### 3. DSpark / CUDA-graph pilot

A separate 16-request, effort50 pilot yielded phrase-threshold repeat cancellations:

| DSpark | Graph mode | Repeat cancellations / attempts |
|---|---|---:|
| enabled | FULL_AND_PIECEWISE | 2/4 |
| disabled | NONE | 2/4 |
| disabled | FULL_AND_PIECEWISE | 1/4 |
| enabled | NONE | 0/4 |

Graph NONE here is not a claim that enforce-eager was used. This small pilot cannot estimate production incidence, but neither DSpark nor graph execution is a necessary condition for the observed loops.

### 4. Failed-history feedback

In an earlier reconstructed CC conversation, keeping a failed assistant body produced 8192 output tokens, all reasoning, with 471 newly generated "Let me write" occurrences and no content/tools (seed42). Removing that body completed with tools; restoring the exact request looped again. One cleaned-history control padded back to the original 106652 input-token length also completed with tools.

This is a small-sample history-amplification signal, not an explanation of the first failure. A later partial comparison also shortened the input by 32002 tokens, so it does not isolate history semantics from length.

## Questions for DeepSeek

1. Is native reasoning/procedural looping of this form a known V4.1-Flash failure? Are there model, encoder, or inference fixes, or recommended diagnostic builds?
2. What is the canonical history contract for tool-enabled thinking: which historical reasoning_content must be retained, and how should incomplete/looping assistant output be represented? How should this differ from ordinary multi-turn requests without tools?
3. Can the model team recommend a reference inference path and precision/cache settings for comparing the same prompt token IDs and generated prefix against our vLLM path?
4. Could CSA2/chunked-KV phase sensitivity contribute to entering such loops? We are referring to [Periodic Weak Spots, arXiv:2609.36322](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.36322) and its [interactive explanation](https://ultimatejupiter.github.io/blog/periodic-weak-spots/). We have **not** performed a meaning-preserving phase sweep, and our 12/13/15/20-token output periods are not evidence of the paper's two-token input-phase periodicity.
5. What artifact format and private channel would your team prefer for prompt/token-prefix replay? Please help connect us to the V4.1 model/inference maintainers.

Related prompt-contract reports: #5 and #6. There is also a similar symptom report in the official harness Discussions: https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/discussions/8425 (a separate user's report, not our evidence).

## Evidence availability and reproduction limits

We retain final request JSON, raw SSE, prompt/generated token IDs, parameter/dispatch records, and per-run results. Publicly shared material here is limited to diagnostic output and aggregate results; original engineering conversations and tool payloads are not attached. This public report is therefore not yet a standalone minimal reproduction. We can prepare a redacted replay package once the maintainers identify the needed fields and an appropriate channel. Redaction may change tokens and reproduction behavior; we will report that limitation explicitly.

Summary and request for model-team triage
We observe DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash entering native-token reasoning loops during long, tool-enabled conversations. It repeatedly announces that it will emit an answer or tool call, but produces neither. Some outputs run to the token limit; others are stopped by our resource-protection observer.
We are asking for the canonical V4.1 prompt/history contract and help routing this report to the model/inference team. The official model card recommends deepseek-recipe and invites issues or contact at
service@deepseek.com
. Our failed runs used vLLM's V4.1 encoder, not deepseek-recipe itself; this is
not a claim that recipe caused the loops
. Please redirect us if another official tracker is preferred.
Environment and workload
Model: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash open weights. This is a local-inference report, not a demonstrated failure of the official hosted API.
Engine in the reported Spark experiments: vLLM 0.28.1rc1.dev388+g8a728663c.
Hardware: four NVIDIA DGX Spark / GB10 nodes forming one TP4/DCP4 model service.
Recorded precision: BF16 engine dtype, MXFP4 routed-expert weights, fp8_ds_mla main attention KV. These refer to different objects.

title: feat(topk_varlen): exact CuTe-DSL primitives top-k backends with fused page-table output (Ampere and newer)
body:
<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

Exact, single-launch top-k for the DeepSeek sparse-attention (DSA) indexer, as four new
`top_k_varlen` backends plus a fused paged output, with Ampere and newer as the floor instead
of Blackwell only.

**New backends** (all CuTe-DSL *primitives* kernels: raw pointers, integer address math,
`cute.arch` PTX wrappers; no layout algebra, so one source compiles for sm_80 through sm_120
and Rubin):

- `walkfirst_primitives` — the decode default. A replica-deterministic sample sets a value
  threshold and a 256-bin scale; every CTA walks its slice once; the last-arriving CTA merges
  the bin-major publish tables and resolves the crossing bin with an exact key-space select.
  Rows up to 16K columns never enter that pipeline: a census arm (<= 4K) and a register-resident
  arm (4K to 16K) solve them in one CTA. Floods past the tie capacity are refined from the
  crossing bin's exact key range; anything else falls through to a fused exact re-solve on
  device, so every call stays sync-free and CUDA-graph capturable.
- `radix_primitives` — SGLang's coarse-histogram structure made exact (no tie truncation),
  fp32/fp16/bf16, grouped rows (`next_n`) and compressed columns (`compress_ratio`), optional
  values, multi-CTA long rows.
- `cutlass_primitives` — the vendored cutlass-primitives library (`VENDORED.md`, Apache-2.0):
  register, clustered-register and streaming kernels with a census split for large k; the
  full-row leader. `flashinfer.topk_varlen` exports its workspace helpers
  (`cutlass_primitives_workspace_bytes`, `cutlass_primitives_row_order`) and
  `release_cutlass_primitives_resources`.
- `sglang` — SGLang's own DeepSeek-V4 indexer top-k (Apache-2.0, vendored verbatim from upstream
  commit 7f27bf4708; `csrc/sglang_dsv4/VENDORED.md`, `licenses/LICENSE.sglang.txt`) under the
  same contract, including a paged variant: the same kernel SGLang runs, for parity and for the
  check that the FlashInfer API adds no overhead over the raw kernel. It is exact only while the
  rank-k bin holds at most 2048 candidates, so `auto` never selects it.

**Fused paged output.** `top_k_varlen(..., page_table=table, page_size=64)` returns physical
KV slots `page_table[q, c // page_size] * page_size + c % page_size` from the selection launch
itself (the SGLang DSA decode contract, one kernel instead of a top-k plus a transform pass).
The table is a contiguous, 16-byte-aligned int32 `(requests, max_pages)` tensor covering every
request's valid length; it may be narrower than the logits width, and rows past its coverage
are clamped to the covered prefix. Served by `walkfirst_primitives`, `radix_primitives` and
`sglang`; `backend="auto"` with a page table ranks the two exact primitives backends (they are
outside the unpaged ranking).

**Also in this PR:** a fix to the pre-existing multi-CTA `radix` kernel (chunks shorter than
their misaligned prefix read past the valid length and wrote shared memory at negative offsets;
CTA 0 could reset the group's arrival counter while a time-sliced peer still spun on it; the
per-group state grows by one int, STATE_SIZE 770 to 771, allocated internally with a bumped
cache key), the trace template for `top_k_varlen` extended with the paged inputs (the page size
names the paged definitions), the benchmarks that produced the numbers below, the four new
backends in `benchmarks/routines/topk_varlen.py`, and a one-line fix to
`tests/trace/example.py` (an upstream call passed a `str` device to `is_sm100a_supported`, which
crashes the example on sm_100 hosts).

**Why.** The DSA indexer runs one top-k per layer per decode step; SGLang today uses its own
fused kernel. These backends are exact where that kernel approximates, faster on every decode
cell we measured across six architectures, and fuse the page-table output so an engine needs
one launch. Measurements (`benchmarks/bench_topk_replay_ties.py`, CUDA-graph replay, 16 rows,
K 512, fp32, rows from a recorded DeepSeek decode trace of 500 to 2100 columns in a 16K buffer;
"paged" = fused page-table output on both sides; us per call):

| GPU | SGLang paged, Gaussian | walk-first paged | SGLang paged, ReLU rows | walk-first paged | 64K full rows: SGLang / walk-first / cutlass_primitives |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| B200 | 3.77 | 3.31 | 5.73 | 3.62 | 13.9 / 7.6 / 7.9 |
| H100 PCIe | 3.99 | 3.44 | 6.20 | 3.78 | 14.8 / 8.8 / 8.8 |
| A100 40GB | 4.88 | 4.37 | 7.77 | 5.65 | 19.2 / 11.1 / 11.0 |
| L40S | 3.00 | 2.83 | 4.66 | 3.59 | 11.8 / 7.8 / 7.7 |
| RTX 5080 | 2.61 | 2.42 | 3.98 | 2.64 | 10.0 / 8.1 / 5.7 |
| Rubin (208-SM part) | 3.02 | 2.69 | 4.48 | 2.90 | 12.6 / 6.3 / 5.3 |

Fixed Gaussian rows of 600 to 16K columns run 1.10x to 1.24x faster than SGLang's kernel on
every GPU above; at 256K columns and K 2048 on B200, 49.0 us (SGLang) vs 12.2 us (walk-first).
The existing `gvr_2` backend, measured on the same trace and GPU in the study that motivated
this work, sits at 4.41 us unpaged where `walkfirst_primitives` now takes 3.21 us; that
comparison comes from two sessions, the SGLang columns above from one job each.

End to end in SGLang with the fused decode call taken over and prefill left on SGLang's kernel
(dummy weights, fp8, CUDA graphs): DeepSeek-V4-Flash on one B200, 96 prompts of 1K to 16K
tokens at 16 concurrent, 183.7 / 184.6 output tok/s for walk-first vs 183.6 / 182.1 for
sgl-kernel (median inter-token latency 10.67 vs 10.63 ms); DeepSeek-V3.2 on 8x B200 TP8 (61
indexer layers, K 2048, full-width rows), 80.8 / 81.9 vs 79.7 / 82.5 output tok/s and a decode
step at bs 16 x 32K context of 9.85 vs 10.17 ms. Parity within run-to-run noise with no
regression: the top-k is 1 to 3 percent of a decode step on these models, so the operator-level
wins cannot become a step-time win there.

## 🔍 Related Issues

- #4811 (the `gvr_2` backend this work started from) and #5311 (page-table fusion for `gvr_2`):
  the paged contract here is the same `slot = page_table[q, c // page_size] * page_size + c %
  page_size` mapping, so the two can share tests.

## 🚀 Pull Request Checklist

Thank you for contributing to FlashInfer! Before we review your pull request, please make sure the following items are complete.

### ✅ Pre-commit Checks

- [x] I have installed `pre-commit` by running `pip install pre-commit` (or used your preferred method).
- [x] I have installed the hooks with `pre-commit install`.
- [x] I have run the hooks manually with `pre-commit run --all-files` and fixed any reported issues.

> If you are unsure about how to set up `pre-commit`, see [the pre-commit documentation](https://pre-commit.com/).

## 🧪 Tests

- [x] Tests have been added or updated as needed.
- [x] All tests are passing (`unittest`, etc.).

`tests/topk_varlen/` (801 tests) passes on every architecture: B200 766 passed / 34 skipped /
1 xfailed, Rubin 767 / 33 / 1, RTX 5080 497 / 304, H100 486 / 315, L40S 486 / 315, A100 486 /
315 (the skips are the Blackwell-only `radix`, `gvr`, `gvr_2` and `radix_filter` tests); the
radix_primitives and walk-first suites gate on each backend's own support predicate, so the
Ampere (warp-aggregated collect, register tie fold) and Hopper (no-PDL) variants run there too.
The adversarial exactness sweeps (tie plateaus, one-bin floods, signed zeros, NaN payloads of
either sign, inf floods, rows of every arm) report zero failures on all six.
Value checks compare sorted value multisets, never index sets, so ties cannot make them flaky.
Coverage includes the grouped-row ABI at non-divisible `next_n` x `compress_ratio` boundaries
for every backend that serves it, NaN payloads of either sign per arm, inf floods, tie plateaus
and one-bin floods, top_k above the row width, empty batches, fp16/bf16 on every walk-first arm,
CUDA-graph replay across arm boundaries in both directions, the paged contract (tables wider and
narrower than the width, rows past the coverage, alignment and int32 bounds), one launch per
call, and the input-validation contract. `tests/trace/` passes (1542 passed, 254 skipped).

## 🔬 Experimental Track

<!-- Only for PRs submitted under the experimental policy (CONTRIBUTING.md → "Experimental APIs and Backends").
     Leave this section untouched for normal PRs. -->

- [ ] This PR is **experimental**: it adds or changes code under `flashinfer/experimental/` and/or an `@flashinfer_experimental_api`. Tracking issue: #
  - [ ] The tracking issue names an owner, the reason for the experimental path, and a graduation plan with a target release.
  - [ ] Core changes are limited to a thin entry point (signature, shared validation, feature-gate check, backend selection, handoff).
  - [ ] Tests live in `tests/experimental/` and were validated on the intended hardware; a runnable example is included.
  - [ ] Nothing is registered in `flashinfer/aot.py`, and no experimental backend is reachable from `backend="auto"` without `FLASHINFER_ALLOW_EXPERIMENTAL_AUTO_BACKENDS=1`. (Calling an `@flashinfer_experimental_api` or naming a backend explicitly is itself the opt-in and needs no environment variable.)
  - [ ] **Test scope declared below.** The experimental CI lane runs exactly these targets, so keep them as narrow as the change allows.

<!-- Required for experimental PRs. Replace the commented lines below with your targets.
     Do not delete the fence or change its `experimental-tests` tag — the experimental-track
     watcher reads it verbatim to decide which targets to ask CI for. -->

```experimental-tests
# One target per line: a directory or a file. (A pytest ::selector is not
# supported -- the sharding runner cannot consume one.) Must be under
# tests/experimental/ and must exist. Delete these comment lines and add yours, e.g.
#
#   tests/experimental/test_my_backend.py
#   tests/experimental/my_backend/
#
# Declaring the whole tree (tests/experimental/) is allowed but means every
# experimental PR pays for every other feature's tests, in every matrix cell.
```

## Reviewer Notes

Where to start: `flashinfer/topk_varlen/topk_varlen.py` (the checkers, the shared validation,
the paged contract and the `_run_*` dispatchers), then `tests/topk_varlen/test_topk_varlen_paged.py`
for the paged contract, then the kernels in the order of the commits. All four backends are
durable (not experimental): public backend values, two of them auto-routed for paged calls,
all JIT-only (CuTe-DSL kernels and a single-architecture nvcc module are not AOT-compiled, so
`flashinfer/aot.py` is untouched).

Known limitations and intentional deviations:

- **Tie floods are exact, and that costs time where SGLang truncates.** On a 16K-column row
  whose rank-k bin holds thousands of distinct values, SGLang's kernel returns an approximate
  set in 7 to 9 us; walk-first stays exact at 13.6 us on B200 (18 to 27 us on A100). ReLU'd
  indexer logits tie at exact zeros, which the uniform-tie shortcut handles at full speed.
- **Rows just above the 16K short-row cap** take the multi-CTA pipeline, whose fixed floor
  leaves them at 0.83x to 0.94x of SGLang's kernel standalone (the one negative cell in the
  DeepSeek-V3.2 end-to-end run, bs 16 at 16K context, 9.81 vs 9.62 ms per step).
- **Ampere/Ada compile a register fold of the tie key range** (cc 8.x serialise same-address
  shared-memory reductions): plateaus 2.2x to 3.4x faster and ReLU rows 21 to 25 percent faster
  there, Gaussian rows about 5 percent (0.1 to 0.2 us) slower. SM90+ compile the direct form.
- **`radix_primitives` waits for the producer before its first global read** (PDL on SM90+;
  the lengths and the page table may come from the preceding kernel, so the earlier metadata
  prefetch was a race). Same-node A/B against the pre-review kernel (B200, two alternating
  rounds, `cutlass_primitives` as the unchanged control column): ReLU paged rows 3.69 to
  3.83 us, 2048-column rows 3.85 to 4.05 us, 16K rows 6.10 to 6.30 us; Gaussian paged rows,
  full rows and every A100 cell unchanged. Walk-first already waited first and is unchanged.
- **Prefill is not taken over.** The kernels are 1.0x to 1.9x faster than SGLang's at prefill
  shapes, but the API specialises a kernel per logits width and prefill chunks present many
  widths; an engine must pad to a fixed width before using these backends there.
- **NaN order.** fp32 ranks every NaN top like `torch.topk` in all three primitives kernels. For
  fp16/bf16 the short-row arms and `radix_primitives` bin the integer key, so a sign-set NaN
  pattern ranks bottom there (top in walk-first's long-row pipeline); documented in the kernel
  docstrings, and real logits do not carry negative NaNs.
- **`sglang` keeps upstream's PDL prefetch**: on SM90+ it reads `seq_lens` and the page-table
  row before its grid-dependency wait, so under programmatic dependent launch the kernel
  immediately preceding the call must not write them (the backend docstring states this; the
  primitives kernels wait before their first global read). It is kept as the kernel SGLang
  runs so the parity and API-overhead checks (API 3.32 us vs raw kernel 3.35 us on the decode
  trace) stay reproducible.
- **`approx_ties`** is honoured by `radix_primitives` only (the docstring says so); `sglang` is
  approximate regardless; exact backends ignore it.
- **`workspace["cutlass_primitives_row_order"]`** hands the caller a CTA-scheduling decision
  (longest rows first pairs long rows against short ones: up to 17 percent on skewed batches).
  An in-call ranking launch measured 1.3 us and loses on uniform batches, so the backend never
  computes it itself; the key is validated (shape, dtype, device) but its contents are trusted.
  Happy to drop the key if the maintainers prefer the API without a scheduling knob.
- **Vendored code:** `flashinfer/topk_varlen/cutlass_primitives/` is an unmodified vendoring
  (edit upstream and re-vendor; comment style and `docs/` references follow the upstream
  library). Three upstream-side items found in review are left for the library: the cluster
  verdict's re-published words have no cluster barrier between a peer's first-round reads and
  the second round (unreachable in practice: the window is a whole filter pass), `_scaled_rank`
  can overflow int32 above a 131072-element aim on 99 KB parts (exact result, perf cliff), and
  `max_active_clusters` falls back silently when the occupancy probe fails.
  `csrc/sglang_dsv4/sgl_kernel/` is verbatim upstream sglang and excluded from the formatting
  hooks so it stays diffable; its launcher documents that the raw ragged entry does not clamp
  lengths to the row width (the `top_k_varlen` entry does, on device).
- **Auto routing:** the primitives backends are outside the unpaged `auto` ranking and are
  selected by `auto` only when a page table is given, where the two exact ones are the only
  candidates.

dimension reviewers each followed by an adversarial verifier (about eighty confirmed findings
from crash risks to nits; every bug and test gap was fixed before opening, the remaining items
are the deviations listed above). One more nit left as is: walk-first's cluster retry
re-publishes two shared words without a cluster barrier between the peers' first-round DSMEM
reads and the overwrite; the reads are issued at the barrier and the overwrite follows a full
re-walk, so the window is not reachable on hardware. The fixes cover the vendored sglang module
building for exactly one architecture per device capability (its headers static-assert the
target against the global gencode list), the paged `sglang` path clamping to a narrow table as
the API promises, device and alignment checks in its launcher, checkers that encode every
kernel constraint so `auto` falls back instead of failing inside a kernel, the `radix_primitives`
arms for top_k above the 2048-entry tie stage, a PDL wait before the first global read, int32
bounds on the paged coverage, walk-first's degenerate-scale key bounds, a 64-bit flood-refine
edge, a per-row status word with real path information, inf-robust sampling, device-aware
compile keys, a capture-safe cluster-capacity probe, the shared validation of `seq_lens`'
device, `top_k` and `compress_ratio`, and license and provenance files for both vendored trees.

title: feat(qsa_ops): add Qwen4Exp quantized sparse attention
body:
<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

Qwen4Exp's quantized sparse attention (QSA) for SM80 and newer, as `flashinfer.qsa_ops`, with the two pieces of common code it needs.

A QSA layer scores a compressed index cache, keeps the top blocks per query, and attends over those tokens where they sit in the paged KV cache. The package has the per-step kernels (pre-indexer, paged scorer, route expansion and mapping, output gate) and three objects that run them out of caller-owned workspaces, so a captured CUDA graph can replay a whole step: `QSASelection`, `QSAAttention` and `QSA`. `qsa_capabilities()` tells a serving stack what the build carries.

Two changes to existing code support it:

- `BlockSparseAttentionWrapper` runs on a paged KV cache (`plan(..., kv_cache_page_size=...)`; dense, FP8 or NVFP4; NHD or HND) and reports its workspace size before planning, so several live plans can share one arena. It also fixes the default FP8 scales, which were sized by the block width instead of the KV-head count.
- `top_k_ragged_transform` takes `out`, `workspace` and a resolved `backend`, so a caller can run it without allocating and with the backend fixed up front. Calls without them are unchanged.

The kernels run on SM80 and every later architecture: the JIT and AOT builds target 8.x through 12.x, and there are no architecture-specific paths, so newer GPUs run the same mma.sync and cp.async code rather than tuned variants. SM7x is excluded because the scorer's m16n8k16 arrived with SM80. The pre-indexer, scorer and route are one JIT module; the gate is a second one built without fast math, so a subnormal logistic is not flushed to zero. `cp_async.cuh` gains one L1-caching copy and `mma.cuh` the m16n8k16 helpers; existing functions are untouched.

#5859, #5860 and #5861 were folded into this PR and closed.

## 🔍 Related Issues

Tracked in #5669.

## 🚀 Pull Request Checklist

Thank you for contributing to FlashInfer! Before we review your pull request, please make sure the following items are complete.

### ✅ Pre-commit Checks

- [x] I have installed the hooks with `pre-commit install`.
- [x] I have run the hooks manually with `pre-commit run --all-files` and fixed any reported issues.

> If you are unsure about how to set up `pre-commit`, see [the pre-commit documentation](https://pre-commit.com/).

## 🧪 Tests

- [x] Tests have been added or updated as needed.
- [ ] All tests are passing (`unittest`, etc.).

Each kernel is checked against a torch reference; the selection, the attention and a whole step against torch, including workspace lifetimes, plan freezing and CUDA-graph replay. The paged block-sparse route is checked against dense attention over the same entries for bf16, FP8 and NVFP4 caches, and the top-k caller-buffer path against the per-call transform. On sm_80 everything in `tests/qsa_ops`, `tests/attention/test_block_sparse.py`, `tests/utils/test_topk.py` and the trace tests passes; the SM90-only FP8 default-scale test skips. Nothing has run on SM90 or newer.

## 🔬 Experimental Track

<!-- Only for PRs submitted under the experimental policy (CONTRIBUTING.md → "Experimental APIs and Backends").
     Leave this section untouched for normal PRs. -->

- [ ] This PR is **experimental**: it adds or changes code under `flashinfer/experimental/` and/or an `@flashinfer_experimental_api`. Tracking issue: #
  - [ ] The tracking issue names an owner, the reason for the experimental path, and a graduation plan with a target release.
  - [ ] Core changes are limited to a thin entry point (signature, shared validation, feature-gate check, backend selection, handoff).
  - [ ] Tests live in `tests/experimental/` and were validated on the intended hardware; a runnable example is included.
  - [ ] Nothing is registered in `flashinfer/aot.py`, and no experimental backend is reachable from `backend="auto"` without `FLASHINFER_ALLOW_EXPERIMENTAL_AUTO_BACKENDS=1`. (Calling an `@flashinfer_experimental_api` or naming a backend explicitly is itself the opt-in and needs no environment variable.)
  - [ ] **Test scope declared below.** The experimental CI lane runs exactly these targets, so keep them as narrow as the change allows.

## Reviewer Notes

The only changes to shared paths are `paged_kv_t`, which gains a `storage_page_size` field and a `resolve_slot` step on every paged kernel's address computation (a uniform branch that is a no-op when the logical block is the page), and the three keyword arguments on `top_k_ragged_transform`. Everything else is new code under `flashinfer/qsa_ops`, `include/flashinfer/attention/qsa` and `csrc/qsa_*`. The paged route is served by the FA2 kernel on every architecture; FA3 and trtllm-gen do not take a paged route here, so on SM90 and newer QSA attention runs FA2. Nothing has run on SM90 or newer.

The combine wire (expert rank -> token owner) is selected by
`combine_wire` on the config (`None` reads
`FLASHINFER_SM90_CAKE_BF16_COMBINE_WIRE`, default `prereduced`) and must be
the same on every EP rank (checked with an allgather at init; a mixed pipe
raises on every rank). `prereduced`: the expert rank pre-reduces all routes
of a token that landed on it in fp32 (`fmaf` in ascending route order), rounds
once to bf16 and sends ONE row per (token, source rank) into the owner's
top-k inbox (slot = the group's smallest route index); the owner sums the
<= ep_size rows in ascending source-rank order in fp32 and rounds once.
`prereduced_hilo`: as `prereduced`, but a source rank holding >= 2 routes of a
token sends its fp32 partial as two bf16 rows (hi, and the residual `p - hi`
in the slot of its second-smallest route index) so no group partial is rounded
to bf16; single-route groups are `bf16(w * y)` exactly as the per-route wire.
`per_route`: one `bf16(fp32(y_k) * w_k)` row per route, summed over k by the
owner (the original wire, kept for A/B comparison; the only wire that also
runs the vendored three-kernel tail). Both wires are deterministic (fixed
reduction order, no floating-point atomics; repeated calls and CUDA-graph
replay are bitwise identical) but not bitwise identical to each other: the
pre-reduced wire rounds each element twice instead of top_k + 1 times. The
section tests run every routing pattern under both wires, including the
pre-reduce-specific cases (all K routes of a token on one remote rank, all on
the local rank) and the wire-mismatch rejection.

dfc9193
…ers for the SM90 MegaMoE backend

Round 2 of the Hopper native BF16 MegaMoE backend
(`sm90_bf16_bf16_bf16_push_cake`,
flashinfer-ai#5958
). Part of
flashinfer-ai#4254
, follow-up to
flashinfer-ai#5708
.

Combine wire (the only numerics change; deterministic):
- `combine_wire="prereduced"`: each expert rank pre-reduces, in fp32 and in
  ascending route order, the routes of a token that it computed, rounds once
  to bf16 and publishes one row per (token, source rank); the owning rank sums
  the per-rank rows in ascending rank order in fp32 and rounds once. Inbox
  reads drop from T*top_k rows to T*world rows.
- `combine_wire="prereduced_hilo"`: the pre-reduced row plus a bf16 residual
  row for multi-route groups (precision-conservative variant).
- `combine_wire="per_route"`: the round-1 wire (one row per route), unchanged.
- Default (`combine_wire=None`, env unset): `per_route` when the per-rank
  token capacity is <= 8, `prereduced` above. `FLASHINFER_SM90_CAKE_BF16_COMBINE_WIRE`
  overrides; all ranks must agree (verified at construction).
- Fixed accumulation order (routes ascending within a rank, ranks ascending
  across ranks), no fp32 atomics on outputs or partial sums; bitwise
  run-to-run and eager == CUDA graph.

Protocol fixed-cost levers (output bit-identical to round 1): publish scratch
self-resets instead of per-round memsets, the pre-reduced worklist is built
inside the compact pass, grid completion counts participating blocks only,
compact assigns rows by static grid stride, publish groups are split across
blocks at decode sizes.

Grouped-GEMM epilogue (sealed sources re-rendered; output bit-identical):
bf16x2 pack, quad transpose and 16-byte stores.

Measured on one 8xH100 node (CUDA graph, CUPTI, paired same-process A/B
against the round-1 backend, 35 benchmark rows, two independent sessions):
geomean 1.031, 33/35 rows improved (best EP4 T=4096: 1.12); against the split
nccl_ep + CUTLASS BF16 baseline geomean 1.55. Precision against an independent
fp32 reference: aggregate mean-abs and rel-L2 below round 1 on every column;
the atol=rtol=1e-2 test gate is unchanged.

Tests: frozen-sources seal, EP1 (all wires, per-shape default, duplicate-rank
and all-local routing, wire mismatch), EP2/EP4/EP8 torchrun;
`run_tests.sh sm90_bf16_push_cake`. Docs: architecture and runbook updated
(wire semantics, determinism note, benchmark `--combine-wire` flag).

body:
<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

Reduce preparation and final-combine overhead in the SM90 MXFP4 MegaMoE path:

- Fuse BF16 cast/abs/per-token amax into a separate safe input-staging kernel. Shared `@cute.jit` helpers preserve the existing finite-input quantization arithmetic and scale wire. The FP32 quantizer signature stays unchanged; unsupported input layouts/dtypes retain the existing path.
- Limit the separate final reducer to live output rows. Previously, a small batch still launched the reducer across the entire preallocated capacity. Dispatch, peer expert work and symmetric workspace allocation retain full capacity; empty local ranks and in-kernel reduction retain their existing path.
- Include output shape/stride in the launch-cache key and extend the existing numerical regression for shrink/grow reuse, poisoned tails and graph replay.

No change to weight representation, precision, expert routing, GEMM tactics or collective work.

**Dependency:** stacked on the tested historical #6738 commit `bfd3072c362822c58098ddb104d6e22ebba001d3`. #6738 has since merged newer main into its branch; this PR has not rebased onto that newer head or claimed to test it. Its main-based diff temporarily includes the dependency. Review the [five-file incremental diff](https://github.com/xijiaat/flashinfer/compare/bfd3072c362822c58098ddb104d6e22ebba001d3...9a913c189fc523834f2b8d7145dd76a249493aa6); the new live-row change is [one two-file commit](https://github.com/xijiaat/flashinfer/commit/9a913c189fc523834f2b8d7145dd76a249493aa6). No commits were added to #6738 by this update.

**Evidence:** [raw samples, complete tables, NCU CSVs, test logs and reproduction scripts](https://github.com/xijiaat/flashinfer/tree/e3c1f0b2418f81fc846ce6e21431ac672a81f84d/live-finalize), on a separate evidence branch in the author's fork. Benchmark artifacts are kept out of the upstream code diff.

### Complete-MoE layer measurements

Four H20-3e (SM90), EP4, H=5120/I=2304/E=384/top-k=6, capacity=4128; synthetic weights/routes with real model dimensions. PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, CUDA 13.0, CuTe DSL 4.7.1, NVSHMEM 3.8.0 / nvshmem4py 0.4.1.

**The following table measures only the additional live-row reducer change against `3eb1befcf7e5ca3175c398fdf3a4569693a26bfd`; both arms already have fused BF16 staging.** Timing includes safe quantization/staging, EP dispatch, FC1, SwiGLU, A2 quantization, FC2 and combine.

| Tokens/rank | Routing | Baseline (us) | Candidate (us) | Speedup | Three rounds (%) |
|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 1 | uniform | 225.914 | 193.562 | +16.714% | +16.715/+16.701/+16.763 |
| 4 | uniform | 511.997 | 479.613 | +6.752% | +6.706/+6.747/+6.796 |
| 16 | uniform | 1200.579 | 1168.646 | +2.732% | +2.726/+2.729/+2.763 |
| 128 | uniform | 1739.770 | 1711.440 | +1.655% | +1.680/+1.557/+1.666 |
| 1024 | uniform | 2666.045 | 2644.531 | +0.814% | +0.809/+0.817/+0.812 |
| 4096 | uniform | 7767.597 | 7769.370 | -0.023% | -0.063/-0.035/+0.022 |
| 16 | skew | 203.130 | 171.414 | +18.502% | +18.479/+18.559/+18.517 |
| 4 | empty-rank | 438.803 | 432.832 | +1.380% | +1.330/+1.305/+1.314 |
| 13 | ragged | 1183.232 | 1150.944 | +2.805% | +2.783/+2.840/+2.803 |


Each case has three rounds of 20 alternating AB/BA pairs, five complete forwards per captured graph, identical input/weights/workspace/tactic, and the maximum latency across four ranks. An unmeasured NCCL start gate aligns ranks. Compilation, warmup and NCU are separate. These rounds share a process and are not independent deployments. Table latencies pool all 60 samples/arm; speedup = before/after - 1.

This is the normal cache/heuristic tactic path: MMA `(256,64,256)`, cluster `(2,1,1)`, `atomic_counter`, `epi_warps`, one dispatch warp, BF16 combine. It is not a best-autotuned-tactic claim. The secondary fixed K128 qualification run and all raw A/A data are also published. Largest absolute A/A round-median delta: **0.096%**.

Ragged counts are 13/14/15/16; empty-rank has zero local rows on rank 0 and four on the others. **M4096 is unchanged within noise.** The gain depends on capacity exceeding live batch size and is strongest for small decode-like batches. Both arms retain the same 42,270,720-byte output buffer and equal post-warmup allocation/reservation. No extra weight copies.

**Prior BF16-staging results use a different baseline and cohort:** compared with #6738 `bfd3072...`, staging alone reduced four launches to one; the V4.1-sized uniform complete-MoE cases improved 1.16–3.45% with a fixed K128 qualification tactic. [All 24 configurations, A/A controls and original evidence](https://github.com/xijiaat/flashinfer/tree/3cd9fdef163bb5e9ee5a6d6bbc0d0358ced95125) remain available. Those gains are **not added to or multiplied by** the incremental table above. Neither cohort measures full-model serving throughput or model quality.

### NCU evidence

Reducer at M16/H5120/K6/capacity4128: **20,640 -> 80 CTAs**, while unprofiled reducer latency is approximately **28.65 -> 1.48 us**. The code eliminates 42,106,880 logical bytes of padded output stores.

| NCU metric | Full-capacity reducer | Live-row reducer |
|---|---:|---:|
| DRAM read (MB) | 1.130496 | 0.927744 |
| DRAM write (MB) | 14.490624 | 0 |
| Profiled duration (us) | 29.760 | 3.456 |

Nine replay passes with `--clock-control none --cache-control none`. The zero observed DRAM write does **not** mean no output writes: valid output can remain in L2. Observed traffic is cache-dependent; profiler durations are not used as benchmark results.

The earlier staging-only profile at M16384/H7168 reduced total DRAM traffic **2649.336 -> 343.102 MB (-87.05%)** and removed **939,589,632 bytes** of incremental eager FP32 temporary allocation. Its raw counters and smaller-M controls remain in the prior evidence.

title: feat(cake_msa): Cake Hopper (SM90) programs behind the four MSA operations
body:
The MiniMax sparse attention (MSA) kernel family on Hopper has four operations. Sparse decode uses bf16 q and fp8 e4m3 KV pages and covers every admitted coordinate. Sparse prefill uses bf16 q, supports GQA groups 4 / 8 / 16 and handles up to 4096 pages per sequence. Proxy score has two regimes. The decode regime takes fp8 and bf16 q, a one-head index cache, Hq in {1,2,4} and max_seqlen_q <= 4. The prefill regime takes fp8 q with both accumulation precisions. Top-k block select has one form per planner coordinate: columns per CTA, tile groups, index bits and mask form. One route table serves 89 generated programs: 22 sparse-decode, 6 sparse-prefill (3 prefill_v1 + 3 prefill_v2), 24 proxy-decode, 5 proxy-prefill and 32 top-k.

This PR delivers the Hopper (sm_90a) variant of the Cake MSA family. That covers all four operations and all 89 programs, compiled with FlashInfer's sm_90a flags. No earlier Cake version of this family ships on sm_90a. So in every row the baseline (`fi_sm90`) is FlashInfer's existing SM90 CuTe DSL kernel for the same operation and shape, measured in the same session on the same GPU. Speedup = fi_sm90 latency / Cake latency, so a value > 1.000 means Cake is faster. All rows were measured on an NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3 (compute capability 9.0, sm_90a, 132 SMs) with CUDA 13.3 and torch 2.13.0a0+9186a08b2c.nv26.07.

*NVIDIA H100 80GB HBM3 (compute capability 9.0, sm_90a, 132 SMs), CUDA 13.3, torch 2.13.0a0+9186a08b2c.nv26.07; same-session interleaved CUPTI medians (cold L2, 3 reps) of the Cake kernel and the fi_sm90 CuTe DSL kernel of the same shape; speedup = fi_sm90 / Cake (> 1.000 = Cake faster); correctness-only shapes carry no timing.*

title: [RFC]: SM90 Exact Fused DSA Prefill Indexer
body: ### Motivation. We propose an optional SM90 backend for vLLM's `SparseAttnIndexer` prefill path. It computes FP8 scores and exact TopK in one CUDA kernel without materializing the full score tensor or intermediate candidates in HBM. The first implementation PR targets only the H64, D=128, topk=2048, single-GPU FP8 prefill path used by DeepSeek V3.2. The existing path remains the default. H32 support will follow in a separate PR. The current vLLM prefill indexer follows this high-level flow: ```text gather K -> fp8_fp4_mqa_logits -> materialize logits -> top_k_per_row_prefill ``` At long context lengths, writing and reading the full logits tensor and the extra kernel boundary become significant. In our current H20 matrix, the `H=1M, B=32, Q=512` case has a 508.25 MiB peak score chunk and materializes 64.03 GiB of scores over one indexer call, while the final TopK index output is 128 MiB. The goal is to replace only the score + TopK stage and eliminate full-score HBM materialization without changing downstream Sparse MLA attention. ### Proposed Change. #### Scope and integration The new backend plugs into the existing `sparse_attn_indexer()` prefill branch: ```text existing Q quantization, KV-cache insert, and chunk metadata | v cp_gather_indexer_k_quant_cache | v SM90 fused score + exact TopK | v existing topk_indices_buffer ``` The first PR is intentionally limited to: - SM90a, validated separately on H20, H800, and H100; - the DeepSeek V3.2 FP8 prefill path; - H64, D=128, and topk=2048; - single-GPU execution without DCP or PCP; - INT32 output shaped `[M, 2048]`, with unspecified order. Decode, KV-cache layout, K gather, and Sparse MLA attention remain unchanged. The proposed configuration is: ```python attention_config.indexer_prefill_backend = "default" | "sm90_exact" ``` `default` preserves the existing vLLM implementation. `sm90_exact` explicitly enables the experimental backend. Selecting `sm90_exact` reports a clear initialization error when GPU, dtype, H/D/topk, DCP/PCP, or shared-memory requirements are not met. Rows shorter than topk use the existing short-sequence path and `-1` sentinel rule. A row exactly equal to topk returns all valid indices without reading Q/K. DCP is excluded because the current DCP merge consumes both local TopK scores and indices, while this kernel outputs indices only. #### Kernel design The current H64 kernel uses a one-query-per-CTA pipeline: ```text TMA K/K-scale double buffer -> 4 WGMMA math warp groups (256 keys/round) -> generation-tagged shared-memory score ring -> FP32 ordered-bit histogram/radix cutoff -> running Top-2048 and final indices ``` The main implementation parameters are: - 768 threads per CTA; - four WGMMA math warp groups; - two TMA stages; - 12,544 scores per selection group and two ring slots; - 704 threads participating in the final drain; - 80 registers per thread; - 232,448 bytes of dynamic shared memory and 1,024 bytes of static shared memory; - zero stack and local-memory usage in the production cubin. Shared-memory usage gives one CTA per SM on H20. H20, H800, and H100 share one SM90a source, while eligibility and performance are validated separately on each device instead of maintaining SKU-specific implementations. The prototype uses runtime NVCC for iteration speed. The upstream version will retain only the selected production variant and use vLLM's static CUDA build, with no first-request JIT compilation. #### Exactness contract `exact` means that the selector computes an exact cutoff for the FP32 scores produced by the fused kernel. For a valid interval, let `c` be its 2048th-largest score. A valid output must: - contain 2048 unique indices from the valid interval; - include every index with `score > c`; - include no index with `score < c`; - fill the remaining positions from indices with `score == c`. Output order and the specific choice among cutoff ties are unstable and are not part of the API contract. This matches unordered TopK set semantics. The score expression is arithmetically equivalent to the current FP8 indexer, but WGMMA and DeepGEMM may use different floating-point reduction orders. Validation must therefore separate selector exactness relative to the fused scores from numerical error and model outputs relative to the latest vLLM backend. This RFC does not claim bitwise equivalence between those score producers. #### Related work - **Current vLLM:** materializes full logits in HBM before TopK and serves as the current baseline. - **[#52696](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52696):** materializes FP16 logits and uses native FP16 TopK, reducing the size of the logits tensor without removing its HBM round trip. - **[#48726](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/48726) and the [LiteTopK paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.11976):** target SM100 with tcgen05 and online candidate filtering, and also include LiteDSA attention work. - **This proposal:** targets SM90 with TMA/WGMMA, keeps scores on chip, performs exact cutoff selection, and changes only the prefill indexer. This proposal has a different architecture, selector, and submission scope from #48726, so it should be reviewed as an independent backend rather than appended to that PR. #### Preliminary results The following preliminary operator-level results use one NVIDIA H20 with synthetic FP8 inputs and fixed H64, D=128, and topk=2048. The benchmark matrix contains 665 shapes: - history KV lengths: 4K, 6K, 8K, 12K, 16K, 24K, 32K, 48K, 64K, 96K, 128K, 192K, 256K, 384K, 512K, 640K, 768K, 896K, and 1M; - batch sizes: 1, 4, 16, 32, and 128; - query lengths: 8, 64, 512, 1024, 2048, 4096, and 8192. The vLLM baseline is vLLM 0.27.1's `fp8_fp4_mqa_logits` with FP32 scores, followed by `top_k_per_row_prefill`. Both paths use the same shapes and mathematical boundaries, but were measured in independent runs. The following speedups are preliminary operator-level comparisons, not paired regression results. Current results: - 1.3918981x geometric-mean speedup over vLLM 0.27.1 FP32 DeepGEMM + TopK across all 665 shapes; - faster than vLLM in 604 of 665 shapes; - 58 of 58 current correctness cases passed; - zero sampled DeepGEMM cutoff deficit. The figure shows four representative shapes covering `B=1/32`, `Q=512/8192`, and 4K--1M history. The 1.3918981x value is calculated from the complete 665-shape matrix, not inferred from these four curves. These results only justify upstream evaluation. The baseline is still vLLM 0.27.1's FP32 synthetic operator path, and the vLLM and fused-kernel results come from independent runs. Latest-main, H800/H100, real-model, CUDA Graph, and end-to-end TTFT validation are still pending. #### Compatibility and scope PR 1 excludes decode, H32, DCP/PCP, FP4/MXFP4, LiteDSA attention, and experimental selector variants. It does not change the default backend or introduce a new KV-cache format. H32 changes the Q layout, WGMMA epilogue, shared-memory budget, and thread-role balance. It will be submitted separately for GLM-5.1/5.2 after the interface and validation method are established. #### Test plan Before requesting implementation review, the PR will provide: - a cutoff oracle built from a test-only fused-score output, requiring 100% TopK set equality for unique scores and the contract above for ties; - random and real-model inputs, all-equal and cutoff-dense scores, extreme gates, ragged and unaligned rows, `0/K`, and multiple ring generations; - custom-op schema, FakeTensor, output mutation, CUDA Graph, multiple streams, dispatcher error/bypass, and compute-sanitizer coverage; - paired H20, H800, and H100 comparisons against latest main's default path, a forced FP32 path, and #52696 if still relevant; - separate reporting for score+TopK latency, full indexer latency, peak HBM, and end-to-end TTFT; - real DeepSeek V3.2 prefill, MRCR/NIAH, and standard accuracy tasks. We propose an implementation evidence floor of at least 1.10x indexer-stage geometric-mean speedup over the target validation matrix and at least 3% TTFT improvement in two long-context configurations. #### Implementation plan 1. **PR 1: H64 / DeepSeek V3.2.** Production H64 kernel, static CUDA build, custom op, prefill dispatcher, tests, and benchmarks only. 2. **PR 2: H32 / GLM-5.1/5.2.** Reuse the reviewed interface and test contract, with separate tuning and validation. Before submission, we will remove experimental selector branches, retain one production implementation, and add SPDX headers, MIT provenance, source commits, and a human-review record. #### Core request for comments We would like maintainer feedback on one decision: **would vLLM accept the H64 SM90 fused prefill indexer first as an opt-in experimental backend, with H32 in a separate PR after the interface and validation method are established?** ### Feedback Period. one week. ### CC List. _No response_ ### Any Other Things. AI assistance was used for investigation, implementation experiments, and RFC drafting. The human submitter will review the RFC, code, and test results before requesting maintainer review. ### Before submitting a new issue... - [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

title: [Kernel][Build] Bump DeepGEMM to the 26/09/30 release and adapt the sparse indexer
body:
## Overview

Bump the vendored DeepGEMM pin to the tip of `vllm-project/DeepGEMM` `dev` (`6ce1c5e`): upstream's 26/09/30 public release (vllm-project/DeepGEMM#30, deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM#462) plus vendoring import fixes (vllm-project/DeepGEMM#31, vllm-project/DeepGEMM#32) and a relaxed paged sparse MQA page-stride guard (vllm-project/DeepGEMM#33). Adapt vLLM to the breaking MQA-logits API.

## Claims

- vLLM builds, vendors and imports DeepGEMM 2.8.1.
- The DSA sparse indexer (DeepSeek-V3.2, GLM-5.x, GLM-5.3, DeepSeek-V4/V4.1, HY-V4) keeps working on SM90/SM100/SM120 with the new MQA-logits API.
- On SM100 the FP8 indexer cache stays numerically identical: same FP8 values and the same per-token power-of-two scale, now stored as four packed UE8M0 bytes (a valid MXFP8 encoding) because SM100 MQA kernels only take MX scales.

## Breaking changes in DeepGEMM `1e1842a` → `6ce1c5e`

| Change | vLLM impact | Handling |
|---|---|---|
| `deep_gemm/__init__.py` imports a new `deep_gemm/locality_domain.py` | not vendored → `import vllm.third_party.deep_gemm` fails | install it in `deepgemm.cmake` |
| `_C.py` registered the locality-domain shim as `deep_gemm._C.locality_domain` | relative import fails when vendored as `vllm.third_party.deep_gemm`, and vLLM then silently treats DeepGEMM as unavailable | fixed in vllm-project/DeepGEMM#31 (in the pin); `tools/check_wheel_deepgemm.py` now imports the package so CI catches this |
| The C++ MLOPart bridge imported `deep_gemm.utils.mlopart` and the epilogue module was named `deep_gemm.epilogue` | `localize()` (not called by vLLM) would fail when vendored | fixed in vllm-project/DeepGEMM#32 (in the pin): `_C.py` passes its `__package__` to the new `init(library_root_path, python_package_name)` |
| `fp8_fp4_paged_sparse_mqa_logits` page-stride guard lowered from 512 to 256 B (vllm-project/DeepGEMM#33) | DeepSeek-V4.1's sparse-logits block stride stays 512-aligned, which still satisfies it | none |
| `fp8_mqa_logits`, `fp8_paged_mqa_logits`, `fp8_gemm_nt_skip_head_mid`, `get_bf16_mega_gate_config` removed | unused by vLLM | none |
| `clean_logits` / `logits_dtype` removed from `fp8_fp4_(paged_)mqa_logits`; `max_seqlen_k` now required (> 0) | wrapper signatures | `vllm/utils/deep_gemm.py`; prefill chunk metadata carries a host `max_seqlen_k` bound (no device sync) |
| `fp8_fp4_mqa_logits` returns **compressed** logits `[M, max_seqlen_k]` (row `i` starts at K position `ks[i]`) on every arch | prefill top-k / candidate-block / DCP consumers indexed absolute columns | consumers run on row starts `0`, ends `ke - ks`; output indices are unchanged (already relative to `ks`) |
| SM100 MQA kernels take only MXFP8/MXFP4 with packed UE8M0 scales, **BF16 weights**, return **BF16 logits**; paged is varlen-only | FP8 indexer (fp32 per-token scale, scale folded into fp32 weights) rejected | see below |
| `bf16_mega_gate` default `scoring_func` → `'sqrtsoftplus'` | vLLM always passes it | none |
| FP8×FP4 / BF16 Mega MoE assert DeepGEMM's SM count equals the device's | only DBO + DeepEP-HT lowers it (`ubatch_utils.py`), not combined with Mega MoE today | none (noted) |
| Epilogue classes (`epilogue=` kwarg), locality domains, `shutdown` | additive | none |

### SM100 FP8 indexer

Every CUDA FP8 indexer writer already stores an exact power-of-two scale `2^ceil(log2(amax/448))` per 128-wide token. On SM100 (`mqa_logits_use_mx_scales()`) the writers store that scale's exponent as four equal UE8M0 bytes instead of the fp32, which is an exact MXFP8 encoding of the same values (same cache size, same FP8 bytes):

| Writer | Models |
|---|---|
| C++ `indexer_k_quant_and_cache` (`scale_fmt="mxfp8"`) | DeepSeek-V2-class `Indexer` (V3.2 via that class, DeepSeek MTP), HY-V4, DeepSeek-V3.2 under PCP |
| DeepSeek-V3.2 fused norm/RoPE (`_fused_norm_rope_kernel`) | DeepSeek-V3.2, GLM-5/5.2 (`GlmMoeDsa`), Dots3Note, V3.2 MTP |
| DeepSeek-V4 compressor (Triton; the CuTeDSL compressor is head-512 MLA only) | DeepSeek-V4 |
| DeepSeek-V4.1 `indexer_k_norm_rope_store` | DeepSeek-V4.1 |
| GLM-5.3 kpool prefill compress + decode update | GLM-5.3 |

Readers need no change: `cp_gather_indexer_k_quant_cache` (prefill, all of the above) and the DCP/PCP gathers copy the 4 scale bytes verbatim, and DeepGEMM reads the paged cache directly. The 512-wide MLA caches, MXFP4 caches, and the MiniMax-M3 / Qwen4 indexers are untouched.

FP8 Q keeps folding its per-(token, head) power-of-two scale into `weights`; `mqa_logits_mx_inputs` passes unit MX Q scales (exact, since `relu(s·x) = s·relu(x)` for `s > 0`) and casts weights to BF16. The BF16 logits are upcast to FP32 for the existing FP32-only top-k kernels (`as_fp32_logits`); routing BF16 logits straight to a BF16-capable top-k (DeepSelect / LiteTopK, #59921/#59922) is a follow-up.

SM90 and SM120 keep the FP8 format, FP32 weights and FP32 logits. Consequently the FP8 indexer cache's scale bytes now differ between SM100 and other architectures: moving that KV cache between SM100 and non-SM100 nodes (cross-generation PD disaggregation, shared KV offload) is not supported for these models. Same-architecture setups are unaffected.

## Validation

All on 4x GB200 (SM100), CUDA 13, torch 2.13; baseline = `main` with the old pin `1e1842a`, same build otherwise.

**GLM-5.3-Flash** (FP8, TP4 + EP, MTP=3, `--max-model-len 131072 --max-num-batched-tokens 131072 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --reasoning-parser glm47`, `reasoning_effort=low`), on the rebased branch vs `main` bfa7e5b7af. MRCR prompts are far longer than the indexer's coverage (2048 pools × 4 = 8K tokens), so they exercise top-k selection; long prefills also engage the TP prefill row sharding from #54951 (confirmed with a temporary log, e.g. 129K-row steps split `[47458, 18791, 42577, 19957]` across ranks):

| | `main` + `1e1842a` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| MRCR, 60 samples of 16K–32K tokens (`tests/evals/mrcr`), match ratio (2 / 4 / 8 needles) | 0.794 (0.823 / 0.798 / 0.760) | 0.810 (0.904 / 0.791 / 0.735) |
| MRCR, 24 samples of 57K–66K tokens, match ratio | 0.578 (4 runs hit max_tokens) | 0.665 |
| GSM8K (1319, 5-shot) | 90.8% | 91.6% |
| Serving, 4 runs of 128 × (4096 in / 512 out) at concurrency 32, output tok/s | 1492 / 1544 / 1491 / 1471 | 1484 / 1476 / 1337 / 1501 |
| Median ITL | 19.85 ms | 19.9 ms |

GLM-5.3 serving throughput tracks the MTP acceptance length, which varies per run (the 1337 tok/s run had 1.31 vs ~1.7–1.8 elsewhere); runs with matching acceptance agree (1476 @ 1.70 vs 1471 @ 1.71).

**DeepSeek-V4-Flash** (before the rebase onto current `main`; baseline 26a488ad93), TP2 + EP, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8 --attention_config.indexer_kv_dtype=fp8`, `--max-model-len 8192`; GSM8K via `tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py` (1319 questions, 5-shot, 2 rounds). GSM8K prompts fit inside the indexer's coverage (512 × 4 = 2K tokens), so this checks the SM100 path end to end rather than top-k selection:

| indexer cache | `main` + `1e1842a` | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| fp8 | 95.5% / 94.6% | 94.8% / 94.6% |
| mxfp4 | 94.9% | 94.7% |

**Serving** — same server, `vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len 4096 --random-output-len 512 --num-prompts 256 --max-concurrency 64 --ignore-eos`, one warm-up + 3 runs each, sequential on the same GPUs:

| | output tok/s | mean TPOT | median ITL |
|---|---|---|---|
| `main` + `1e1842a` | 2968 (2962–2974) | 18.73 ms | 12.80 ms |
| this PR | 2946 (2928–2958) | 18.89 ms | 12.94 ms |

The ~0.8% gap matches the two extra small kernels per indexer layer on SM100 (weights → BF16, row-aware logits → FP32, ~3 µs together). Feeding BF16 straight from the Q producers and into a BF16 top-k removes both.

**Unit tests** (GB200):

```
pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_deepgemm_attention.py                      # 7 passed (SM100 MX + varlen paths)
pytest tests/model_executor/layers/test_mla_short_prefill_indexer.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_*.py tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_indexer_decode_seq_lens.py \
  tests/v1/attention/test_glm5next_indexer_block_sizes.py tests/v1/attention/test_kpool_*.py \
  tests/models/glm5next/test_sparse_indexer_topk_dispatch.py tests/v1/cudagraph/test_breakable_cudagraph.py \
  tests/kernels/test_compressor_kv_cache.py tests/kernels/test_fused_indexer_q_rope_quant.py \
  tests/kernels/test_kpool_decode_update_batched.py tests/v1/attention/test_rocm_paged_mxfp4_indexer_plan.py
                                                                               # 558 passed, 35 skipped
pytest tests/kernels/test_fused_deepseek_v32_norm_rope.py                      # 222 passed
pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_deepgemm.py tests/kernels/moe/test_batched_deepgemm.py \
  tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_mega_moe.py tests/kernels/mhc/test_mhc_kernels.py \
  tests/model_executor/test_deep_gemm_warmup.py                                 # all passed
pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_block_fp8.py tests/kernels/moe/test_block_fp8.py -k deep_gemm
                                                                               # 100 passed, 169 skipped
python tools/check_wheel_deepgemm.py                                           # now also imports the package
```

`tests/kernels/moe/test_silu_mul_fp8_quant_deep_gemm.py` fails on this GB200 with `unspecified launch failure` identically on `main` + `1e1842a` (pre-existing, unrelated). Not run (no hardware): SM90 and SM120; CI's H100 DeepGEMM job covers the SM90 attention tests. CI has no SM100 DeepGEMM job, so the MX path is validated only by the runs above.

**Pin delta `1448881` → `6ce1c5e`**: the end-to-end runs above used `1448881`. The two later commits change no kernel math (vllm-project/DeepGEMM#33 only lowers the host and device stride asserts, vllm-project/DeepGEMM#32 only module naming). Re-checked on `6ce1c5e` on GB200 (the GPUs were shared with another job, so no end-to-end rerun):

```
python tools/check_wheel_deepgemm.py                                           # imports; init takes the package name
pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_deepgemm_attention.py \
  tests/model_executor/layers/test_mla_short_prefill_indexer.py tests/model_executor/test_deep_gemm_warmup.py
                                                                               # 42 passed, 7 skipped (need pip deep_gemm)
pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_deepgemm.py tests/kernels/quantization/test_block_fp8.py -k "deep_gemm or deepgemm"
                                                                               # 125 passed, 28 skipped
# DeepGEMM's tests/test_attention.py::test_sparse_mqa_logits, paged cases only, on the vendored build:
# 60/60 passed with 64-token pages of 8448 B (MXFP8) / 4352 B (MXFP4), 256- but not 512-aligned
```

## Details

- `tools/build_deepgemm_C.py` now passes `--force` to `setup.py build_ext`. DeepGEMM's `setup.py` lists only `csrc/python_api.cpp`, so after a pin change that touched only headers (`config.hpp` in vllm-project/DeepGEMM#32) an incremental build silently kept the old extension and the import failed with `deep_gemm::init() expected at most 1 argument(s)`. CMake already reruns this step on DeepGEMM header changes and `python_api.cpp` is the only translation unit, so forcing adds no work.
- Why not duplicate: no open PR bumps DeepGEMM past `1e1842a` or adapts the indexer to the new MQA API (#59503 bumps to an older SM107 fix already contained in the current pin; #59482 is the Stable ABI migration).
- AI assistance (Claude Code) was used; the submitter reviewed every changed line and ran the tests below.
